title: Acts 26:5
text: I lived a Pharisee. See note on  Acts 7:58 ; also notes on  Matthew 3:7 .

title: Acts 26:6
text: The promise made of God to our fathers. That they would be blessed in Abraham's seed, the Messiah.  See  Genesis 22:18 .

title: Acts 26:7
text: Our twelve tribes. A patriotic Jew always loved to speak of his race as it was in the days of its greatest power.  He would instinctively refuse to think less of it because it had been divided into the two kingdoms of Israel and Judah, or because of the captivity of Babylon.  To an Israelite of the Dispersion, who lived outside of Palestine, Jerusalem was always the Holy City.  At home or abroad, no Jew could be free from his consciousness of an elect and divinely designated membership in the chosen people.

title: Acts 26:8
text: Why is it judged incredible, etc.  The question was suggested by 'this hope' in the preceding verse.  The hope cold only be realized by the advent of a spiritual Messiah whom God would raise from the dead in order that he might be the spiritual Savior of his people.

title: Acts 26:9
text: Contrary to the name, etc.  Contrary to the teaching and divine authority of Jesus of Nazareth.

title: Acts 26:10
text: I gave my vote against them. He consented, that is, gave his vote for the stoning of Stephen, the first Christian martyr ( Acts 8:1 ); but according to this verse he had also helped to put others to death for their faith in Jesus.

title: Acts 26:11
text: Foreign cities. Cities outside of Palestine.  Damascus was only one of the places he had visited in his persecuting zeal.  Paul evidently intended the listening Jews to know that, during the time of his hatred of Jesus, he was a sincere and relentless enemy of the sect to which he now belonged.  If honest then, could they refuse to believe at least that he was honest in his reasons for the great change that had since been wrought in him?

title: Acts 26:12
text:
:18
 
As I journeyed to Damascus, etc.  See notes on  Acts 9:2-4 Acts 9:15 Acts 9:18 Acts 9:20 Acts 9:22 .
 

 
Goad. A stick used for driving beasts, and pointed with metal.

title: Acts 26:23
text:
How that the Christ must suffer. See  Isaiah 53:1-12 Luke 24:26 Luke 24:46 .  The belief that the Christ or Messiah must suffer was not held by all the Jews.  Many thought that suffering and humiliation were incompatible with the glory and power of the Messiahship.  See  John 12:34 .
 

 
That he first by the resurrection, etc.  That is, the Messiah's manifested power over death would first reveal the light of his everlasting truth to his own people, the Jews, and to the rest of the world.

title: Acts 26:24
text: Thy much learning is turning thee mad. The 'learning' was Paul's familiarity with and powerful reasoning from the Scriptures of the Old Testament.  It was not remarkable that an affirmation that Jesus-crucified within the recollection of some then present-was alive and that he was the Messiah of the Jews should seem to Festus like the raving of a person of unsound mind.  Still more so would seem Paul's serious statements about the resurrection.  These were the very height of presumption to the governor, trained as he was in the hard, prudential maxims of Roman official life, of which religion was only a department, and not the most important one.  Roman literature contained little that was memorable about life and death, and it is not certain that Festus knew that little.  How strange to him must have seemed Paul's inspired certainty of the stupendous fact about which Roman philosophers reasoned in the dark!

title: Acts 26:26
text: For the king knoweth of these, etc.  On the judgment seat with Festus was the king to whom the apostle turned for confirmation of the reasonableness of his words.  It was a compliment, which Agrippa did not decline, though guarding against a hurtful interpretation of it.

title: Acts 26:28
text: With but little persuasion, etc.  Agrippa's reply was half truth, half embarrassment.  Paul's argument was strong; but strong also was the king's desire to remain popular with the Jews.  It would probably have cost him his crown if he had declared himself a believer in Jesus and the resurrection.

title: Acts 26:31
text: Doeth nothing worthy of death or of bonds. Agrippa saw that Paul had done nothing contrary to Jewish law and that his argument was permissible because drawn from the Scriptures.  The Jews were able controversialists, as their opposing rabbinical schools testify.  Paul had done no act which either Festus or Agrippa could pronounce a legal offence.

title: Acts 27:1
text:
They. The soldiers, by order of the governor.
 

 
Centurion. See note on  Matthew 8:5 .
 

 
The Augustan band. One of the five cohorts of imperial troops stationed at Caesarea.  A cohort contained six hundred men.

title: Acts 27:2
text:
Adramyttium. A seaport of Mysia.
 

 
Asia. The Roman province of Asia.
 

 
Aristarchus. See  Acts 19:29 Acts 20:4 .
 

 
Thessalonica. See note on  Acts 17:1 .

title: Acts 27:3
text: Sidon. A seaport on the coast of Phoenicia, twenty miles north of Tyre.

title: Acts 27:4
text: Under the lee of Cyprus. On the side of the island which was sheltered from the wind.  See note on  Acts 13:4 .

title: Acts 27:5
text:
Cilicia and Pamphylia. See note on  Acts 15:23 .
 

 
Myra. Situated on the river Andriacus, two and a half miles from the coast.  It was an important port in the grain trade.

title: Acts 27:6
text: A ship. Laden with wheat ( Acts 27:38 ).

title: Acts 27:7
text:
Cnidus. A seaport of Caria.
 

 
Crete. See note on  Acts 27:4 Acts 2:11 .
 

 
Salmone. The eastern extremity of Crete.

title: Acts 27:8
text:
Fair Havens. A bay on the southern coast of Crete.  It still retains its ancient name.
 

 
Lasea. A city about four miles east of Fair Havens.  It ruins were discovered in 1856.  Neither Fair Havens nor Lasea is known to have been mentioned by any other writer than the writer of Acts.

title: Acts 27:9
text: The Fast. That was observed on the Day of Atonement, the tenth day of Tishri, the seventh month of the Jewish year, about the same as the latter part of September and the first part of October.  Storms were the to be expected.

title: Acts 27:10
text: Lading. Cargo.

title: Acts 27:11
text: Master. The sailing master or captain.

title: Acts 27:12
text: Phoenix. The modern port of Loutro.

title: Acts 27:14
text: Euraquilo. A northeast wind.

title: Acts 27:16
text:
Under the lee. See note on  Acts 27:4 .
 

 
Cauda. Twenty-three miles south of Phoenix.

title: Acts 27:17
text:
Under-girding the ship. Passing strong ropes or cables around the hull, in order to keep the timbers in place.
 

 
Syrtis. Quicksands to the southwest of Cauda.
 

 
Lowered the gear. Let down some one of the sails, probably the mainsail.

title: Acts 27:24
text: Stand before Caesar. That is, go to Rome and be heard by the emperor.  He was to bear heroic witness for Christ in the capital of the Roman Empire.

title: Acts 27:26
text: We must be cast, etc.  A prediction which was fulfilled ( Acts 27:44 Acts 28:1 )

title: Acts 27:27
text:
The fourteenth night. After they had sailed from Fair Havens.
 

 
The sea of Adria. That part of the Mediterranean Sea which is between Italy, Greece and Africa.

title: Acts 27:28
text:
Twenty fathoms. One hundred and twenty feet.
 

 
Fifteen fathoms. Ninety feet.

title: Acts 27:40
text: The bands of the rudders. That is, lowering the rudders again into the water so that the ship could be steered safely.  The ships of ancient times had two large oar-shaped rudders, which in this case had been raised out of the water and tied fast while the ship was drifting, so that they might not be destroyed.

title: Acts 27:41
text: Where two seas meet. A narrow strait between the coast of Malta and the small island of Salmonetta.

title: Acts 28:1
text: Melita. Malts.  The scene of Paul's shipwreck is, according to tradition, St. Paul's Bay, about eight miles northwest of Valetta, the capital of the island.

title: Acts 28:2
text: Barbarians. Those who were not Greeks and Romans were called barbarians.

title: Acts 28:4
text: Justice. The goddess of justice, according to the idolatrous notions of the natives.

title: Acts 28:6
text: Said that he was a god. As they did at Lystra.  See  Acts 14:11  and notes thereon.

title: Acts 28:7
text: The chief man. An inscription since discovered verifies this title.

title: Acts 28:11
text:
Whose sign, etc.  Meaning the figurehead.
 

 
Twin Brothers. Castor and Pollux.  In Roman mythology they were sons of Jupiter.  They were the favoring gods of sailors.

title: Acts 28:12
text: Syracuse. Capital city of the island of Sicily.  It was at this time a Roman colony, and was a hundred miles north of Malta.  For explanation of a Roman colony see note on  Acts 16:12 .

title: Acts 28:13
text:
Rhegium. A city at the southern extremity of Italy, on the Straits of Messina.  Its modern name is Reggio.
 

 
Puteoli. Then the chief port of Rome.  It was on the north shore of the Bay of Naples.

title: Acts 28:15
text:
The Market of Appius. A town on the Appian Way, and forty-three miles from Rome.  It was a great resort for sailors.
 

 
The Three Taverns. A place about ten miles nearer Rome than the Market of Appius.

title: Romans 1:1
text:
Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, etc.  The salutation in  Romans 1:1-7  is remarkable as a disclosure of Paul's spiritual experience and beliefs.  It contains an affirmation of his apostleship, his message of good tidings concerning the Son of God, the fulfillment of Old Testament prophecy in the coming of Christ ( Romans 1:2 Romans 1:3 ), and the divinity of Jesus the Messiah as manifested by the resurrection ( Romans 1:4 ).  As to the name of the apostle, see notes on  Acts 7:58 Acts 13:9 .
 

 
Called. Chosen by Jesus Christ while Paul, then a persecuting Pharisee, was journeying to Damascus.  See  Acts 26:12-18 Acts 9:2-4 Acts 9:15 Acts 9:18 Acts 9:20 Acts 9:23 .
 

 
Apostle. See note on  Matthew 10:2 .
 

 
Separated. See  Acts 9:15 Acts 13:2 Galatians 1:15 Galatians 1:16 .

title: Romans 1:3
text: Of the seed of David. See  Isaiah 11:1 Mark 12:35 John 7:42 Matthew 1:1 .

title: Romans 1:4
text: According to the spirit of holiness. Or, in respect of the divine as opposed to the human, nature of our Lord.

title: Romans 1:5
text:
Grace. The favor of God shared by all believers in Jesus Christ.
 

 
Unto obedience of faith. That is, unto submission, in the spirit of Christian humility, which is essential to faith.
 

 
All the nations. The Gentiles.

title: Romans 1:6
text: Called to be Jesus Christ's. All who sincerely believe in Jesus Christ are called by him and belong to him.

title: Romans 1:7
text:
Saints. Christians, consecrated to the service of God.  In this sense all such Christians may be said to be saints.  The term does not imply perfection or entire holiness in believers, but that they shall become such by the will and under the guidance of God.
 

 
Grace. The Greek form of salutation.
 

 
Peace. The Hebrew form of salutation.
 

 
+ Romans 1:8 
 
That your faith is proclaimed. There was special importance in the strength of Christian faith at Rome, the capital of the empire and center of its power.  The cities of the provinces would be likely to follow such an example.

title: Romans 1:11
text: Some spiritual gift. That is, any spiritual advantage which his visit to Rome would enable Paul to confer.

title: Romans 1:13
text: Was hindered hitherto. See  Acts 16:6 Acts 16:7 .

title: Romans 1:14
text:
Greeks and to Barbarians. A division of mankind according to language.  'Greeks' here includes the Romans, as the majority of educated Romans spoke Greek.  In Paul's time all nations other than the Greeks and Romans were called barbarians, a term originally applied to those who could not speak a language intelligible to a Greek.
 

 
To the wise and to the foolish. The educated and the uneducated.

title: Romans 1:15
text: To you also that are in Rome. To you that are in the world's chief city. Where the claims of the gospel will be most severely scrutinized, if not contemptuously rejected; where all the imperial pride and power will be confronted by a religion whose founder died on the cross.

title: Romans 1:16
text:
Salvation. That is, eternal life.  Nothing less than this expresses the fUll meaning of salvation.  It implies final deliverance from all foes and perils, temporal and spiritual.
 

 
To every one that believeth. A free offer of salvation to all who accept Jesus Christ as Savior and Lord.
 

 
The Jew first. According to promise.
 

 
Greek. Gentiles.  Paul here divides mankind into Jew and Greek, or Gentile, according to religion.

title: Romans 1:17
text:
A righteousness of God. That is, the grace or favor of God toward mankind through faith in Jesus Christ.
 

 
From faith unto faith. In other words, one must have faith in order to receive and benefit by the divine favor, and this in turn increases faith.

title: Romans 1:18
text:
The wrath of God. The eternal and unalterable opposition of His nature to sin.
 

 
Is revealed. By the misery, loss and destruction which result from disobedience of His laws.

title: Romans 1:19
text:
That which is known of God. That which mankind has learned about God.
 

 
Is manifest in them. Is known through the light of conscience in each normal person.

title: Romans 1:20
text:
For the invisible things of him, etc.  The meaning is that the power and wisdom of God are and have always been abundantly revealed in nature.
 

 
Without excuse. Conscience and intelligence have enabled them to see the power and goodness of God in His works; they are barred from pleading ignorance.

title: Romans 1:23
text: Changed the glory of the incorruptible God, etc.  Those who had this light from God in nature nevertheless disregarded it and dishonored their Maker by turning to idolatry in its grossest forms.  Birds, beasts and even insects were worshipped as deities.  The heathen world in Paul's day was full of the proofs of this wandering away from the spiritual apprehension and worship of the true God.

title: Romans 2:2
text: According to truth. According to the degree of spiritual enlightenment and responsibility of each person.

title: Romans 2:3
text: O man, who judgest them that practice such things, etc.  The apostle means his countrymen, the Jews, and his aim is to convince them that, as they have sinned, they have no right to judge and condemn the wickedness of Gentiles.

title: Romans 2:5
text:
After. According to.
 

 
The day of wrath, etc.  The day of God's judgment upon the unrighteous ( Amos 5:18 Isaiah 2:12 Matthew 3:7 ).

title: Romans 2:8
text: Factious. Resisting the divine authority.

title: Romans 2:9
text: Every soul of man, etc.  Alluding to the penalty suffered by man's spiritual nature through disobedience.

title: Romans 2:11
text: No respect of persons with God. No partiality or favor given on account of external advantages, apart from character.

title: Romans 2:12
text:
Sinned without the law. That is, without knowing that they were acting unlawfully in the sight of God.
 

 
Shall also perish without the law. This means that such transgressors shall suffer only for the violation of their consciences, but that they shall not suffer the penalties of a law of which they were ignorant.
 

 
Under the law. 'The law' here mans law which is clearly revealed and known, and whose penalties inevitably fall upon those who disobey.

title: Romans 2:13
text: The doers of the law shall be justified. The apostle here contrasts hearers with doers of the law.  Jews thought that merely hearing the law made them better than Gentiles.  Paul means to remind them that only doers of the law, if any, shall be justified at all, that is, judged righteous according to the law and free from its penalties.  That the apostle does this only to heighten the contrast between living sincerity and dead formalism, is evident from his own showing that no one has fully obeyed the law (whether the law of conscience or the law of Moses) an therefore never has been justified or acquitted by God.  But 'justified' in this verse is not to be taken in the sense of 'justification by faith' ( Romans 5:1 ).  That is the believer's acceptance with God through faith in Jesus Christ.  It comes through a 'law of faith' ( Romans 3:27  and note thereon).

title: Romans 2:14
text: Are the law unto themselves. Gentiles, not being under the Mosaic law, governed their thoughts and acts according to the light of conscience.

title: Romans 2:15
text:
The work of the law written in their hearts. Its work or effect was to make men think and act with reference to the distinction between right and wrong.
 

 
Their conscience bearing witness therewith. But an imperfect or misleading witness unless directed and enlightened by communion with God.  As to the corruption and blindness of conscience see  I Corinthians 8:7 I Corinthians 8:10 Titus 1:15 Matthew 6:23 .

title: Romans 2:16
text:
My gospel. Paul's message to Jew and Gentile.
 

 
By Jesus Christ. The appointed agent of God in judgment.

title: Romans 2:17
text: And restest upon the law. Upon its possession, instead of active obedience to it.

title: Romans 2:20
text:
,21
 
A corrector of the foolish, etc.  The apostle condemns the Jews because of their failure to live up to the truth known to them as favored possessors of the law.  Their special danger was a false sense of security.
 

 
Thou that preachest, etc.  It was well known that many faithful observers of the ceremonial law were immoral in their private lives.

title: Romans 2:25
text: Thy circumcision is become uncircumcision. Thy special light and privilege, when disregarded, place thee spiritually among the heathen.

title: Romans 2:26
text: Be reckoned for circumcision. If the uncircumcised Gentile, in following the natural light of his conscience, does those things which are commanded by the Mosaic law, he shall be counted as one of those who possess the law.

title: Romans 3:1
text: What advantage then hath the Jew? Having shown that both Jew and Gentile have sinned and are equally under condemnation, the apostle reverts to the special advantage they still possess as being entrusted with the 'oracles of God,' the words and promises of God in the Scriptures, the Old Testament.  There were other privileges.  See  Romans 9:4 Romans 9:5 Romans 11:28-32 .  These privileges gave to the Jews the opportunity of leadership in spreading the truth among the Gentiles.

title: Romans 3:6
text:
For then how shall God judge the world? The apostle says in effect:
 
   There would be no judgment of sin at all if the arguments of some unbelieving Jews were sound.  They urge that the rejection of Jesus as Messiah only makes the faithfulness of God more clear; therefore it accomplished a certain good and cannot be so wicked.  Paul answers that their reasoning, if true, would sweep away the distinction between right and wrong and leave the world in moral darkness.

title: Romans 3:8
text: Whose condemnation is just. The condemnation of those who are so blind and willful as to say, 'Let us do evil that good may come.'

title: Romans 3:19
text:
The law. The Mosaic law.
 

 
Them that are under the law. The Jews.

title: Romans 3:20
text:
The works of the law, etc.  Acts done as tasks in obedience to a command: in other words, laboring for salvation without faith.
 

 
Through the law cometh the knowledge of sin. That is, through the law as a power of punishment.  Law is an educator; it sets up a standard, develops conscience and helps a man t discern between right and wrong.  He who violates law becomes increasingly conscious of its authority ad of the danger of disregarding it.  He learns more about the disastrous effects of sin.

title: Romans 3:21
text:
But now apart from the law, etc.  Paul does not mean to disparage the idea of law in general, but to say that the righteousness of God, in other words, the acceptance of the believer by God through faith in Jesus Christ, establishes the law ( Romans 3:31 ).
 

 
Hath been manifested. In Christ.  This righteousness is therefore a gift from God, and the believer is not entitled to claim any merit in enjoying its benefits.
 

 
Witnessed by the law and the prophets. The faith of Abraham, the chief of the race for whom the Mosaic law had been given as a discipline, was accounted as righteousness.  Therefore even in the beginning of Jewish history faith was supreme in the religious life.  See  Genesis 15:6 .

title: Romans 3:22
text: Unto all them that believe. All they who accept Jesus Christ as Savior and Lord have this righteousness.

title: Romans 3:24
text:
Being justified freely. Only those who believe are justified ( Romans 3:22 ).
 

 
The redemption. The deliverance.  The idea was developed from the ancient practice of redeeming or delivering from bondage, a slave or captive by the payment of a ransom or price.  Christ's voluntary death is here represented, in language borrowed from the customs of war and the marketplace, as the price he paid to bring us into favor with God.  See  Mark 10:45 I Corinthians 6:20 I Timothy 2:6 .

title: Romans 3:25
text:
A propitiation. That which wins favor.
 

 
Of the sins done aforetime. The times of ignorance, in which God did not punish sin, 'passing over' it, or temporarily delaying the judgment and penalty.

title: Romans 3:27
text: A law of faith. The requirement of faith in God's goodness, which brings the believer into intimate communion with Him.  By 'law of faith' Paul means the condition or means whereby man comes into acceptance with God; the law of faith is the way of faith.

title: Romans 3:28
text: Is justified by faith apart, etc.  This is true only when living faith is contrasted with works done as tasks to gain merit.  But a living faith naturally results in good works; works are the thermometer of faith and measure its sincerity and fervor.

title: Romans 3:30
text: He shall justify the circumcision, etc.  A contrast between Jewish and Gentile Christians is indicated here.  The former thought that they were justified by faith because they already had circumcision and obeyed the Mosaic law; but they also thought that Gentile Christians could not be justified until, in addition to faith, they observed the Mosaic law and were circumcised.  Paul here reminds both that they are wrong, that justification is by faith.

title: Romans 4:1
text: Hath found according to the flesh. The meaning is, what special benefit had Abraham by being circumcised?

title: Romans 4:3
text: For what saith the scripture? The apostle, who is here speaking to the Jews, shows them that justification by faith is found in their Scriptures; that it is as old as Abraham, to whom his faith was accounted righteousness before God.  Paul's line of argument brings out the fact that the Jews did not understand the inner meaning of the revelation God had made to them.

title: Romans 4:4
text: To him that worketh, etc.  Referring to the wages of the daily toiler, which are paid to him as a debt.

title: Romans 4:5
text: That justifieth the ungodly. Accepting the faith even of the wicked who turn to Him.  The thought is that the ungodly, through faith, may be brought into acceptance with God without works, and apart from works.  But see note on  Romans 3:28 .

title: Romans 4:10
text: In uncircumcision. The faith of Abraham long preceded his circumcision.  See  Genesis 15:6 Genesis 17:10 Genesis 17:24 .

title: Romans 4:11
text:
A seal. Completing, or in token of, his acceptance through faith.
 

 
The father of all them that believe. The supreme example of the power of faith among men.

title: Romans 4:12
text: The father of circumcision, etc.  The apostle intends here to emphasize, for the benefit of his own race, the true view of circumcision.  Abraham was not the father of circumcision in the traditional Jewish sense of the term; he was the father only of the circumcised who had faith.  See  Romans 2:28 Romans 2:29 .

title: Romans 4:13
text: Heir of the world. See  Genesis 12:2-4 Genesis 22:17-19 .

title: Romans 4:14
text: Faith is made void, etc.  The meaning of the verse is that faith is necessary to heirship.

title: Romans 4:15
text: The law worketh wrath. See  Romans 3:20  and note thereon.

title: Romans 4:16
text:
For this cause. That is, since the 'law worketh wrath' and there is no hope for mankind by reason of their willful persistence in breaking the law.
 

 
It is of faith. Since the law has failed, salvation must be by faith, a free gift to those who believe.
 

 
May be sure to all the seed. Salvation must be by faith, on the believer's part, and 'according to grace' or the favor of God, in order that the promise may be 'sure,' by a power above the law (whether the law of Moses or the law of conscience) which is constantly being broken; and sure 'to all the seed,' all those who have faith.  'Seed' means here both Jewish and Gentile believers, all who, like Abraham, had faith.

title: Romans 4:18
text: Who. Abraham.

title: Romans 4:25
text:
Delivered up. By the Father ( Romans 8:32 ); nevertheless the death of Christ was voluntary; he delivered up himself ( Galatians 2:20 Ephesians 5:2 ).
 

 
Raised for our justification. For our justification by faith.  If Christ had not been raised from the dead, faith in him, as emphasized by the apostle, would have had no beginning and no purpose or end to which it could have been directed.  See  Acts 17:31 .  Without the resurrection the gospel message, through which justification by faith is given, would never have been proclaimed.

title: Romans 5:1
text:
:11
 
Peace with God. The first and greatest consequence of justification by faith.  It includes all the blessings specified by the apostle in these verses.
 

 
This grace. This favor.
 

 
Rejoice in our tribulations. Peace with God warrants rejoicing under all circumstances.  See  Philippians 4:4-7 .
 

 
Weak. Through sinfulness.
 

 
A righteous man. A just, upright, moral man.  A 'righteous' man in this sense might not inspire such affection and devotion as would cause one to die for him.  One would 'scarcely' die for a man whose righteousness made him appear self-sufficient.
 

 
The good man. 'Good' is here intended to represent a more lovable kind of man than 'righteous.'
 

 
Christ died for us. The apostle here brings out the contrast between the timid, halting selfishness of those who would refuse to die even for the 'righteous' or the 'good,' and the compassionate self-surrender of Christ, who died for sinners.
 

 
By his life. By union of the believer's life with the life of the risen Christ.

title: Romans 5:12
text: As through one man sin entered, etc.  Entered the world through man's inheriting a sinful tendency.

title: Romans 5:13
text:
Until the law sin was in the world. The Mosaic law is here meant.  Sin, the violation of God's command, was in the world 'until,' that is, before, the law of Moses was given.
 

 
But sin is not imputed, etc.  That is, the transgressions of God's law committed by those who were not fully conscious of what they were doing, did not merit the same penalty as that incurred by willful transgressors against the clearer light under the law.

title: Romans 5:14
text:
Even over them, etc.  Even over those who had not, like Adam, continuously sinned.
 

 
Figure. Type.
 

 
Him that was to come. Christ.

title: Romans 5:15
text:
:17
 
But not as the trespass, so also is the free gift. The apostle in these verses emphasizes the life-giving work of Christ as compared with the death-bringing transgression of Adam.  On the one side are trespass, sin, judgment, death; on the other, free gift, grace, justification, righteousness, life.  In  Romans 5:14  Adam was the type of Christ in the sense that he so lived and sinned that he brought death on mankind without their fault; in  Romans 5:15-17  Christ, the last Adam, is represented as so living and suffering that he brought eternal life to mankind without their merit.  Adam is represented as the type of Christ only in so far as to heighten the stupendous contrast between the life and work of each.

title: Romans 5:18
text:
One act of righteousness. The meaning here is, the justification obtained by Jesus Christ for mankind.  It does not refer only to the death of Christ.
 

 
Justification of life. Justification whose effect is life.

title: Romans 5:20
text:
The law came in besides. Came in as an afterthought.
 

 
That the trespass might abound. That is, that sin might multiply in order to show the failure of the law to uproot it.

title: Romans 5:21
text: Reigned in death. Reigned as a tyrant in the midst of the ruin he had caused.  Sin is here personified.

title: Romans 6:3
text: Into his death. Into the death to sin obtained for the believer by Christ's voluntary sacrifice of himself.

title: Romans 6:4
text:
We were buried therefore, etc.  The apostle means to emphasize the idea that the true believer is so inseparably united by faith to Jesus Christ, the slain and risen Savior, that he shares both the grave and the resurrection glory with him.
 

 
Newness of life. A life free from the trammels and dangers of the old experience, even as the life of Christ after the resurrection was more free and glorious than his life on earth.

title: Romans 6:6
text:
Our old man. Our old self.  Compare  Romans 7:22 II Corinthians 4:16 Ephesians 3:16 Ephesians 4:22 Ephesians 4:24 Colossians 3:9 I Peter 3:4 .
 

 
The body of sin. The body considered as the instrument or servant of sin ( Colossians 2:11-13 ).

title: Romans 6:7
text: He that hath died. He who has died in Christ; he who has shared in Christ's death to sin.

title: Romans 6:10
text: Liveth unto God. For evermore.

title: Romans 6:13
text: As alive from the dead. As in the possession of eternal life.  See note on  John 11:25-27 .

title: Romans 6:14
text:
Not under law, but under grace. That is, under law in the wider sense of the term; any code of rules.
 

 
Under grace. In a state of acceptance with God; justified by faith.

title: Romans 6:16
text: Servants unto obedience. Servants who really obey.  The apostle takes his illustration from slavery, because only slavery, where the master has absolute power over the life and liberty of the slave, could here adequately represent the truth about man's position and dangers under the power of sin.  Each person must chose his or her master, must take a line of conduct which leads either to spiritual freedom (life), or spiritual slavery and denial of life (death).

title: Romans 6:17
text: That form of teaching, etc.  Their lessons in Christian faith and practice.  See  Acts 2:42 .

title: Romans 6:19
text:
I speak after the manner of men, etc.  The apostle illustrated the fact of the deliverance of the Corinthian Christians from sin by employing the language of the slave market, with which they were familiar.
 

 
Righteousness unto sanctification. The had chosen the right Master, Christ; let them now proceed, by growth in the spiritual life, unto sanctification.

title: Romans 6:20
text: Were free in regard of righteousness. In other words, they knew nothing about it.

title: Romans 6:22
text: Ye have your fruit unto sanctification, etc.  Paul here contrasts the shame and humiliation due to fleeting, sinful pleasures, with the blessedness and eternal life resulting from acceptance of Jesus Christ as the gift of God.

title: Romans 7:1
text:
Or are ye ignorant, brethren, etc.  The question is asked with the object of explaining how Christians are not under the law.  Had his Jewish converts forgotten that the power of law over a person ends with the latter's death?  Had he not made clear to them that a believer who becomes dead to sin with Christ is thereby released from the power of law, having been saved by faith?  There was evidently some lingering confusion of thought on the subject, which the apostle sought to remove by an illustration taken from the law of marriage ( Romans 6:2 Romans 6:3 ).
 

 
Men who know the law. 'Law' is here used in the wider sense of the term; law in general.

title: Romans 7:4
text: Wherefore, my brethren, ye also were made dead to the law, etc.  The apostle here extends the argument from the law of marriage, to the law which, when broken, results in sin and death.  As the woman was released from the marriage law by the death of her husband, so the Christian is released from the law of sin by the death of his old self, through his union with the crucified and risen Christ.

title: Romans 7:5
text: The sinful passions, which were through the law. 'Sinful passions,' those which have led to wrong indulgence through yielding to temptation.  Nevertheless the tempted one's failure came through the existence of the law ( Romans 7:7 ).

title: Romans 7:6
text: Newness of the spirit. Newness of motive, intention and outlook, resulting from the ascent to a higher plane of life.

title: Romans 7:7
text: Not known sin, except through the law. The apostle means that the law gave him the occasion for sin and brought down the penalties of transgression upon him.  'Known' is here practically equivalent to 'committed.'  In  Romans 2:20  there is a somewhat different meaning.  The 'knowledge of sin' is there equivalent to the discovery or detection of sin.  In  Romans 7:7-25  the apostle most probably outlines his own experience before he found deliverance from the law by faith in the risen Christ.  He means to record his experience as typical of that of the average person.

title: Romans 7:8
text:
Finding occasion. Through the law.
 

 
Apart from the law sin is dead. The consciousness of wrongdoing first comes from the shock of broken law, from the check to natural inclinations.

title: Romans 7:9
text:
Alive apart from the law once. During the time of undeveloped conscience, when he was happily unconscious of any disobedience of the law.  It may have been in his youth, or even in the period of his Pharisaic self-satisfaction and persecution of the Christians.
 

 
Sin revived. By the knowledge that law had been violated.
 

 
Died. Felt condemned.

title: Romans 7:10
text:
The commandment, which was unto life. See  Romans 10:5 Leviticus 18:5 
 

 
Found to be unto death. By reason of his inability to obey it.

title: Romans 7:11
text:
Beguiled me. Signifying the deceiving allurements of sin.  The sinner, by breaking the moral law, does not really obtain what he expected; the fancied pleasure or gain turns to ashes, so to speak, in his possession or seems worse than worthless by reason of the loss and suffering it brings back upon him.  In this sense a breaker of the law is always 'beguiled' or deceived.  See  Genesis 3:13 II Corinthians 11:3 I Timothy 2:14 .
 

 
Slew me. With the realized feeling of guilt.

title: Romans 7:12
text: The law is holy. The apostle emphasizes the holiness of the law in contrast to the degrading results of sin.  He had spoken so often about deliverance from sin and law that a critical Jew might have objected that the two terms were intended to mean the same thing.  But Paul, while admitting that the law is the occasion of sin, and even provokes sin, is careful to prevent any confusion of thought by affirming that the law is holy.

title: Romans 7:13
text: But sin. The meaning becomes clear by adding, 'became death unto me.'

title: Romans 7:14
text:
The law is spiritual. Requires the control of the flesh by the spirit.
 

 
Am carnal, sold under sin. Am therefore unable to obey the law.

title: Romans 7:16
text: I consent unto the law. Unto its authority, the rightful rule of the spirit over the flesh.

title: Romans 7:17
text: No more I. 'I' here is the higher self.  See  Romans 7:20 .

title: Romans 7:18
text:
Flesh. The higher self gone wrong.
 

 
To will is present with me. The wish to do right is ever before me.
 

 
To do that which is good is not. The wish fails to result in actually doing good.

title: Romans 7:22
text: The inward man. The light of conscience and reason.

title: Romans 7:23
text:
But I see a different law in my members. 'I', the higher self, am conscious that the delight of the inward man in the law of God cannot be realized, owing to 'a different law,' the power of sin, 'in my members' or, over the flesh.
 

 
The law of my mind. See note on  Romans 7:22 .

title: Romans 7:24
text: The body of this death. The sinful tendency of the unregenerate self.  See  Romans 6:6  and notes thereon.

title: Romans 7:25
text:
I thank God. Because of the deliverance from 'the body of this death' through faith in Jesus Christ.
 

 
So then I of myself, etc.  These and the remaining words of the verse indicate that, although the law of God is uppermost in the mind of him who has been delivered from sin by accepting Christ, yet the deliverance is only fully and finally realized by continuing the inward struggle between the spirit and the flesh.

title: Romans 8:1
text: In Christ Jesus. Justified and sanctified by faith in him and union with him.  In this chapter the apostle outlines the results of faith in the spiritual life and joy of the believer.

title: Romans 8:2
text:
The law of the Spirit of life. The way or process of the Spirit of life.  See note on  Romans 3:27 .
 

 
Made me free, etc.  The power of the Spirit of life destroys the power of sin and death.

title: Romans 8:3
text:
What the law could not do. What it was powerless to do.
 

 
In that it was weak through the flesh. Because it was unable to regenerate and sanctify. The nature of the 'flesh,' or the unregenerate self, could not be changed by the law.
 

 
God, sending his own Son. The sinless life of Jesus in the flesh 'condemned sin in the flesh.'

title: Romans 8:4
text: That the ordinance of the law might be fulfilled in us. The law itself was utterly powerless to vindicate its ordinance, or requirement, of holiness; but faith in Christ enables the believer to do this, that is, to fulfill the holiness of the law not by a perfect obedience, by a continued inner conflict with sin inevitably resulting in final victory through faith.

title: Romans 8:8
text: In the flesh. Ruled by the flesh.

title: Romans 8:9
text: In the Spirit, if so be, etc.  Showing the power and glory of the Spirit from the moment of its dwelling in the believer's heart.  This was not to be won by effort, but received through faith.

title: Romans 8:10
text:
The body is dead. The physical body doomed to die as the punishment of sin.
 

 
The spirit is life because of righteousness. The human spirit in whom the Divine Spirit has begun to dwell through faith in Christ.  'Life' here means eternal life, which results from the righteousness made possible by Christ.

title: Romans 8:12
text:
:17
 
So then, brethren, we are debtors, etc.  In these verses Christians are urged to live according to their privileges as sons and heirs of God.
 

 
Not to the flesh. But to the Spirit, who alone can deliver from the rule of the flesh.
 

 
Ye must die. Because the way of the flesh, or the sinning self, leads to destruction.
 

 
Sons of God. Fully conscious of their rights and privileges, as compared with children under guardianship and tutelage.
 

 
The spirit of bondage. The feeling of servile subjection and liability to punishment.
 

 
The spirit of adoption. Fatherly love attraction filial devotion.  'Adoption' derives special force in this passage by reason of its contrast to fatherhood and sonship in the ordinary sense.  Among the Greeks and Romans one who was entirely unrelated to the family could be made a son by legal process.  Here the Father is represented as willing to accept, or adopt, as sons those who are alien to him as slaves to sin.  See  Galatians 4:5 Galatians 4:6 .
 

 
Abba, Father. 'Abba' is Chaldee for 'father.'  Both words, though they have the same meaning, are used by the apostle according to a custom, which had obtained among Gentile converts.  Our Lord used the same expression ( Mark 14:36 ).
 

 
Beareth witness with our spirit. The human spirit is conscious of and testifies to the approval of the Divine Spirit.
 

 
Joint-heirs. See  Romans 8:29 .

title: Romans 8:18
text: For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time, etc.  In  Romans 8:18-25  the believer is exhorted to remain steadfast and to consider his sufferings as of no account in view of the glory that shall be revealed.  The apostle reckons or counts the gains as compared with the losses in accepting Christ, but finds the glory to come incalculably greater than the sufferings of the present.  The 'glory' is companionship with the risen Christ, the being made more perfect with him in heaven after suffering on earth in obedience to him.

title: Romans 8:19
text:
The earnest expectation of the creation waiteth, etc.  'Creation' here means nature as commonly understood; all life as well as things without life.  It is poetically conceived of by the apostle, as sharing in the higher life which man shall attain to by faith in Jesus Christ.
 

 
The sons of God. See notes on  Romans 8:12-17 I Corinthians 15:51-53 I Thessalonians 4:16 I Thessalonians 4:17 .

title: Romans 8:20
text:
Was subjected. See  Genesis 3:17-19 .
 

 
Vanity. Evil, loss, delusion.  See  Ephesians 4:17 II Peter 2:1 
 

 
Him who subjected it. God.

title: Romans 8:21
text:
The bondage of corruption. The processes of physical decay, disintegration and death.
 

 
The liberty of the glory, etc.  The free development of the spiritual and mental powers.

title: Romans 8:22
text: Now. The time of deliverance which had just come through the truths of the gospel.

title: Romans 8:23
text:
The first fruits of the Spirit. The pledge of the spiritual harvest to come.  See  Romans 11:16 Romans 16:5 I Corinthians 15:20 .
 

 
Redemption of our body. Release from physical decay and death.

title: Romans 8:24
text: Hope that is seen is not hope. When the thing hoped for is seen, it then ceases to be an object of hope.

title: Romans 8:26
text: Our infirmity. Human weakness and limitations, especially, in this connection, inability 'to pray as we ought.'

title: Romans 8:27
text:
He that searcheth the hearts knoweth, etc.  God, the Father.
 

 
The mind of the Spirit. The intention.
 

 
The saints. Consecrated believers in Christ.  See note on  Romans 1:7 .

title: Romans 8:28
text:
All things. Earthly trials and misfortunes as well as rewards and successes.
 

 
His purpose. Which is to have mercy upon all ( Romans 11:32 ).  This contradicts the idea that God intends to save some and reject others.

title: Romans 8:29
text:
,30
 
Foreknew. See note on  Romans 11:2 .
 

 
 Foreordained. See  Acts 4:28 I Corinthians 2:7 Ephesians 1:5 Ephesians 1:11 .
 

 
Conformed. Made essentially similar.
 

 
Called...Justified...Glorified. There is nothing in these two verses which contradicts the truth that God's foreknowledge and foreordination are in harmony with his gracious purpose to have mercy upon all ( Romans 8:28 ).

title: Romans 8:31
text: If God is for us, who is against us? A question equivalent to the strongest affirmation of the safety of Christian believers.  This safety is the theme of the remaining verses of the chapter.

title: Romans 8:33
text:
Elect. See  Romans 8:29 Romans 8:30  and notes thereon.
 

 
It is God that justifieth. On account of Christ's life, death and resurrection.

title: Romans 8:34
text: Intercession. See  Hebrews 7:25 I Timothy 2:1 .

title: Romans 8:37
text: More than conquerors. Not only victorious over all enemies, but stronger in faith and knowledge through the intensity of the struggle ( II Corinthians 4:17 ).

title: Romans 8:38
text:
,39
 
For I am persuaded, etc.  Or, I am confident.
 

 
Neither death, nor life. Neither the terrors of death, which are certain, nor the changing allurements and uncertainties of life.
 

 
Angels. Paul's mention of angels was intended as a condemnation of Jewish extravagant beliefs in them and worship of them.  In the earlier history of the Jews angels were considered as messengers of God to men, but after the Babylonian captivity the belief in evil angels became widespread.  The latter are meant in  Romans 8:38 .
 

 
Principalities. A Jewish title for a high rank in the hierarchy of angels.
 

 
Powers. To be taken in the same sense as principalities.
 

 
Nor height, nor depth. An expression for the immensity of space.
 

 
Any other creature. All else not already mentioned.

title: Romans 9:2
text:
:5
 
I have great sorrow, etc.  Paul's grief over the exclusion of the Jews from the Messianic kingdom impelled him all the more keenly to refute Jewish reasons against Christianity that were based on that exclusion.  He maintained that Christianity was the fulfillment of the Messianic kingdom; but Jewish objectors replied that this could not be true if their race was shut out from that kingdom.  The apostle, in an argument extending through this and the two following chapters, show how God freely chooses such peoples and spiritual agencies as suit 'His purpose; that because the Jews rejected Christ God admitted the Gentiles to that position in the Messianic kingdom which the Jews might have obtained.  Moreover, it is in the power of those who have been chosen or elected by God to reject the benefits of His grace.  The Jews were chosen and fell away because of their refusal to accept the gospel, and Gentiles who are chosen may also fall away; but the purpose of God through the chastisement of disobedience is to be merciful to all, both Jew and Gentile ( Romans 11:32 ).
 

 
Anathema. Devoted to ruin.
 

 
Israelites. The God-governed people.  'Hebrew' refers to the language; 'Jew' to the racial contrast between the chosen people and Gentiles.
 

 
Adoption. Of Israelites as God's chosen ( Exodus 4:22 ).
 

 
Glory. God's presence as manifested on the mercy seat.  See  Exodus 25:22 Leviticus 16:2 .
 

 
Covenants. With Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
 

 
Service. Of the Tabernacle and the Temple.
 

 
Promises. Of the coming of the Messiah ( Romans 1:2 Galatians 3:19 Hebrews 6:12 Hebrews 11:13 ).
 

 
God. See  John 1:1 John 10:30 Colossians 2:9 .

title: Romans 9:6
text: Not all Israel, that are of Israel. Not all who are descended from Israel shall inherit the promises.

title: Romans 9:7
text: Neither, because they are Abraham's seed, etc.  Those who are Abraham's children by natural descent shall not for that reason alone inherit the promises.

title: Romans 9:8
text:
Children of the flesh. By natural descent.
 

 
Children of the promise. Children born in fulfillment of the divine promise.  See  Galatians 4:23 .

title: Romans 9:11
text:
The purpose of God. To save mankind ( Romans 8:28 Ephesians 1:9-11 )
 

 
Not of works, but of him that calleth. Free choice by God, apart from human merit.

title: Romans 9:13
text: Hated. Rejected.  The apostle, in quoting from the prophet Malachi, does not mean the individuals Jacob and Esau but the nations, Judah and Edom, of which they respectively were ancestors.  Paul here opposes the Jewish claim of exclusiveness on the ground of physical descent, and in the course of his argument contrasts the destiny of Israel with that of other nations.  Throughout  Romans 9:1-14:23  the apostle considers chiefly nations, not individuals, as affected by the purposes of God.

title: Romans 9:14
text: With God. The words are used with reference to God as a righteous judge, implying that there cannot be injustice in His court, or toward those who appear at His bar.

title: Romans 9:15
text: For he saith to Moses, etc.  The meaning is: God cannot have been unjust in preferring one nation to another because, with regard to Judah and Edom.  He did the same with regard to Moses, whom He also chose freely, apart from any merit in the chosen one.  Nor was God's choice arbitrary; His supreme will and purpose in choosing were to be taken as final, in accordance with His nature.

title: Romans 9:16
text: Runneth. As in a race.  Neither man's power of will nor his most strenuous action can have merit in claiming God's favor.

title: Romans 9:17
text:
The scripture saith Here equivalent to 'God saith.'
 

 
Did I raise thee up. Pharaoh was chosen that he might be an everlasting example of divine justice.

title: Romans 9:19
text: Thou will say then. The apostle often wrote as if in the presence of opponents who must be refuted.

title: Romans 9:20
text:
,21
 
Nay but, O man, who art thou, etc.  'Man' represents the Jewish people.  Paul addresses them as objecting on the ground that, if God hardened their hearts as he hardened the heart of Pharaoh, they were blameless.  Even in their rejection of Christ, therefore, they were fulfilling God's purpose and were not accountable.  The apostle rebukes them because of their presumption in finding fault with their Maker, from whim their being is derived.  The illustration of the potter and clay has often been too narrowly considered.  Nothing more is meant than the selection of certain nations for certain tasks, and the implied rejection of others.  There could be no intention to doom any one nation to final dishonor or destruction, as that would contradict the gracious purpose of God to have mercy upon all ( Romans 11:32 ).

title: Romans 9:22
text:
Endured with much longsuffering. The apostle shows how God, far from arbitrarily punishing the Jews, had borne patiently with their shortcomings and sins.  Jewish history had, in fact, been a record of His mercy.
 

 
Vessels of wrath. Deserving wrath and punishment.
 

 
Filled unto destruction. Fitted for it by their own unwillingness to be molded into vessels of honor.  Scholars have noticed the significant absence of 'He' from before 'fitted.'

title: Romans 9:23
text: Vessels of mercy. Vessels receiving and enjoying His mercy.  The figure of the potter and the clay is continued; but the average reader often forgets that if God is the potter, man is the clay made in God's image and therefore free to be molded into the image of God, or to reject His grace.

title: Romans 9:24
text: Also from the Gentiles. Not only had the Gentiles been chosen as a result of the rejection of Christ by the Jews, but they had been included in the mercy of God from the beginning.

title: Romans 9:28
text: Finishing it and cutting it short. In  Isaiah 10:22 Isaiah 10:23 , here quoted, it is shown that the judgment of the Lord will be summary and decisive.

title: Romans 9:29
text:
Sabaoth. Hosts.
 

 
Sodom. See  Genesis 18:1-19:38 Matthew 11:23 Matthew 11:24 Luke 10:12 .

title: Romans 9:30
text:
What shall we say then? What then shall we conclude?
 

 
Who followed not after righteousness. The Gentiles had not, like the Jews, an ideal set before them by revelation.
 

 
Righteousness which is of faith. The righteousness of God, as revealed in the gospel; the state of acceptance with God.

title: Romans 9:31
text:
A law of righteousness. Here the Mosaic law.
 

 
Did not arrive at that law. Did not arrive at, or fulfill, the purpose of that law.  They missed the goal of true righteousness by working along the line of precepts and minute observances.  They had not the faith of their father Abraham which was accounted unto him for righteousness.

title: Romans 9:32
text: The stone of stumbling. The truth in which they would not believe; their wrong attitude toward faith was the cause of their stumbling.

title: Romans 9:33
text: A stone of stumbling and a rock of offence. Jesus Christ ( Matthew 21:42 I Corinthians 1:23 ).

title: Romans 10:1
text:
8
 
The word of faith. Which demands faith as the way of salvation.
 

 
Which we preach. Which was therefore already known to many Jews.

title: Romans 10:2
text:
I bear them witness. Paul had once shared their unbelief and now understood its limitations.
 

 
Not according to knowledge. Lacking spiritual insight ( Colossians 1:9 ).

title: Romans 10:3
text:
God's righteousness. The righteousness as revealed in the gospel.  See  Romans 9:30 Romans 9:31  and notes thereon.
 

 
Did not subject themselves to the righteousness of God. Did not submit to God in humble faith.

title: Romans 10:4
text:
For Christ is the end of the law. The termination of the Mosaic law, which came to a close when Christ appeared.
 

 
Unto righteousness. Acceptance with God through faith in Christ.

title: Romans 10:5
text:
The righteousness which is of the law. A perfect obedience to which none attained ( Romans 7:14 Romans 7:15 ).
 

 
Shall live thereby. Shall live in happiness in this world and hereafter.

title: Romans 10:6
text: The righteousness which is of faith. The righteousness of God.  See notes on  Romans 9:30 Romans 9:31 .  This righteousness is here personified.

title: Romans 10:7
text: The abyss. Hades, the abode of departed spirits.  See  Acts 2:27 I Peter 3:19 I Peter 4:6 .

title: Romans 10:9
text: Because if thou shalt confess, etc.  The apostle here explains the conditions of salvation as implied in the preceding verse and follows the order there indicated, thus making confession first and faith second.  His meaning is that faith, which is really first, is valueless unless it results in confession.

title: Romans 10:10
text:
The heart. The seat of the inward thoughts and affections.
 

 
Unto righteousness. Resulting in righteousness.
 

 
Salvation. Eternal life.  See note on  Romans 1:16 .

title: Romans 10:12
text:
Lord of all. With power to save all.  See 1Co 12.5; Ac 10.36; Php 2.10,11.
 

 
Rich. In the gifts and blessings of the Spirit ( Ephesians 3:8 ).
 

 
Unto all that call upon him. Why invoke him in prayer, thus recognizing his divinity ( I Corinthians 1:2 ).

title: Romans 10:14
text:
,15
 
In whom they have not believed. An argument for the conversion of the heathen.  In these verses the apostle meant to emphasize the truth that the Jews themselves ought to have sent missionaries to proclaim the Messiah to Gentiles.

title: Romans 10:17
text: The word of Christ. See note on  Romans 10:8 .

title: Romans 10:18
text: But I say, Did they not hear? At this time the gospel message had been proclaimed in all the chief cities of the Roman empire which had a Jewish population.

title: Romans 10:19
text: But I say, Did Israel not know? Had Israel not received prophetic warning that the Gentiles would accept the Messiah, and that the Jews themselves would reject him?  Both Moses and Isaiah proved the contrary.

title: Romans 10:20
text: Isaiah is very bold. Very certain and specific.

title: Romans 11:1
text: The tribe of Benjamin. The tribes of Judah and Benjamin remained faithful to the House of David.  Jerusalem was in the territory of the tribe of Benjamin.

title: Romans 11:2
text: Which he foreknew. And included in His purpose to have mercy upon all ( Romans 11:32 ).  See notes on  Romans 8:28 Romans 8:30 Romans 8:31 .

title: Romans 11:4
text: Baal. The Sun god or chief deity of the Canaanites.  'Baal' means lord.  Each locality had its special Baal, and the various local Baals were summed up under the name of Baalim, 'lords.'

title: Romans 11:5
text:
Remnant. The Jews who had accepted Christ.  Paul aims in this chapter to show that the rejection of the Jews was only temporary.  Some had been faithful and even the great majority, though they had rejected Christ, were not finally cast off.  The Gentiles had been admitted to the place in God's favor, which the chosen people might have had.  Influenced by Gentile example, the Jews would yet accept Christ.
 

 
The election of grace. Chosen by the favor of God apart from merit or works.

title: Romans 11:6
text: Otherwise grace is no more grace. That is, if it can be earned and demanded as a debt.

title: Romans 11:7
text:
That which Israel seeketh for, that he obtained not. Because righteousness was attempted as a task instead of being accepted by faith as the gift of God.
 

 
Election. See  Romans 11:5 .
 

 
Were hardened. By their own faults.

title: Romans 11:8
text: A spirit of stupor. By their failure in faith they had become spiritually insensible.

title: Romans 11:9
text:
A snare and a trap. The spiritual self-sufficiency, ending in unbelief and worldliness, which had resulted from the Jews trusting in the mere possession of the law and its ordinances.
 

 
Recompense. Penalty.

title: Romans 11:11
text:
Did they stumble that they might fall? The question here implies that the stumbling did not and could not end in a final fall; their temporary fall due to their rejection of Christ resulted in the salvation of the Gentiles.
 

 
Jealousy. Ending in the desire to emulate the Gentiles in willingness to accept Christ.

title: Romans 11:12
text: Their fullness. The salvation by faith of the whole Jewish people.

title: Romans 11:13
text:
,14
 
I speak to you that are Gentiles. In these two verses Paul's intention is to remind the Gentiles that what he wrote about the Jews has an application to them also.  He rejoices in the probability that, by reason of the Gentiles, people of his own race may be saved.

title: Romans 11:15
text:
Reconciling of the world. See  II Corinthians 5:18 II Corinthians 5:19 Colossians 1:20 .
 

 
Life from the dead. Their salvation by faith would be spiritual life, or as a resurrection from the dead compared with their former condition.

title: Romans 11:16
text:
First fruit. See  Numbers 15:19-21 .  The first fruits were Abraham and the other Jewish patriarchs.
 

 
Holy. Here to be taken in the sense of being set apart, dedicated to God.

title: Romans 11:17
text: Thou, being a wild olive, etc.  Referring to the Gentiles, who were without the special favor, which God had shown to the Jews, and were therefore a worthless branch of wild olive in comparison with the real olive tree.

title: Romans 11:18
text: Glory not over the branches. Do not be proud and scornful toward the Jews because you have gained their place in God's favor.

title: Romans 11:21
text: Neither will he spare thee. A warning to the Gentiles in the church at Rome and other places to continue in faith.

title: Romans 11:23
text: Shall be grafted in. Saved by faith.

title: Romans 11:26
text: The Deliverer. See  I Thessalonians 1:10 .

title: Romans 11:27
text: When I shall take away their sins. A covenant of forgiveness of sins as contrasted with a covenant under which laws were to be obeyed.

title: Romans 11:28
text:
As touching the gospel. In regard to God's purpose in spreading the gospel.
 

 
Enemies. Punished as enemies for their rejection of Christ.
 

 
Election. God's favor to them as the chosen people.
 

 
The fathers' sake. The patriarchs; the great ancestors.

title: Romans 11:29
text: Not repented of. That is, God's purpose of mercy in regard to the Jews remains the same.

title: Romans 11:30
text:
,31
 
But now have obtained mercy. The disobedience of both Jews and Gentiles is emphasized in order to bring out more clearly their deliverance through God's mercy.  The fact that Jews were especially favored did not in this respect put them in a more advantageous position than Gentiles.

title: Romans 11:32
text:
God hath shut up all unto disobedience. 'All' here has no reference to individuals, but to the great mass of Jews and Gentiles, collectively considered, who have rejected God's goodness.
 

 
That he might have mercy upon all. Here appears the divine purpose from the beginning.  The penalties of disobedience were inflicted only to make the divine mercy supremely manifest.  The Jews were first favored by God, but fell away from Him; the Gentiles had also fallen away through neglecting the light of conscience within them, but afterwards heard the divine message and received salvation.  But in all God's discipline of both Jews and Gentiles His supreme purpose was to have mercy upon them.

title: Romans 11:33
text: Unsearchable. Not to be fully understood and explained.

title: Romans 11:35
text: Who hath first given to him, etc.  Who hath laid God under any obligation?  God's mercy without man's merit is the underlying truth.

title: Romans 12:1
text:
I beseech you therefore, brethren, etc.  In  Romans 12:1-13:14  the apostle gives the practical application to all Christian life of the truths set forth in the preceding chapters.  'Therefore' implies a brief review of and conclusion from the considerations through which the goodness and mercy of God have been made clear, so that believers might promptly act conformably thereto.
 

 
A living sacrifice. In contrast the dead bodies of beasts sacrificed under the Mosaic law.

title: Romans 12:2
text: Transformed. The word has the same meaning as in  Matthew 1:1-28:20 Matthew 17:2 II Corinthians 3:18 .

title: Romans 12:3
text:
Through the grace that was given me. By virtue of which he exercised the authority of an apostle ( Romans 1:5 ).
 

 
A measure of faith. According to which each believer was also to exercise the gift and perform the task allotted to him.

title: Romans 12:5
text: One body in Christ. Through union with him.  See  I Corinthians 12:1-14:40 Ephesians 4:15 Ephesians 4:16 Colossians 1:18 .

title: Romans 12:7
text:
Ministry. Service, practical Christian work.
 

 
He that teacheth. An expounder of Christian truth.  See  I Corinthians 12:28 Ephesians 4:11 .

title: Romans 12:8
text:
He that exhorteth. A variety of teaching, more especially with reference to encouraging and consoling those oppressed by difficulties.
 

 
He that ruleth. One in any position of authority.

title: Romans 12:13
text: /Communicating to the necessities of the saints. Freely relieving their poverty and distress.  See  Acts 2:42 Acts 2:45 .

title: Romans 12:14
text: Bless. See  Matthew 5:44 .

title: Romans 12:15
text: Rejoice with them that rejoice, etc.  Show sympathy under all circumstances, whether joyful or sorrowful; as Jesus did at the Cana marriage feast and on the way with the mourners to the tomb of Lazarus.  See note on  John 11:35 .

title: Romans 12:16
text: Be of the same mind. Have steadfast confidence in and unchanging kindness toward one another.

title: Romans 12:17
text: Render to no man evil for evil. See  Matthew 5:39 I Thessalonians 5:15 .

title: Romans 13:1
text: The higher powers. The state; civil authority.  The apostle in this chapter speaks of the Christian's duty to civil rulers.  No reference is made to any particular form of government; but obedience is commanded to civil government in general, or 'the powers that be,' which 'are ordained of God.'  Religious principle therefore sanctions obedience to the civil power.  These instructions to Christians in Rome were urgently needed, especially by the Jewish converts.  The Jewish population of Rome at that time was turbulent.  It was in every way desirable that Christians should appear law-abiding.  Paul's Roman citizenship, and the protection he had received from it against his own countrymen, had large part in determining his attitude on the relation of subjects to rulers.  His principles are true and applicable at all times, and agree with those laid down by Christ himself when he was asked for opinions on or to interfere in legal and political matters.  Christ always upheld the civil power by precept and example.  See  Matthew 17:24-27 Matthew 22:21 Matthew 26:52 Luke 12:14 .

title: Romans 13:3
text: For rulers are not a terror to the good work, etc.  Here the root of the difficulty is indicated with regard to obeying rulers.  The individual's moral and mental attitude toward lawful authority decides whether he shall be a free, loyal, honorable citizen or a criminal.  Does he look upon the ruler as his friend or as his enemy?  The apostle says in effect that the ruler is not only his protector and friend, but a minister of God to him for good; therefore he is to be cheerfully accepted as well as obeyed.  The Christian is to think of lawful rulers rightly so that it will be easier to obey them.

title: Romans 13:4
text: He beareth not the sword IN vain. Not content with persuading the Christians at Rome to be friendly and loyal to rulers, he warns in regard to their power of punishment, accentuating his warning by an illustration of convincing force.  The sword used in beheading a criminal was sometimes borne before a magistrate in token of his authority.

title: Romans 13:6
text: Tribute. Taxes paid by a subject people to a ruling state ( Luke 20:22 ).

title: Romans 13:7
text:
Custom. Tax on merchandise ( Matthew 17:25 ).
 

 
Fear. Strict obedience.
 

 
Honor. Respect for authority.

title: Romans 13:8
text: Hath fulfilled the law. Has done all that the law commands.  See  Matthew 22:40 .

title: Romans 13:11
text:
:14
 
And this, knowing the season, etc.  The meaning is: Do this-all I have advised and warned you to do-for the time of Christ's second coming is near; there is not much time left for the works of light; let us therefore 'cast off the works of darkness.'
 

 
Salvation. Which would be complete when Christ came.
 

 
Walk becomingly. Upright conduct.  The explanation of  Romans 13:11-14  is found in the belief of early Christians that Christ's second coming was very near.

title: Romans 14:1
text: Decision of scruples. The believer whose faith was weak was to be made to feel that differences with the church authorities on minor points should not be allowed to prejudice him, provided he held the essential truths of the gospel.  In this chapter the apostle considers the doubts of some Christians in regard to food and other matters. This was necessary only because they were weak in faith, and if their scruples were not judiciously dealt with they might desert their stronger brethren.  These latter were too well established in the faith to be troubled with doubts on comparatively unimportant questions.

title: Romans 14:5
text: Assured. Sincere.

title: Romans 14:6
text: Eateth. Meat.

title: Romans 14:9
text: Lord of both the dead and the living. Master of the believer both on earth and in heaven.

title: Romans 14:10
text: Why dost thou judge thy brother? Why dost thou judge thy brother, when thou knowest that thou also shalt be judged?

title: Romans 14:15
text: Thy meat. Thy prejudice about so small a matter as the food a Christian ought to eat.

title: Romans 14:16
text: Your good. The Christian enlightenment and freedom which make you spiritually strong and useful.

title: Romans 14:17
text: The kingdom of God. The reign of Christ in the heart in this world and the world to come.

title: Romans 14:22
text:
Have thou to thyself before God. Be strictly accountable for it to God alone.
 

 
That judgeth not himself. That hath not occasion to rebuke himself for wrong indulgence.

title: Romans 15:1
text: Ought to bear the infirmities of the weak, etc.  In  Romans 14:1-15:33  the apostle considers the church at Rome as divided into the strong and the weak, placing upon the strong the responsibility of setting a good example to the weak.

title: Romans 15:2
text: Unto edifying. The upbuilding of Christian character, both in the individual and the community.  The verse implies a warning against going too far to please our neighbor even in that which is good.  The restriction is, unto the good, which edifies.

title: Romans 15:4
text: Learning. Instruction.

title: Romans 15:8
text: A minister of the circumcision. Under the old covenant, in order that he might show himself to the Jews as their promised Messiah.  See  Matthew 15:24 .

title: Romans 15:9
text: That the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy. The Gentiles were included in the promises made to Abraham by reason of his faith, and before he was circumcised.

title: Romans 15:15
text: The grace that was given me of God. Through which he became an apostle to the Gentiles (Ro1.5).

title: Romans 15:16
text: The offering up of the Gentiles. The giving themselves up as a willing sacrifice.  See  Hebrews 10:10 .

title: Romans 15:19
text: Illyricum. The Roman name of the extensive province lying along the east coast of the Adriatic Sea, north of Macedonia and west of Thrace.  It thus contained all or parts of modern Croatia, Dalmatia, Bosnia, Albania, and Montenegro.  There is no mention of this province in Acts, and it is probable that the apostle means 'unto the borders of Illyricum.'  See  Acts 20:1 Acts 20:2 .

title: Romans 15:20
text: Upon another man's foundation. See  II Corinthians 10:12-16 .

title: Romans 15:21
text: To whom no tidings of him came, etc.  These words were spoken of the suffering Servant of Jehovah.  Paul quotes them as expressing a motive and a purpose similar to those which actuated him in preaching the gospel where it had never been heard before.

title: Romans 15:22
text: From coming to you. Paul had long intended to visit Rome ( Acts 19:21 ).

title: Romans 15:23
text: These regions. That part of the Roman empire in Europe which was east of the Adriatic Sea.

title: Romans 15:24
text: Whensoever I go unto Spain Some scholars think that this journey was accomplished.

title: Romans 15:25
text: Ministering unto the saints. That is, presenting to the church at Jerusalem the contribution from Gentile churches.

title: Romans 15:26
text:
Macedonia. See note on  Acts 16:9 .
 

 
Achaia. The name of Greece as a Roman province after its conquest.

title: Romans 15:27
text: Carnal things. Meaning here the bodily necessities for which contributions were sent ( Romans 15:25 ).

title: Romans 15:28
text: And have sealed to them this fruit. And have publicly borne witness that the contributions brought to Jerusalem have become the property of the receivers.

title: Romans 15:31
text: Them that are disobedient. The Judaizers within the church.  They had opposed Paul from the beginning of his apostleship, maintaining that Gentiles were not to be accepted as Christians unless they were circumcised.  They also disapproved of Paul's devotion to the Gentiles, striving unceasingly to restrict his work and influence to the furtherance of Judaism.

title: Romans 16:1
text: Cenchreae. The eastern part of Corinth.  See note on  Acts 18:1 .

title: Romans 16:3
text: Prisca and Aquila. See  Acts 18:2 Acts 18:18 Acts 18:26 .  Paul first knew them at Corinth, and went with them a year and a half later to Ephesus, where they helped to correct certain errors in the beliefs of Apollos.  When Paul wrote this epistle they were in Rome.  They were last known to be in Ephesus ( II Timothy 4:19 ).

title: Romans 16:5
text:
Epaenetus. Not mentioned elsewhere in the New Testament.
 

 
Asia. The Roman province of that name.  See notes on  Acts 6:8-15 Acts 19:10 .

title: Romans 16:6
text: Mary. Probably a Gentile convert.

title: Romans 16:7
text: Andronicus and Junias. The first is a Greek name, the second it Latin; but both men were Jews.  It was the custom of Jews who traveled or engaged in commerce to assume Latin or Greek names.  These two probably belonged, as did Paul, to the tribe of Benjamin, but there is no evidence that they were closely related to Paul.  The only relative mentioned is his nephew ( Acts 23:16 ).

title: Romans 16:8
text:
:10
 
Ampliatus . . . Urbanus. Latin names.
 

 
Stachys . . . Apelles . . . Aristobulus. Greek names.

title: Romans 16:11
text:
Herodion, my kinsman. A Greek name.  See note on  Romans 16:7 .
 

 
Narcissus. Supposed to be a well-known Roman freedman.

title: Romans 16:12
text: Tryphaena and Tryphosa. Probably two sisters.  Their names are Greek, as is also that of Persis.

title: Romans 16:13
text:
Rufus. A Latin name.  This Rufus may have been the same as he who is mentioned in  Mark 15:21 .
 

 
The chosen in the Lord. He who by his faith and example is honored for his work in the Lord.

title: Romans 16:14
text: Asyncritus, etc.  The names are all Greek.

title: Romans 16:15
text: Philologus, etc.  All the names are Greek, except 'Julia' a Latin name.  Julia was probably either the wife or sister of Philologus (lover of wisdom).

title: Romans 16:17
text: Them that are causing the divisions, etc.  The Judaizing teachers within the church ( Romans 15:31 ).  Some scholars think that other forms of error were meant.

title: Romans 16:18
text: Their own belly. Their objectionable religious notions and schemes.  See  Philippians 3:17-20 Colossians 2:20-23 .

title: Romans 16:19
text:
Your obedience is come abroad, etc.  Your loyalty to Christian truth is everywhere known.
 

 
Simple unto that which is evil. Uncontaminated by evil, though knowing its danger.

title: Romans 16:20
text:
The God of peace. Invoked by the apostle with reference to the strife and divisions of which he had just spoken.
 

 
Shall bruise Satan. Shall enable you to triumph over him.
 

 
Shortly. In view of the expected Second Coming of Christ ( Romans 13:11 Romans 13:12 ).

title: Romans 16:21
text:
Timothy. See note on  Acts 16:1 .
 

 
Lucius. Possibly the same as Lucius of Cyrene, in North Africa.  See  Acts 13:1 .
 

 
Jason. Possibly the Jason mentioned in  Acts 17:5-7 Acts 17:9 .
 

 
Sosipater. Possibly Sopater the Beroean ( Acts 20:4 ).
 

 
My kinsman. See note on  Romans 16:7 .

title: Romans 16:22
text: Tertius. Paul's amanuensis, who wrote the apostle's letters from dictation.  His sudden interruption here in order to add his own name to those who wished to salute his Christian brethren in Rome is dramatic.

title: Romans 16:23
text:
Gaius. The same name as the Latin Caius.  It is not certain that he was the same as the Caius referred to in  Acts 19:29 ; or as the Gaius of Derbe ( Acts 20:4 ); or of  III John 1:1 .
 

 
Erastus. A Greek name.
 

 
City. Corinth.
 

 
Quartus. A Latin name.

title: Romans 16:25
text:
To establish you. Make firm and steadfast.
 

 
My gospel. Paul's teaching of the salvation by faith for Jew and Gentile.
 

 
The preaching of Jesus Christ. The preaching done in the name of Jesus Christ by Paul and the other apostles.
 

 
The revelation of the mystery. The making known of the secret purpose of God was followed by the proclamation of the gospel.

title: Romans 16:26
text: Unto obedience of faith. The humble submission which faith implies.

title: I Corinthians 1:1
text:
Called to be an apostle. An apostle by divine calling.  'Called' has the same sense in  I Corinthians 2:16 .  Paul was not one of the twelve, called by Jesus at the opening of his ministry ( Matthew 10:1-4 ); hence his title to the apostleship could not rest upon an original divine call, such as had been given the other apostles.
 

 
Sosthenes. Supposed by some, but without sufficient evidence, to be the chief ruler of the synagogue mentioned in  Acts 28:17 , with the assumption that he was afterwards converted.  He must have been a person of much consideration to be joined with Paul in the salutation.

title: I Corinthians 1:2
text:
The church of God which is at Corinth. See 'Corinth and its church' in the introduction to the first epistle to the Corinthians.
 

 
Sanctified. Made holy. 'Sanctified' is here applied to all true believers in the church; sanctification was the object for which they were called, and was then begun, even if not completed in them.
 

 
Called. See note on  I Corinthians 1:1 
 

 
Saints. 'Saints' in the New Testament denotes not persons of rare and exceptional piety, but all true believers; holiness of life was the purpose of their divine calling in Christ.
 

 
With all that call, etc.  That is, directly invoke Jesus Christ in prayer as the exalted Redeemer ( Acts 7:59 ).
 

 
In every place. The apostolic epistles were passed from church to church ( Colossians 4:16 ).  In Corinth, a great commercial center, there were likely to be believers from many parts of the civilized world, who would thus be included in the greeting.

title: I Corinthians 1:5
text: That in everything ye were enriched. The members of the Corinthian church had begun the Christian life with an abundant supply of spiritual blessings.

title: I Corinthians 1:6
text:
,8
 
Confirmed. The meaning of 'confirmed' and confirm' in these two verses is 'made firm, stable, steadfast.'

title: I Corinthians 1:9
text: God is faithful. To comfort and sustain believers.

title: I Corinthians 1:10
text: Divisions. Into parties, resulting in contentions such as those indicated in  I Corinthians 1:11 I Corinthians 1:12 .

title: I Corinthians 1:11
text: Chloe. Not elsewhere noticed, but so well known to the Corinthians that it was sufficient to mention her name without description.

title: I Corinthians 1:12
text:
Apollos. See  Acts 18:24-28 .  At the writing of this epistle Apollos was with or near Paul, and it is evident that there was perfect harmony between them, from Paul's words, 'as touching Apollos the brother, I besought him much to come unto you with the brethren.'  But the apostle adds, 'it was not at all his will to come now' ( I Corinthians 16:12 ).  It seems clear that Apollos had been made by his admirers, against his own will, the leader of a party against Paul, and on discovering this had taken the surest way to quench the rivalry by absenting himself from the church and joining the apostle.  There is no evidence that he ever revisited Corinth.  There is cordial mention of Apollos in  Titus 3:13 .
 

 
Cephas. Peter, who was the nominal head of the party with Judaizing tendencies ( Galatians 2:11 Galatians 2:14 ).  It is not probable that Peter himself had anything to do with the contest in Corinth.
 

 
Of Christ. Those who called themselves 'of Christ' were doubtless some who had attended the ministry of Jesus or who had been directly instructed by some of his immediate followers.

title: I Corinthians 1:14
text:
Crispus. The converted ruler of the synagogue at Corinth ( Acts 18:8 ).
 

 
Gaius. Doubtless the same person mentioned in  Romans 16:23 .  Others of the name are mentioned ( Acts 19:29 Acts 20:4 III John 1:1 ).

title: I Corinthians 1:16
text:
The household of Stephanas. Stephanas was the first Corinthian convert under Paul's ministry ( I Corinthians 16:15 ), and was with the apostle at the time ( I Corinthians 16:17 ).  Of whom his household consisted we are not informed, but we learn from  I Corinthians 16:15  that they have set themselves to minister to the saints.
 

 
I know not, etc.  The apostle declares himself not sure whether the list, evidently supplied from memory, is complete.

title: I Corinthians 1:17
text:
Not to baptize, etc.  Baptism could be performed by any qualified administrator, but preaching was Paul's special work.  ( Acts 9:15 Acts 22:15 Acts 22:16 Acts 26:16 )
 

 
Lest the cross, etc. Lest human systems, logic, or eloquence should lead the minds of men away from the simplicity of the gospel message.  This thought is the key to all the verses that follow in this chapter.

title: I Corinthians 1:19
text: For it is written, etc.  The quotation is taken freely from the Septuagint, the Greek version of the Old Testament.  See note on  Acts 6:5 Acts 6:6 .

title: I Corinthians 1:20
text: Where is the wise, etc.  Where, as regards the redemption of man?

title: I Corinthians 1:21
text:
In the wisdom of God. By his providence.
 

 
Knew not God. Whatever the world's wisdom in ante-Christian days had attained, it had not known God in his spirituality, purity, and love as revealed in Christ.

title: I Corinthians 1:25
text:
The foolishness of God. The divine teaching which the world deems foolish.
 

 
 The weakness of God. The divine method which the world deems weak, as not employing arms, political power, or learned research.  The highest example: a Savior 'crucified through weakness' ( II Corinthians 13:4 ).

title: I Corinthians 2:1
text: And I, brethren, etc.  Paul's action was in accordance with this view of the divine simplicity of the Gospel.

title: I Corinthians 2:2
