text: Paradise. The word is used to signify the heavenly abode of departed spirits.  See  Luke 23:43 Revelation of John 2:7 .

title: II Corinthians 12:6
text: For I shall speak the truth. The inference is that Paul's accuser was not careful to restrict his boasting to simple fact.

title: II Corinthians 12:7
text: A thorn in the flesh. There have been many conjectures as to the nature of this affliction.  Paul's reference to it suggests that it was a source of constant humiliation, lest he be consumed with pride.

title: II Corinthians 12:9
text: My grace is sufficient for thee. From this it would seem that the desired healing was denied to Paul, and that it was shown him that the grace of God manifest in him was wholly sufficient to overbalance any physical deficiency.

title: II Corinthians 12:10
text: For when I am weak, then am I strong. His weakness led him the more quickly and earnestly to seek the power of Christ.

title: II Corinthians 12:11
text: Though I am nothing. All glory belongs to Christ.  See  I Corinthians 2:2 Philippians 3:9 .

title: II Corinthians 12:12
text: By signs and wonders.  See note on  II Corinthians 12:6 .

title: II Corinthians 12:14
text: But the parents for the children. Paul stood in the place of father to the church in Corinth ( II Corinthians 11:2 ).  This relation ought to be a sufficient answer to his critics.  See  II Corinthians 12:13 II Corinthians 11:7 .

title: II Corinthians 12:18
text: Did Titus take any advantage of you? Whether a similar charge had been made against Titus or not, Paul answers it.

title: II Corinthians 12:21
text: Should humble me before you. Through the relapsing into sinful ways, without repentance, of some of Paul's converts.  This was also doubtless intended as a rebuke and warning to those who had thus fallen away.

title: II Corinthians 13:4
text: For he was crucified through weakness. Jesus was crucified in the weakness of his 'likeness of men' ( Philippians 2:7 Philippians 2:8 ), 'being put to death in the flesh' ( I Peter 3:18 ).  See  Romans 8:3 .

title: II Corinthians 13:7
text: Though we be as reprobate. Paul's desire for the Corinthians is that their attainment shall be so exalted that his own shall seem reprobate in comparison.  A similar meaning is apparent in  II Corinthians 13:9 .

title: II Corinthians 13:10
text: Not for casting down. Paul's ardent desire to forestall any need for rebuke marks his great wisdom in developing the church along the lines of love, with no display of that authority which was a prominent feature of the government of the Jewish people under the law, and which the Judaizers continued to exert.

title: Galatians 1:1
text:
An apostle not from men, neither through man, but through Jesus Christ.  Paul did not receive his appointment from any man or any body of men, but was called on his way to Damascus by Jesus Christ and chosen by God himself ( Galatians 1:15 ).  Paul enlarges upon his election from  Galatians 1:12-24 Galatians 2:1-18 .
 

 
 Raised from the dead. It was the risen Lord, to whom all authority had been given, who had called Paul- a sufficient seal of his apostleship.

title: Galatians 1:2
text: Churches. Local congregations in Galatia.

title: Galatians 1:4
text:
Gave himself for our sins. The whole epistle conveys Paul's contention that the law can define and forbid sin, but cannot cure it.  We are justified by faith in Christ, not by the law.
 

 
 This present evil world. The time of temptation and sin prior to the reign of Christ in the heart.

title: Galatians 1:6
text:
I marvel that ye are so quickly removing. Paul's rebuke at the very outset of the epistle indicates the grave danger into which the Galatians had so readily fallen.
 

 
 From him that called you. From God ( Romans 1:28 ).

title: Galatians 1:7
text: Not another gospel. The gospel preached by Paul offered men redemption from the law.  Judaizers were trying to graft the gospel on the law.

title: Galatians 1:8
text: Anathema. Accursed.

title: Galatians 1:10
text: Am I now seeking favor of men? Paul's introductory rebuke is a sufficient guaranty of his freedom from all self-seeking.

title: Galatians 1:12
text: Persecuted the church of God. See  Acts 8:3 Acts 9:1 .

title: Galatians 1:14
text:
More exceedingly zealous. See  Philippians 3:4-6 .
 

 
 Traditions of my fathers. Religious precepts were handed down from father to son, often orally.  Jesus spoke of the Pharisees as making void the law by their traditions, which they had added to the law until it had become a burden grievous to be borne ( Matthew 23:4 ).

title: Galatians 1:15
text: Separated me, even from my mother's womb. Consecrated even before birth.  Compare  Isaiah 49:1 Luke 1:15 .

title: Galatians 1:16
text:
Reveal his Son in me. The knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ ( II Corinthians 4:6 ).
 

 
 Among the Gentiles. Paul, being born a Roman as well as a Jew, seems to have had a broader outlook.  See  Galatians 2:7-9 .
 

 
 Conferred not with flesh and blood. Paul did not ask instruction of the disciples at Damascus, nor even of the apostles at Jerusalem, but went into seclusion to be taught of God.  See  Matthew 16:17 .  However, from  Acts 9:20 , it is evident that immediately upon his conversion he proclaimed his faith publicly.

title: Galatians 1:17
text: Up to Jerusalem. The word 'up' may refer to the elevation of Jerusalem, 2,593 feet above the sea.  The direction from Damascus to Jerusalem was southwesterly.

title: Galatians 1:18
text:
After three years.  This was about A.D. 40.  It was not until then that Paul had met any of the apostles and compared his revelation of Jesus Christ with them.
 

 
 Cephas. was Peter ( John 1:42 ).

title: Galatians 1:21
text: Syria and Cilicia. These were adjoining countries.  Antioch was the capital of Syria, and Tarsus, of Cilicia, was Paul's birthplace.

title: Galatians 2:1
text: After fourteen years. Commentators differ as to whether this period should be counted from Paul's conversion or from his previous visit.  At all events the occasion seems to be, beyond dispute, the council of the apostles and elders recorded in  Acts 15:4 .

title: Galatians 2:2
text:
By revelation. Compare  Acts 16:6 Acts 16:7 Acts 19:21 Acts 20:22 Acts 20:23 Acts 22:17 Acts 22:18 .
 

 
 Laid before them the gospel which I preach. Paul may have thought his teaching might be condemned by the apostles, as it had been by men from Judea ( Acts 15:1 ).  In this private conference, however, with those who were of repute, probably James, Peter and John ( Galatians 2:9 ), Paul was upheld.

title: Galatians 2:3
text: Not even Titus who was with me, etc.  The contention of the Judaizers was that the Gentile Christians must be circumcised to partake of the gospel.  Paul's argument, doubtless in the line of  I Corinthians 7:19  and  Galatians 5:6 , prevailed.

title: Galatians 2:6
text: Imparted nothing to me. The revelation to Paul had been so complete and had been received with such faith and intelligence that even the apostles who had been personally in the company of Jesus could add nothing to his understanding of the gospel.

title: Galatians 2:7
text:
When they saw that I had been intrusted. As the Lord said unto Ananias ( Acts 9:15 ), Paul was 'a chosen vessel' to bear His name 'before the Gentiles.'
 

 
 Gospel of the circumcision.  The gospel of those of the circumcision, the Jews; in the words of Peter 'to the elect who are sojourners of the Dispersion' ( I Peter 1:1 ).

title: Galatians 2:9
text:
James and Cephas and John. This James was the brother of the Lord, who had taken the place of James the son of Zebedee, slain by Herod ( Acts 12:2 ).  Cephas was Peter ( John 1:42 ).  John was the beloved apostle, the son of Zebedee ( Matthew 4:21 Matthew 10:2 ).
 

 
 The right hands of fellowship. A token of agreement in the faith, and of unity of feeling and purpose.

title: Galatians 2:10
text: Remember the poor. These were evidently the poor among the Jews at Jerusalem.  That the Gentiles, under Paul, did make such contributions is evident from  Romans 15:26 Romans 15:27 .

title: Galatians 2:11
text:
When Cephas came to Antioch.  This is believed to have been previous to the visit of Paul to Jerusalem recounted in the preceding verses.
 

 
 He stood condemned.   Peter had been taught not to make a distinction between Jews and Gentiles.  See  Acts 10:11-15 Acts 10:26-29 ; also  Galatians 2:12 .

title: Galatians 2:12
text: Ate with the Gentiles. The Jews were restricted to certain foods ( Deuteronomy 14:3-21 ).  The Gentiles were not under this law.

title: Galatians 2:13
text: Even Barnabas was carried away.  Barnabas, although the appointed assistant to Paul in the preaching of the gospel to the Gentiles ( Acts 11:22 ), was a Jew, and a Levite ( Acts 4:36 ).  He was the cousin of Mark the evangelist.

title: Galatians 2:14
text: Before them all. Paul felt that the unity of the church was imperiled by Peter's movement toward retaining the old line of separation between Jew and Gentile, and he made his remonstrance publicly.  Paul's rebuke of Peter seems to end with  Galatians 2:14 .  The remainder of the chapter is a plea to the dissembling Jews.

title: Galatians 2:18
text: Those things which I destroyed. After preaching that justification was not by the law, but through faith, Paul argues that he cannot now claim justification through the observance of Jewish customs which were a part of the law.

title: Galatians 2:19
text: For I through the law died unto the law. The law was 'our tutor' to bring us to Christ ( Galatians 3:24 ).  When the law, his tutor, had brought Paul to Christ, he was no longer under the tutor, but had outgrown the necessity for him.

title: Galatians 2:20
text: Crucified with Christ. See  Galatians 5:24 ; also  Romans 6:6 .

title: Galatians 2:21
text: Died for nought. Paul's argument is that Christ died to redeem men from the law and its curse upon the lawbreaker. But if righteousness was still a matter of justification under the law, the death of Christ had been of no avail.

title: Galatians 3:3
text: Having begun in the Spirit, are ye now perfected in the flesh? The Galatians were not turning away from Christianity, but seeking to perfect themselves therein by observing the Jewish laws and customs.  Compare  II Corinthians 3:6 .

title: Galatians 3:5
text: Worketh miracles among you. See  I Corinthians 12:10 Hebrews 2:4 .

title: Galatians 3:6
text: Abraham believed God. Salvation through faith is the teaching of the Old testament as well as of the New.  But the faith required then, as now, is one of the vital kind which is perfected in obedience and expressed in works. See  James 2:21-23 .

title: Galatians 3:7
text: Sons of Abraham. In the spiritual sense those who receive the faith are Abraham's sons, whether Jews or Gentiles.

title: Galatians 3:8
text: In thee shall all the nations be blessed. See  Genesis 12:3 .  Jesus Christ, of the seed of Abraham, brought salvation not only to the Jews, but to the whole world.

title: Galatians 3:10
text: Cursed is every one who continueth not, etc.  This is the concluding paragraph of the condemnation under the law pronounced by the Levites from Mount Ebal ( Deuteronomy 27:26 ). The law demanded entire obedience.  He who violated one commandment was guilty of all ( James 2:10 ).  Since no man is perfect, he who abides under the law and does not keep all, abides under the curse.  Justification is by faith through obedience.

title: Galatians 3:12
text: Shall live in them. 'In them' in the sense of 'by means of them.'

title: Galatians 3:13
text: Having become a curse for us. Jesus came under the law and in his death paid the penalty of the law.  Like the symbolic scape-goat ( Leviticus 16:5-26 ), he was the representative of the sin and the curse which it entailed.

title: Galatians 3:14
text: Receive the promise of the Spirit through faith. Faith is the only channel through which the promised gift of the Spirit can be received.

title: Galatians 3:16
text: To Abraham were the promises spoken. See  Genesis 12:1-3 Genesis 17:2-8 .

title: Galatians 3:17
text: Confirmed beforehand by God. 'He is faithful that promised' ( Hebrews 10:23 ).

title: Galatians 3:18
text: For if the inheritance is of the law. An inheritance founded on the law would fail through failure to keep the law.  It is saved by faith in the promises and in Christ as the fulfilment of the promises.

title: Galatians 3:19
text:
What then is the law?  It was added because of transgressions. 'The law made nothing perfect' ( Hebrews 7:19 ), but is a guide leading unto Christ ( Galatians 3:24 ), who 'having been made perfect, he became unto all them that obey him the author of eternal salvation' ( Hebrews 5:9 ).
 

 
 Till the seed should come. The iniquities of the unrighteous extended to the third and fourth generations ( Exodus 20:5 ).
 

 
 Ordained through angels. See  Acts 7:53 Hebrews 2:2 .

title: Galatians 3:20
text: A mediator is not a mediator of one. The offices of a mediator are needed only when the parties are divided. There was no mediator between God and Abraham; there is no mediator between Christ and the believer.

title: Galatians 3:21
text: Is the law then against the promises? The law of Moses ended in the higher law of the gospel.  For Christ became 'the mediator of a better covenant' ( Hebrews 8:6 ).  See also  Hebrews 8:7-13 .

title: Galatians 3:23
text: Shut up unto the faith. In bondage under the law, in the absence of the higher motive power of faith, until released by righteousness through faith.

title: Galatians 3:24
text: The law is become our tutor. See  Galatians 4:1 Galatians 4:2 .

title: Galatians 4:5
text: The adoption of sons. See  Romans 8:14-17 .

title: Galatians 4:8
text: In bondage to them that by nature are no gods. That is, the Galatians were formerly idolaters.

title: Galatians 4:9
text: Rudiments. Jewish laws and ceremonies which were but symbols of the gospel revealed in Jesus Christ, through which they were to know God as Father, and be known by Him as sons.  The turning back to exalt mere forms was idolatry.  See note of  Galatians 4:8 .

title: Galatians 4:10
text: Ye observe days, etc.  The Jews held certain days sacred to certain feasts and festivals.  See  Colossians 2:16 Colossians 2:17 .

title: Galatians 4:11
text: I am afraid of you. The expression is one of anxiety, not of fear.

title: Galatians 4:12
text: Become as I am. Although a Hebrew of the Hebrews ( Philippians 3:5 ), Paul knew that in Christ he was free of the old Jewish law.  His remonstrance is the more pointed to the Galatians who had never been under the law.

title: Galatians 4:13
text:
An infirmity of the flesh. This is understood to refer to an illness of Paul's, which was a temptation ( Galatians 4:14 ) to the Galatians to despise him who had wrought miracles of healing upon others, yet seemed unable to heal himself ( Acts 14:8-10 ).
 

 
 Received me as an angel.  Compare  Acts 14:11-13 .

title: Galatians 4:17
text: They desire to shut you out. The Judaizers, by insisting upon conformity to Jewish rites and observances, aimed to shut out the whole body of Gentile believers.

title: Galatians 4:19
text:
My little children.  This expression is one used often by John.  Paul's use of it here expresses unusual tenderness.
 

 
 In travail. In agonizing anxiety.
 

 
 Formed in you. 'Transformed by the renewing of your mind' ( Romans 12:2 ).

title: Galatians 4:22
text: Abraham had two sons. Ishmael, see  Genesis 16:15 ; and Isaac, see  Genesis 21:2 Genesis 21:3 .

title: Galatians 4:23
text: Born through promise.  Genesis 17:16 Genesis 17:19 Genesis 17:21 .

title: Galatians 4:24
text: Mount Sinai.  The covenant of Mount Sinai was the covenant of the law.  See  Exodus 34:2 Exodus 34:28 .

title: Galatians 4:25
text: Jerusalem that now is. The city then in Palestine.

title: Galatians 4:26
text: The Jerusalem that is above. 'The city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem' ( Hebrews 12:22 ).

title: Galatians 4:27
text:
Thou barren. Sarah, who became the mother of Isaac, the child of promise.
 

 
 More are the children. They include all nations.  In the allegory the son of the bondwoman represents the bondage of the law; the son of the freewoman the freedom which comes by faith.  See  John 8:32-36 Romans 8:2 .

title: Galatians 4:29
text: But as then he that was born after the flesh. See  Genesis 21:9 .

title: Galatians 4:30
text: Shall not inherit. The children of the flesh, and thereby under bondage of the law, shall not inherit with the children of the gospel, free of the law by righteousness through faith.

title: Galatians 5:1
text: For freedom did Christ set us free. See  John 8:36 .

title: Galatians 5:2
text: Christ will profit you nothing. The receiving of the outward rite of circumcision is virtually a denial of the complete sufficiency of the truth as it is in Christ.

title: Galatians 5:3
text: Debtor to do the whole law. There is no middle ground. If one provision of the law (circumcision) is necessary to salvation, the whole law must be necessary.

title: Galatians 5:4
text: Severed from Christ. Through denial of the gospel. 'For Christ is the end of the law' ( Romans 10:4 ).

title: Galatians 5:8
text: This persuasion. To assume the bondage of the law by making it of equal importance with the revelation of Jesus Christ.

title: Galatians 5:9
text: A little leaven. If circumcision were accepted the whole burden of bondage to the law would be developed.

title: Galatians 5:10
text: None otherwise minded. Compare  Philippians 2:5 Philippians 3:15 .

title: Galatians 5:11
text:
If I still preach circumcision. This refers to the fact that Paul advised the circumcision of Timothy ( Acts 16:3 ), as his mother was a Jewess.  Paul had also observed other Jewish customs ( Acts 21:21-26 ).
 

 
 Stumblingblock of the cross. The great discord was in the superseding of the discipline of the Mosaic law, with its minute and hallowed observances, by faith in the teachings of One who had died the shameful death of the cross.

title: Galatians 5:13
text: Use not your freedom for an occasion to the flesh. See  Romans 6:12-15 .

title: Galatians 5:14
text: The whole law is fulfilled in one word. Paul is writing of the law as to the brethren.  The same end was attained by faith in Christ as under the law (Le 19.18), but under faith the regeneration was from within, through love ( Galatians 5:13 ).

title: Galatians 5:16
text: Walk by the Spirit. See  Romans 8:9 .

title: Galatians 5:17
text: For the flesh lusteth against the Spirit.  See  Romans 7:14-23 .

title: Galatians 5:18
text: Not under the law. The observance of the law was an outward obedience through fear.  The true fulfilment of the law was in love ( Romans 13:10 ), through the influence of the indwelling Spirit.

title: Galatians 5:24
text: Have crucified the flesh. See  Galatians 2:20 Romans 6:6 .

title: Galatians 5:26
text: Let us not become vainglorious. Even Jesus said, 'The Son can do nothing of himself' ( John 5:19 ). See  Philippians 2:13 .

title: Galatians 6:1
text: Spirit of gentleness. Not with condemnation, but with meekness, as of one also subject to temptation.  See  Romans 7:19 .

title: Galatians 6:2
text: Bear ye one another's burdens. See  Romans 15:1 .

title: Galatians 6:3
text: Thinketh himself to be something. See  I Corinthians 9:16 Romans 7:24 .

title: Galatians 6:8
text:
Soweth unto his own flesh. Compare  Matthew 6:19 .
 

 
 Soweth unto the Spirit. Compare  Matthew 6:33 .

title: Galatians 6:10
text: Especially toward them that are of the household of faith. Fellowship in Christ calls for special love and tenderness.  Compare  I Peter 1:22 .

title: Galatians 6:11
text: With mine own hand. The letters of Paul were usually written by a scribe, only the closing sentences being in Paul's own hand.  Compare  Romans 16:22 I Corinthians 16:21 Colossians 4:18 II Thessalonians 3:17 .

title: Galatians 6:13
text:
For not even they. See  Galatians 6:15 .
 

 
 Glory in your flesh. In the outward appearance.

title: Galatians 6:15
text: A new creature. Compare  John 3:3-6 I Peter 1:23 .

title: Galatians 6:17
text: Branded on my body. Paul here compares the scars of martyrdom for his faith with the empty rite of circumcision.  See  II Corinthians 11:23-25 .

title: Ephesians 1:1
text:
Through the will of God. See  Acts 9:15 .
 

 
 The faithful in Christ Jesus. Paul's thought while addressed to the Ephesians in particular was toward the entire body of the faithful in Christ.

title: Ephesians 1:3
text: In the heavenly places. In the spiritual realm.

title: Ephesians 1:4
text:
He chose us in him. This refers not to the Jews as the 'chosen people,' but to the 'Israel of God' ( Galatians 6:16 ).  Compare  Romans 4:11 Romans 4:12 .
 

 
 Before the foundation of the world. As the spiritual world was before the physical world, so was God's divine plan as to man before the physical man.

title: Ephesians 1:5
text: Unto adoption as sons. Adoption is in itself a choosing into a new relation.  Compare  Galatians 4:7 .  Also  Romans 8:15 Romans 9:4 .

title: Ephesians 1:6
text: The beloved. Compare  Matthew 3:17 .

title: Ephesians 1:7
text: Through his blood. The blood signifies the life.  But the redemptive work of Jesus preceded ( Ephesians 1:4 ) and follows ( Ephesians 2:7 ) his human life.

title: Ephesians 1:9
text:
Mystery of his will. God's will could not be understood until revealed in Christ.  See  Ephesians 3:3 Ephesians 3:4 Ephesians 3:9 Ephesians 6:19 .
 

 
 His good pleasure which he purposed in him. This refers to the divine purpose concerning salvation through Christ Jesus.  See  Ephesians 5:11 Ephesians 3:11 .

title: Ephesians 1:10
text: The fulness of the times. Through the development of the ages the world was ready for the revelation.

title: Ephesians 1:11
text: In whom also we were made a heritage. Partakers of salvation through Christ by the grace of God.

title: Ephesians 1:13
text: Sealed with the Holy Spirit. The indwelling of the Holy Spirit was the seal or pledge of adoption.  'The Spirit himself beareth witness with our spirit that we are children of God' ( Romans 8:16 ).  See also  Ephesians 4:30 II Corinthians 1:22 .

title: Ephesians 1:14
text: An earnest of our inheritance. Through adoption (see note on  Ephesians 1:13 ) we become children, 'and if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ' ( Romans 8:17 ).

title: Ephesians 1:18
text: Having the eyes of your heart enlightened.  Compare  Matthew 13:13-16 .

title: Ephesians 1:23
text: Which is his body. Compare  Ephesians 5:23 Colossians 1:18 Colossians 2:19 John 15:5 .

title: Ephesians 2:1
text: Did he make alive. Jesus himself distinguished between life and mere human existence.  To be dead in trespasses and sins does not mean unconsciousness or nonexistence.  See  I Timothy 5:6 Revelation of John 3:1 .

title: Ephesians 2:2
text: Prince of the powers of the air. This is a reference to the prevailing superstition that the air was full of evil spirits.  Compare  Ephesians 6:12 John 12:31 Acts 26:18 Colossians 1:13 .

title: Ephesians 2:3
text: Even as the rest. Though not under the law of the Jews, the Gentiles were, by the nature of their worldly desires, equally under condemnation.

title: Ephesians 2:8
text: By grace have ye been saved. See  Romans 11:5-7 .

title: Ephesians 2:9
text: Not of works. The works are the fruitage of faith; the effect of salvation, not its cause.

title: Ephesians 2:12
text: Strangers from the covenants. The Gentiles had not even the hope of the promises which had been made to the Jews as the chosen nation.

title: Ephesians 2:14
text: Brake down the middle wall of partition. This probably is a symbolic reference to the partition in the Temple which set apart the court of the Gentiles.  Its destruction was typified in the rending of the veil of the Temple at the time of the crucifixion ( Matthew 27:51 ).

title: Ephesians 2:15
text: The enmity, even the law of commandments. It was this law which separated the Jews from the Gentiles.  The new covenant abolished the old.  See  Hebrews 8:8-13 .

title: Ephesians 2:18
text:
We both. Jews and Gentiles.
 

 
 Access in one spirit. 'The Spirit of his Son' ( Galatians 4:6 ).  Compare  Romans 8:15 .

title: Ephesians 2:20
text: The foundation. Compare  I Corinthians 3:10 I Corinthians 3:11 Matthew 16:18 Matthew 21:42 I Peter 2:6 .

title: Ephesians 2:22
text: A habitation of God. Compare  I Peter 2:5 .

title: Ephesians 3:1
text: The prisoner of Christ Jesus. Paul was made a prisoner in Jerusalem because he brought Gentiles (Greeks) into the Temple.  See  Acts 21:28 .  Compare  II Timothy 1:8 II Timothy 1:1 Philemon 1:1 Philemon 1:9 .

title: Ephesians 3:2
text: The dispensation... to youward. Paul reminds the Gentiles that he was specially chosen to their service ( Acts 9:15 ).

title: Ephesians 3:3
text: The mystery. In  Ephesians 3:6  this is explained to be the revelation that the Gentiles are fellow-heirs.  The meaning is that the promises were not to be fulfilled in the racial flesh of the Jews, but in the spiritual acceptance of the gospel in which 'neither circumcision (Jew) anything, not uncircumcision (Gentile), but a new creature' ( Galatians 6:15 ).  Compare  Romans 12:2 .

title: Ephesians 3:8
text:
Less than the least. Paul never forgot that he began his career by persecuting the Christian church. See  I Corinthians 15:9 .
 

 
 Unsearchable. Salvation was not discoverable by human agency.  A revelation was needed.

title: Ephesians 3:9
text: The mystery. See note on  Ephesians 3:3 .

title: Ephesians 3:10
text: The principalities and the powers in the heavenly places. Taken in connection with such passages as  Colossians 2:10 Colossians 2:15  2.15, the meaning is evidently the powers and influences of the human mind before it has been regenerated by the grace of Christ Jesus.  See note  Ephesians 1:3 .  See also  Ephesians 6:12 Colossians 1:16 .

title: Ephesians 3:13
text: That ye may not faint. The spectacle of Paul's persecutions seemed likely to frighten weak believers away from their faith.  That he stedfastly endured them was rather to their encouragement as proving his own faith unshaken.

title: Ephesians 3:14
text: I bow my knees. Kneeling in prayer was a posture peculiar to the Christians.  The Jews prayed standing ( Luke 18:11 ).  See  Luke 22:41 Acts 20:36 .

title: Ephesians 3:15
text: Every family. The structure of the human family is a symbol of the divine relation of the fatherhood of God and the sonship of man in the one family where all are joint heirs with Christ ( Romans 8:1 ).  See also  Ephesians 4:4-6 .

title: Ephesians 3:16
text: The inward man. The inward man is the spiritual man-the immortal spirit-as distinguished from the outward man which decays.  See  II Corinthians 4:16 .

title: Ephesians 4:1
text:
26
 
 Be ye angry, and sin not. The anger which is not sinful is that directed against sin, even in one's self; not against sinners, toward whom the Christly attitude is compassion.  See  Hebrews 5:2 .

title: Ephesians 4:7
text: According to the measure of the gift of Christ. The gift of Christ was equal to all.  Its acceptance was unequal, and its manifestation differed accordingly.  See  Ephesians 4:11 ; also  I Corinthians 12:4-11 .

title: Ephesians 4:9
text: What is it but that he also descended? Paul's argument is that he who ascended must first have descended.  In talking with Nicodemus Jesus declared, 'No one hath ascended into heaven but he that descended out of heaven' ( John 3:13 ).  See  Romans 10:6 Romans 10:7 .

title: Ephesians 4:13
text: Unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ. Paul sets the standard at the summit, as did Jesus in the Sermon on the Mount: -'Ye therefore shall be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect ( Matthew 5:48 ).  See  John 1:16 .

title: Ephesians 4:14
text: By the sleight of men, in craftiness. The meaning here is beyond that of simple false teaching.  The deceit was intentional.  See  Galatians 1:7 Romans 16:17 Romans 16:18 .

title: Ephesians 4:17
text: In the vanity of their mind. Vanity that is-'nothingness'-as in  Ecclesiastes 1:2 ; not the self-conceit of the Pharisees.  See  Romans 1:21 .

title: Ephesians 4:18
text: Darkened in their understanding. Unable even to grasp the truth.  In the words of Jesus: 'He that walketh in the darkness knoweth not whither he goeth' ( John 12:35 ).

title: Ephesians 4:19
text: Being past feeling. 'Lost to the accusations of conscience.' This condition is explained in  Romans 1:28 : -'Even as they refused to have God in their knowledge, God gave them up unto a reprobate mind.' See  I Timothy 5:6 .

title: Ephesians 4:22
text: The lusts of deceit. The enticements of earthly pleasures and desires which lead only to ruin.  See  II Peter 2:18 II Peter 2:19 Romans 1:29 Hebrews 3:13 .

title: Ephesians 4:29
text: Corrupt speech. It is by speech that good or evil thought becomes active.  James calls the tongue, 'the world of iniquity among our members... full of deadly poison' ( James 3:6 James 3:8 ).  The warning of Paul is not to give utterance too a corrupting thought.  See  Matthew 12:34 Matthew 12:36 Matthew 15:18 Matthew 15:19 .

title: Ephesians 4:30
text: Sealed unto the day of redemption. Circumcision is spoken of as the seal of Abraham's faith ( Romans 4:11 ).  The seal of redemption was the indwelling of the Holy Spirit, but salvation was to be worked out ( Philippians 2:12 ), unto the day of complete redemption.

title: Ephesians 5:2
text: An offering and a sacrifice. This reference to the ceremonial sacrifices of the ancient Jews has been variously construed as a sacrifice of consecration ( Exodus 29:1-46 ), a peace-offering, ( Leviticus 3:1-17 ) and a sin-offering ( Leviticus 4:1-35 ).

title: Ephesians 5:5
text: Who is an idolater. The term idolatry is frequently used by Paul to denote devoted pursuit of earthly things, or even bondage to them;- 'that by nature are no gods' ( Galatians 4:8 ).  In the first sense he uses the expression 'whose god is the belly' ( Philippians 3:19 ).  See also  I Corinthians 10:18-20 .

title: Ephesians 5:13
text: When they are reproved. Reproof brings a fault into the light; that is, it is seen to be a fault, and clamors for correction.

title: Ephesians 5:14
text: Arise from the dead. 'Passed out of death into life' is frequently used to express the change wrought by acceptance of Christ.  In the same sense Paul exhorts in his letter to Timothy 'Lay hold on the life eternal' ( I Timothy 6:12 ).  See  John 5:24 Colossians 2:13 I John 3:14 .

title: Ephesians 5:21
text:
Subjecting yourselves one to another. Not all grace and wisdom were given to one ( I Corinthians 12:8-10 ).  That all may 'attain unto the unity of the faith' ( Ephesians 4:13 ).  Paul counsels lowliness and meekness ( Ephesians 4:2 ) toward one another.
 

 
 In the fear of Christ. In anxiety to know all: fear lest any truth be lost.

title: Ephesians 5:25
text: Even as Christ also loved the church. In this and the preceding verses the true relation of husband and wife is compared to that of Christ and the church.  The importance of this view leads Paul to repeat it in several different ways.  See  Ephesians 5:32 .

title: Ephesians 5:26
text: The washing of water with the word. The phrase refers to the baptism of water, itself symbolical of the cleansing baptism of the Holy Spirit ( Acts 1:5 ), unto sanctification.  See  Acts 22:16 .

title: Ephesians 6:4
text: The chastening and admonition of the Lord. Admonition refers to the warnings as to those things which are not to be done ( I Corinthians 10:11 Titus 3:10 ): chastening, to the inward  training toward holiness ( Hebrews 12:10 ).

title: Ephesians 6:5
text:
That according to the flesh are your masters. The coming of the kingdom of Christ did not work a revolution in the outward world, but it implanted the spirit of the brotherhood of man in which slavery could no more exist, and made the masters servants in Christ to their own slaves.
 

 
 With fear and trembling...as unto Christ. Whole-hearted and conscientious service sums up and embodies all the Christian graces.

title: Ephesians 6:8
text: The same shall he receive again from the Lord. This is in effect a paraphrase of the declaration of Jesus, 'with what measure ye mete it shall be measured unto you again' ( Matthew 7:2 ).

title: Ephesians 6:12
text: Not against flesh and blood. The enemy is an invisible one, the powers of evil to be met in one's own being.  See  Romans 7:21-23 .

title: Ephesians 6:20
text: An ambassador in chains. When Paul was rescued by the soldiers at Jerusalem he was bound with two chains ( Acts 21:33 ).  Paul seems touched by the irony of the chaining of an ambassador.

title: Ephesians 6:21
text: Tychicus. The bearer of this epistle to the Ephesians was a native of Asia ( Acts 20:4 ) and probably an Ephesian.  He is mentioned also as Paul's messenger to the Colossians ( Colossians 4:7 ),.  See  II Timothy 4:12 Titus 3:12 .

title: Philippians 1:1
text:
Paul and Timothy. The church at Philippi had been established by Paul when Timothy was with him.  See Ac 16.1, 12-15.
 

 
 The saints. Those who were 'sanctified in Christ Jesus' (1Co 1.2).
 

 
 Bishops and deacons. The increasing number of believers made organization a necessity in the churches.  See  Acts 6:2 Acts 6:3 .  The qualifications demanded of bishops and deacons are set forth in  I Timothy 3:1-10 .

title: Philippians 1:5
text: The first day. The reference is to the day of Paul's first preaching in Philippi.  See  Acts 16:13 .

title: Philippians 1:6
text:
He who began. 'It is God who worketh in you' ( Philippians 2:13 ).
 

 
 The day that the Son of man is revealed' ( Luke 17:30 ).  'When the Son of man shall come in his glory' ( Matthew 25:31 ).  See  Philippians 1:10 Philippians 2:16 I Corinthians 1:8 .

title: Philippians 1:7
text: In my bonds. Paul was at this time in chains largely because of his association with the Gentiles.  See  Philippians 1:13 Acts 21:33 .

title: Philippians 1:9
text: Discernment. The word thus translated is found in the New Testament only in this place.  Its full meaning is 'refined spiritual insight.'  See  Romans 14:1-8 .

title: Philippians 1:10
text: The things that are excellent. 'Whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honorable, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report' ( Philippians 4:8 ).

title: Philippians 1:13
text: The whole praetorian guard. This was composed of ten thousand picked soldiers who were the personal body-guard of the emperor, and was placed in a fortified camp on the northeast of Rome.  Paul made use of the publicity that came from his arrest to preach more widely the gospel of Christ.

title: Philippians 1:15
text: Even of envy and strife. Those who differed from Paul seem to have seized upon his imprisonment as evidence that he had not the true doctrine.  But their contentious served to spread the knowledge of the gospel.  See  Philippians 1:18 .  Thus God makes even the wrath of man to praise him ( Psalms 76:10 ).

title: Philippians 1:19
text: My salvation. The meaning here is release from the overwhelming influences of the flesh.

title: Philippians 1:21
text: To live is Christ, and to die is gain. Life in the flesh, to Paul, meant the intense joy of spreading the gospel: death meant release not only from  persecution, but also from the continual warfare with the flesh; and rest with Christ.

title: Philippians 1:28
text: An evident token of perdition. Persecutions and afflictions were esteemed a 'token of the righteous judgment of God' ( II Thessalonians 1:5 ).  The opposite condition was evidence of perdition.

title: Philippians 2:1
text: If there is therefore any exhortation in Christ. The intensity of Paul's plea indicates that there was serious personal strife for place among the Philippian Christians.

title: Philippians 2:3
text: Lowliness of mind. The attitude of supremacy is fatal to growth.  From the day when the mother of James and John sought places of special honor for her sons ( Matthew 20:21-24 ), Jesus himself ( Matthew 20:26 ), and the apostles counseled self-denial.

title: Philippians 2:7
text: But emptied himself. That is, he gave up everything and made himself of no reputation.

title: Philippians 2:9
text: The name which is above every name. Christ made the supreme sacrifice. Salvation had to come from above and none other was equal to the task.  It was accomplished once for all.  It cannot be done again.  The name of Christ must stand at the summit as the one and effectual Saviour of the world.

title: Philippians 2:12
text:
Work out your own salvation. Thought salvation is through Christ it must be worked out by obedience.  See  Hebrews 5:8 .
 

 
 With fear and trembling. That is, earnest anxiety.

title: Philippians 2:14
text: Without murmurings and questionings. The phrase recalls the murmurings of the children of Israel against Moses and Aaron ( Numbers 16:41 ).  Obedience cannot be half-hearted: it is then disobedience, and can result only in disaster.

title: Philippians 2:16
text: The day of Christ. See second note,  Philippians 1:6 .

title: Philippians 2:17
text: Offered upon the sacrifice. Paul's meaning is figurative, referring in humility to his service as the drink-offering which was added to the burnt-offering of sweet savor.  See  Exodus 29:40 .

title: Philippians 2:19
text: To send Timothy. See note  Philippians 1:1 .

title: Philippians 2:20
text: No man likeminded. Timothy had a peculiar and whole-souled interest in the church at Philippi, which would lead him to bring to Paul a more exhaustive report than he would get from any one else.

title: Philippians 2:21
text: for they all seek their own. Paul's workers were too closely interested each in his own particular field to give intimate attention to the spiritual condition of the Philippians.

title: Philippians 2:23
text: How it will go with me. The reference here is to the outcome of Paul's long imprisonment, and the expected trial in the near future.

title: Philippians 2:25
text: Epaphroditus. he had been the bearer of gifts to Paul from the brethren at Philippi, and upon his return, Paul sends by him this epistle to the Philippians.

title: Philippians 2:30
text: That which was lacking in your service. The most important part of the mission of Epaphroditus was not the gift he brought but the comfort and encouragement of his presence, which no gift, however costly, could supply.  See  Philippians 4:10 I Corinthians 16:17 .

title: Philippians 3:1
text: The same things. These were repetitions of his former counsels, to be kept continually in mind on the score of safety.

title: Philippians 3:2
text:
The dogs. This term applies to those of unholy tastes and desires, of whom Jesus warned the multitude in the Sermon on the Mount:-'Give not that which is holy unto the dogs' ( Matthew 7:6 ).
 

 
 The concision. The word signifies the mutilation practised by fanatics.  See  I Kings 18:28 .  It is here used by Paul in scorn for the circumcision of the flesh, as being of no greater spiritual importance.

title: Philippians 3:3
text: For we are the circumcision. The rite of circumcision signified consecration unto God, but it was merely a symbol.  The real consecration was from within.  As Paul says, in  Romans 2:29 , 'Circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit not in the letter.'  See  Romans 2:25-29 .

title: Philippians 3:7
text: What things were gain to me. In the two proceding verses Paul enumerates his superior outward qualifications as an orthodox Jew.  These things, while gain from a worldly viewpoint, he counts as 'but refuse' ( Philippians 3:8 ) compared with the knowledge of Christ, and 'the righteousness which is from God, by faith' ( Philippians 3:9 ).

title: Philippians 3:10
text: Conformed unto his death. Paul is not referring to the death on the cross, but that death unto the flesh which resulted in the resurrection.  See  Romans 6:5-11 .

title: Philippians 3:11
text: If by any means I may attain unto the resurrection from the dead.   This was the goal of Paul's hope, as it was the consummation of the human life of his lord.  See  I Corinthians 15:1-4 I Corinthians 15:12-25 .

title: Philippians 3:12
text: Not that I have already obtained. Paul was working out his own salvation with fear and trembling (see note  Philippians 2:12 ), and he permitted no self-confidence to deceive him.

title: Philippians 3:13
text: Forgetting the things which are behind. Paul had held a position of high honor and influence among the Pharisees at Jerusalem because of his learning, both in literature and the law.  In giving allegiance to Christ he became a despised outcast to his former associates.  See  Philippians 3:5 Philippians 3:6 .

title: Philippians 3:17
text: Imitators together of me. The context ( Philippians 3:18 Philippians 3:19 ) shows that the imitation urged was as to Paul's attitude toward the things of the world as well as the anxious spirit in which he pressed onward.

title: Philippians 3:18
text: Enemies of the cross of Christ. These were not of the unbelievers, that some among the brethren.  As the cross is the symbol of self-sacrifice, those who 'mind earthly things' ( Philippians 3:19 ) are at enmity to all that the cross stands for.

title: Philippians 3:20
text: Our citizenship is in heaven. This illustration was drawn from the fact that the citizenship of the Philippian was in Rome.  Paul voiced the same idea in  Hebrews 13:14 :- 'for we have not here an abiding city, but we seek after the city which is to come.'

title: Philippians 3:21
text:
The body of our humiliation. This is the body of the flesh which so humiliated Paul, when he declared 'For the good which I would do not: but the evil which I would not, that I practise' ( Romans 7:19 ).
 

 
 Conformed to the body of his glory. This may refer to the glorified body of Jesus at the transfiguration ( Matthew 17:2 ), or to Paul's vision of him on the way to Damascus ( Acts 9:3 I Corinthians 15:8 ).  Paul enlarges on the coming change in  I Corinthians 15:51-54 .

title: Philippians 4:2
text: I exhort Euodia and I exhort Syntyche. It is generally accepted that these prominent women were in marked disagreement and tat Paul is urging them to find reconciliation in the 'mind of the Lord.'

title: Philippians 4:3
text:
True yokefellow.  This is by some commentators believed to be Epaphroditus, the bearer of the epistle.  See  Philippians 2:25 .
 

 
 They labored with me in the gospel. In the early church, women were engaged as active helpers in spreading the gospel.  See  Acts 17:4 Acts 17:12 .
 

 
 Whose names are in the book of life. It is plain that the possession of saving grace is of greater moment than a record of deeds.  Jesus said, 'Rejoice not that the spirits are subject unto you; but rejoice that your names are written in heaven' ( Luke 10:20 ).

title: Philippians 4:10
text: Ye have revived your thought for me. Paul had suffered want more than once, and the Philippians had before this contributed to his needs.  See  II Corinthians 11:8 II Corinthians 11:9 .

title: Philippians 4:15
text:
In the beginning of the gospel. When Paul first began his work among them.
 

 
 When I departed from Macedonia. See  Acts 16:40 .

title: Philippians 4:16
text: Even in Thessalonica. See  Acts 17:1 .

title: Philippians 4:17
text: Not that I seek for the gift. The desire to give was the added 'grace' in which Paul delighted.  See  II Corinthians 8:4 II Corinthians 8:7 .  The compassionate love of the brethren was a sign that they had 'passed from death unto life' ( I John 3:14 I John 3:17 ).

title: Philippians 4:18
text: An odor of a sweet smell. A figure of speech alluding to the ceremony of the burnt-offering.  See  Exodus 29:18 Exodus 29:25 .

title: Philippians 4:22
text: Especially they that are of Caesar's household. Paul had taken advantage of his imprisonment to preach the gospel even to the soldiers who were his jailers, and they joined him in sending greeting to the Philippians.  See  Philippians 1:13 .

title: Colossians 1:1
text: Through the will of God.  Paul keeps always in mind the fact of his conversion by the miraculous intervention of God.  See  Acts 9:3-22 . It was not through his own will that he became an apostle.

title: Colossians 1:2
text:
To the saints. This name was used to signify those who were set apart or consecrated-in the world but not of the world.
 

 
 At Colossae. Colossae, in the time of Paul was a small town in Phrygia, Asia Minor, a few miles southeasterly from Laodicea.  It is believed that Paul wrote the epistle while he was imprisoned at Rome.

title: Colossians 1:7
text: Of Epaphras. Paul's endorsement of the teachings of Epaphras shows that there were false teachers among the Colossians also.  These men seem to have followed the apostles about, devoting their energies to leading astray those who had already embraced Christianity.

title: Colossians 1:8
text:
Declared unto us. Epaphras had come to Paul with his trouble and he also was made a prisoner.  See  Philemon 1:23 .
 

 
 In the Spirit has been construed as showing that Paul had not then visited the Colossians.  See  Colossians 2:1 .

title: Colossians 1:9
text: Wisdom and understanding. The subtle arguments and enticements of the false teachers required of Christians a high degree of wisdom to 'prove all things: hold fast that which is good' ( I Thessalonians 5:21 ).

title: Colossians 1:12
text: In light. In understanding; as contrasted with the darkness of ignorance.  See  Colossians 1:13 Acts 26:18 Ephesians 4:18 Ephesians 5:8 .

title: Colossians 1:15
text: The firstborn of all creation. Christ was 'before all things' ( Colossians 1:17 ), 'in the beginning with God' ( John 1:1 John 1:2 ).  See  John 8:58 .

title: Colossians 1:16
text: Thrones or dominions or principalities or powers.  This is taken to be an allusion to the system of angel worship introduced by the false teachers in Colossae.  See  Romans 8:38 Ephesians 1:21 I Peter 3:22 .

title: Colossians 1:18
text: The firstborn from the dead. The first to experience the resurrection of the body.  See  Acts 26:23 I Corinthians 15:20 I Corinthians 15:23 Revelation of John 1:5 .

title: Colossians 1:22
text:
Reconciled. 'God was in Christ reconciling the world unto himself' ( II Corinthians 5:19 ).
 

 
 In the body. Christ came 'in the likeness of sinful flesh' ( Romans 8:3 ).  See  Romans 8:10 .

title: Colossians 1:23
text: If so be. There was a condition upon which reconciliation became effective-continuance in the faith of the pure gospel.

title: Colossians 1:24
text: On my part. Whatever lack there might be in Paul's afflictions through continual persecution because of his faith, he made up on his own part by anxious solicitude regarding the churches.  See  II Corinthians 2:4 .

title: Colossians 1:26
text: The mystery. To Paul the mystery of the gospel was that the gentiles, equally with the chosen people-The Jews-should be saved; and by a salvation not through obedience to the outward ordinances of the law, but of 'Christ in you' ( Colossians 1:27 ); accepted by the inward man and renewing the whole being; through which they passed out of death into life ( I John 3:14 ).

title: Colossians 2:1
text:
I strive. In prayer and earnest counsel.
 

 
 Laodicea. A town near Colossae and Hierapolis, damaged with them by an earthquake, in the time of Nero.  It was a place of great wealth.  See  Revelation of John 3:17 .

title: Colossians 2:2
text: The mystery of God. See  Colossians 1:27  and note on  Colossians 1:26 .

title: Colossians 2:6
text: As... ye received. According to the gospel as first preached to you.

title: Colossians 2:8
text:
Spoil. Or booty; in the sense of leading captive your understanding through deceitful reasonings.  See 2Pe 2.1, 19.
 

 
 The rudiments of the world. The elementary forces of the life of the flesh; the powers of darkness.  See  Colossians 1:13 Galatians 4:3 Galatians 4:9 .

title: Colossians 2:11
text: Made with hands. The circumcision among the Jews was a seal of the old covenant.  Under the new covenant the circumcision of Christ was the putting off of the body of the flesh:-that is, the whole carnal nature.  See  Romans 2:29 Romans 6:6 Romans 6:11 Galatians 5:24 .

title: Colossians 2:13
text: The uncircumcision. This does not refer to the Jewish rite, but is in the sense given in the note on  Colossians 2:11 .  See  Romans 2:26 Romans 2:27 .

title: Colossians 2:14
text:
In ordinances. The Jewish law.
 

 
 Against us. The law was against the nature of the people.  Through regeneration by the Spirit the nature was changed to work righteousness regardless of the law which was thus blotted out.  See  Romans 10:4 Ephesians 2:15 .

title: Colossians 2:15
text: Principalities, etc.  The invisible 'spirits of the air,' believed in as mediators and avengers.  Christ did his work openly, in the sight of all men.  See  Ephesians 2:2 Ephesians 6:12 .

title: Colossians 2:16
text: Judge you. Comdemn you- because of eating or not eating; keeping a feast day, or not keeping it.  See  Romans 14:1-23 I Chronicles 23:31 .

title: Colossians 2:18
text: Voluntary humility. Some of the false teachers made a show of humility by dressing in rags and scourging themselves with whips.  See  Colossians 2:23 .

title: Colossians 2:19
text:
Holding fast the head. 'If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch, and is withered' ( John 15:6 ).
 

 
 The increase of God. That growth 'in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ' ( II Peter 3:18 ), through which 'we all attain...unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ' ( Ephesians 4:13 Ephesians 4:16 ).

title: Colossians 2:23
text: Severity to the body. Referring to the practices of scourging, or slashing the body with knives, and other self-inflictions, all equally ineffective in renewing the inter man.  See  Galatians 6:15 Ephesians 4:24 .

title: Colossians 3:3
text: For ye died. Through the crucifixion of 'the flesh with the passions and the lusts thereof' ( Galatians 5:24 ).  See  Romans 6:6 Galatians 2:20 Galatians 6:14 .

title: Colossians 3:5
text: Your members. Paul found in himself a law of his members warring against the law of his mind ( Romans 7:23 ).  It was this carnal nature that was to be put to death.  The same thought was voiced by Jesus in  Matthew 5:30 : 'If thy right hand causeth thee to stumble, cut it off, and cast it from thee.' See also  Romans 6:13 Romans 6:19 Ephesians 5:5 James 4:1 .

title: Colossians 3:11
text:
Greek and Jew. The title 'Greek' was used to include all Gentiles.
 

 
 Scythian. The most barbarous type of the barbarians.  The new Christ-man blotted out all human classifications.

title: Colossians 3:14
text: Bond of perfectness. Christian love is the one perfect bond.  See  John 13:34 .

title: Colossians 3:24
text: Ye serve the Lord Christ. All conscientous service done as it to Christ is in fact service of Christ.

title: Colossians 3:25
text: No respect of persons. The law that 'whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap,' is universal.  There are no exceptions.  The fruitage is in the seed itself.  See  Galatians 6:7 Galatians 6:8 Acts 10:34 .

title: Colossians 4:3
text:
The mystery. See note  Colossians 1:26 .
 

 
 In bonds. the chains with which Paul was bound.

title: Colossians 4:6
text: Seasoned with salt. So filled with wisdom as to be acceptable to the understanding of those to whom it was addressed.

title: Colossians 4:7
text: Tychicus. The epistle to the Ephesians was also sent by Tychicus.  See  Acts 20:4 Ephesians 6:21 II Timothy 4:12 .

title: Colossians 4:9
text: Onesimus. A fugitive slave of Philemon, one  of the Colossian church.  He was sent with Tychicus to Colossae, and bore an epistle to Philemon.  See  Philemon 1:10 .

title: Colossians 4:10
text:
Aristarchus. A Macedonian who had been a fellow-worker with Paul.  He and Gaius had been seized with Paul at Ephesus, and at the time of the writing of this epistle he was a prisoner with Paul.  See  Acts 19:29 Acts 20:4 Acts 27:2 .
 

 
 Mark. John Mark, the evangelist who was the cause of the separation of Paul and Barnabas.  See  Acts 12:12 Acts 13:13 Acts 15:37-39 .
 

 
 Receive him. A passing endorsement of Mark, to set aside any prejudice against him because of his former trouble with Paul.

title: Colossians 4:11
text: Who are the circumcision. The only Jewish workers who were with Paul.

title: Colossians 4:16
text: The epistle from Laodicea. This letter is believed to be the one now known as the Epistle to the Ephesians.  Many excellent arguments support this view, especially as the oldest copies of the epistle omit the world Ephesus in the greeting.  No other epistle to Laodicea is in existence.

title: Colossians 4:17
text: Archippus. Mentioned also in  Philemon 1:2 .

title: Colossians 4:18
text: Remember my bonds. It was Paul's habit to have his letters written by a secretary, and to write a brief salutation at the close with his own hand to assure their authenticity.  See  II Thessalonians 3:17 .  The bonds to which Paul here refers consisted of a chain joining his right hand to the left hand of a soldier.  Probably it caused such a difference in his handwriting as to require this explanation.

title: I Thessalonians 1:1
text:
Silvanus. Another name for Silas.  See  Acts 15:22 Acts 15:40 .
 

 
 Timothy. Chosen by Paul at Lystra ( Acts 16:1 ), to accompany himself and Silas.  The three labored together at Thessalonica ( Acts 17:10 Acts 17:14 ), and also at Corinth ( Acts 18:5 ).  See  II Corinthians 1:19 .  Thessalonica was a 'free city' as distinguished from a colony like Philippi, or Troas.  As a free city it was wholly self-governing, and had no Roman garrison.  This epistle was written upon the return of Timothy to Athens from Thessalonica.  See  I Thessalonians 3:6 .

title: I Thessalonians 1:2
text: We. Although others are joined with Paul in the salutation ( I Thessalonians 1:1 ), the body of the epistle shows that Paul used to plural here, as also in the epistles to the Corinthians, to designate himself alone.  See  I Thessalonians 3:1 .

title: I Thessalonians 1:5
text: In power. The 'power of signs and wonders' ( Romans 15:19 ) which accompanied Paul's ministry as well as that of the other apostles.  See  Acts 14:3 Acts 15:12 II Corinthians 12:12 ; also  John 4:48 Acts 2:43 Acts 4:30 I Corinthians 1:22 .

title: I Thessalonians 1:6
text: In much affliction. The first converts of Paul and Silas at Thessalonica were subjected to much persecution.  See  Acts 17:5-9 .

title: I Thessalonians 1:7
text: In Macedonia and in Achaia. At this time these two provinces included all of Greece: Macedonia the northern, and Achaia the southern part.

title: I Thessalonians 1:8
text: In every place. Thessalonica was the commercial centre of a large region and an important seaport as well.  News from there would be widespread, and the disorderly demonstrations referred to in  Acts 17:5-9 , would be sure to be reported with much detail.

title: I Thessalonians 1:10
text: The wrath to come. The wrath of God which falls upon the sons of disobedience ( Ephesians 5:6 ), 'is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men' ( Romans 1:18 ).  See  Romans 1:28 Romans 1:32 Romans 2:8 Romans 2:9 Ephesians 2:3 Colossians 3:6 .

title: I Thessalonians 2:2
text: Shamefully treated...at Philippi. See  Acts 16:22-24 .

title: I Thessalonians 2:6
text: Authority. Paul led his converts into the truth, he did not exercise lordship over them.  See  II Corinthians 1:24 .

title: I Thessalonians 2:9
text: Might not burden any. One of the arguments used against Paul by his critics was the fact that he did not ask maintenance of those to whom he ministered, according to the declaration of the Lord, that 'the laborer is worthy of his hire' ( Luke 10:7 ).  At Thessalonica he worked 'night and day' to maintain himself.  See  Acts 18:3 Acts 20:34 I Corinthians 9:3-14 II Thessalonians 3:8 II Thessalonians 3:9 .

title: I Thessalonians 2:15
text: Drove out us. The Jews were particularly bitter against Paul because of his ministering to the Gentiles. See  Acts 17:10-14 .  Even the Christian Jews followed him from place to place declaiming against him and his work.  See  Acts 15:1 II Corinthians 11:4 Galatians 1:7 .

title: I Thessalonians 2:18
text: Satan hindered. It is surmised that illness prevented Paul's going to Thessalonica.  See  II Corinthians 12:7-9 .

title: I Thessalonians 3:1
text: No longer forbear. Paul's anxiety to hear from them grew so strong as to lead him to send Timothy, even though it left him alone.  See  I Thessalonians 3:5 .

title: I Thessalonians 3:3
text: We are appointed. See  Acts 9:16 .

title: I Thessalonians 3:4
text: As it came to pass. See note  I Thessalonians 1:6 I Thessalonians 2:14 .

title: I Thessalonians 3:5
text: The tempter. When Jesus was being tempted of the devil in the wilderness the tempter's first suggestion to him was to return to the ease of worldly life by using his divine power to relieve the hunger of his body ( Matthew 4:3 ).  Paul feared lest the Thessalonians would be led back into the easier life of the world through weariness of persecutions.

title: I Thessalonians 4:3
text: Even your sanctification. Complete sanctification is impossible until the flesh is overcome with all its lusts.  See  Hebrews 10:10 Romans 6:12 Romans 6:13 .

title: I Thessalonians 4:4
text: How to possess himself. The continual struggle for this possession, or mastery of the body is pictured in  Romans 7:15-24 ; and is epitomized in Paul's exclamation, 'The good which I would I do not: but the evil which I would not, that I practise.'

title: I Thessalonians 4:8
text: Rejecteth not man.  In rejecting Paul's message, they rejected not him, but God, whose messenger he was.

title: I Thessalonians 4:11
text:
To be quiet. Paul seems to be admonishing the Thessalonians against religious excitement concerning the second coming of Christ, which they believed to be imminent.  See 2Th 2.2; 3.11.
 

 
 Work with your hands. Paul himself had set them an example of industry.  See note  I Thessalonians 2:9 .

title: I Thessalonians 4:12
text: Becomingly. Outward behavior to those who are not Christians is to be carefully guarded lest it give offense.  Paul set an example in his own conduct, which he urged the Thessalonians to imitate.  See  II Thessalonians 3:7-9 .  Also  Romans 14:1-7 Romans 14:13 Romans 14:15 Romans 15:2 .

title: I Thessalonians 4:13
text: As the rest. The belief held generally by the Greeks was that there was no resurrection; that death was the end of all things.

title: I Thessalonians 4:14
text: And rose again. Paul bases his argument for the resurrection upon the resurrection.  See  I Corinthians 15:12-23 .

title: I Thessalonians 5:2
text: As a thief in the night.  In reminding the Thessalonians that they 'knew perfectly' that the day of the Lord would come in this manner, Paul was doubtless referring to the words of Jesus recorded in  Luke 12:39 .  See also  Luke 21:34 Luke 21:35 .  The word translated 'thief,' is, more exactly, 'bandit,' a murderer as well as a thief.

title: I Thessalonians 5:4
text: Darkness. The word is used to signify ignorance as to the spiritual meaning of the gospel.  See  Matthew 4:16 John 8:12 John 12:46 I John 2:9 I John 2:11 .

title: I Thessalonians 5:5
text: Sons of light. Those whose understanding has been regenerated in Christ.  See  John 8:12 John 12:36 Ephesians 5:9 .

title: I Thessalonians 5:6
text: The rest. The unregenerate; the 'children of wrath' ( Ephesians 2:3 ). See  Romans 1:28-31 .

title: I Thessalonians 5:9
text: Obtaining of salvation. Salvation is a gift but it must be grasped to become effective.  Paul exhorted the Philippians to work out their salvation 'with fear and trembling' ( Philippians 2:12 ).  See  Philippians 3:12 Philippians 3:13 I Timothy 6:12 I Timothy 6:19 Hebrews 6:18 .

title: I Thessalonians 5:17
text: Without ceasing. True prayer is unceasing-the earnest, ever present desire for spiritual blessings ( Ephesians 1:3 ); by no means the long prayers of the scribes which Jesus condemned (Mk 12.40).  See  I Thessalonians 2:13 Romans 1:9 II Timothy 1:3 .

title: I Thessalonians 5:19
text: Quench not the Spirit. Sensual and worldly living means the exclusion of the Spirit, 'for the flesh lusteth against the Spirit,' and 'these are contrary the one to the other' ( Galatians 5:17 ).  See  Romans 8:6 Romans 8:13 .

title: I Thessalonians 5:20
text: Prophesyings. More exactly, 'inspired preaching.'  This was a common gift among the early Christians, and was subject to some abuses.  See  I Corinthians 14:1-40 ; especially  I Corinthians 14:31 .  Also  Romans 12:6 I Corinthians 12:10 I Corinthians 12:29 I Corinthians 13:2 I Corinthians 13:9 .

title: I Thessalonians 5:21
text: Prove all things. This injunction to put all things to the test before accepting them as good probably relates to the prophesyings mentioned in the preceding verse.  See  I Corinthians 14:24 I Corinthians 14:29 .

title: I Thessalonians 5:26
text: A holy kiss. The kiss was the common form of salutation between friends.  It was often insincere in that it did not express true fellowship; as the treacherous kiss of Judas.

title: II Thessalonians 1:1
text: Silvanus, and Timothy. Silas and Timothy were still with Paul when this epistle was written.  Timothy was later at Ephesus with Paul, but meanwhile Silas had dropped out of the historical record.

title: II Thessalonians 1:3
text: Your faith groweth. The Thessalonians believed that the second coming of Christ was at hand, and under this spur their faith increased exceedingly, together with such an outpouring of brotherly love that Paul is moved to unstinted thankfulness and commendation.  See  II Thessalonians 1:4 .

title: II Thessalonians 1:5
text: A manifest token. The manner in which the Thessalonians had borne their persecutions had already brought forth fruit in a higher degree of faith and a larger measure of love among themselves.

title: II Thessalonians 1:6
text: To recompense affliction. The divine law of recompense is declared by Jesus in the words: 'For with what measure ye mete it shall be measured to you again' ( Luke 6:38 ).  Under this law every man established his own recompense.  See  Romans 2:6 II Corinthians 5:10 .

title: II Thessalonians 1:8
text: Vengeance. The word is not used in the sense of revenge, but of just recompense.  See note on  II Thessalonians 1:6 ; also  Romans 12:19 Romans 12:20 .

title: II Thessalonians 1:11
text:
Every desire of goodness. Progress comes through desire.  Paul himself was constantly reaching forward ( Philippians 3:13 ), and urging his hearers to higher levels.  See  I Corinthians 12:31 I Corinthians 14:1 Ephesians 5:9 .
 

 
 With power. The unusual power which worked wonders.  See preceding note on this verse; also  Romans 15:19 I Corinthians 2:4 I Thessalonians 1:5 .

title: II Thessalonians 2:2
text: By epistle as from us. The inference must be that a letter falsely declared to be from Paul, had been used to uphold the contention of a faction in the Thessalonian church which believed the second coming of Christ to be at hand.  It is probable that this incident, with the continued fanatical excitement of the people, led Paul to write this second epistle.  See note  I Thessalonians 4:11 .

title: II Thessalonians 2:3
text:
Falling away. In the Greek, 'apostasy.' See  I Timothy 4:1 II Timothy 3:1 II Timothy 3:5 .
 

 
 The son of perdition. A title also applied to Judas Iscariot.  See  John 17:12 John 6:70 .

title: II Thessalonians 2:4
text: He that opposeth. See Re 13.5-8

title: II Thessalonians 2:7
text: One that restraineth. Generally accepted as being the Roman government, which, for a time, protected the early Christians from the attacks of the Jews.  See  Acts 18:14 Acts 18:15 Acts 21:32 Acts 23:12-24 .

title: II Thessalonians 2:9
text: Lying wonders. Some of the false Christs also worked signs and wonders.  See  Matthew 12:27 Matthew 24:24 Acts 19:13 Revelation of John 13:13 Revelation of John 13:14 .

title: II Thessalonians 2:11
text: A working of error. The error of worldly wisdom.  See  Romans 1:21 Romans 1:22 Romans 1:24 Romans 1:25 Romans 1:28 .  When the people harden their hearts against the truth as it is in Christ they pay the penalty of becoming victims of their own delusions.

title: II Thessalonians 2:12
text: Pleasure in unrighteousness. There were some who seized joyfully upon the doctrines of the false teachers, because they were permitted to indulge their fleshly desires under promise that all sin was already atoned for in the death of Christ.  See  II Peter 2:1 II Peter 2:2 II Peter 2:19 .

title: II Thessalonians 2:15
text: Traditions. Not the traditions of the Jewish nations, but the teachings of the apostles.

title: II Thessalonians 3:2
text:
Unreasonable. Those not controlled by reason-violent.  They were probably Jews who did not accept Christianity.
 

 
 Faith. In Jesus Christ.

title: II Thessalonians 3:5
text:
Love of God. Love for God.
 

 
 Patience of Christ. Using the word patience in the sense of stedfastness, Paul is urging the Thessalonians to a similar stedfastness in the fact of tribulations.

title: II Thessalonians 3:6
text: Walketh disorderly. See note  I Thessalonians 4:11 ; also  II Thessalonians 3:11 .

title: II Thessalonians 3:8
text: At any man's hand.  See note  I Thessalonians 2:9 II Corinthians 11:7-9 .

title: II Thessalonians 3:9
text: The right. With the commission to 'the seventy' went the injunction to expect maintenance as a right from those to whom they ministered; 'for the laborer is worthy of his hire' ( Luke 10:7 ).  See  I Corinthians 9:7-14 .

title: I Timothy 1:1
text: The commandment. See  Acts 9:6 .

title: I Timothy 1:2
text: Unto Timothy. Then preaching at Ephesus.  The epistle seems to have been written to afford Timothy documentary proof that Paul endorsed his teachings.

title: I Timothy 1:3
text:
Ephesus.  The chief city of Asia Minor and one of the 'free' cities under the Roman empire.  Here was the celebrated temple of the goddess Diana, to whose worship they city, as a whole, was devoted.  See  Acts 19:23-41 .
 

 
Macedonia. The northern Roman province of Greece, the southern being Achaia.  Its chief city was Philippi.  See  Acts 16:12 Acts 20:1 .

title: I Timothy 1:4
text:
Fables. Fanciful traditions as to the origin of angels and their powers, and similar superstitions.  See  I Timothy 4:7 II Timothy 4:4 Titus 1:14 II Peter 1:16 .
 

 
 Genealogies...questionings. Fruitless speculation on things of no importance. The one vital matter was faith in Christ Jesus.

title: I Timothy 1:7
text: Of the law. From the context this is accepted as being the Mosaic law, which the Judaizers were trying to impose upon the Ephesian church.

title: I Timothy 1:13
text:
A persecutor. See  Acts 8:3 Philippians 3:6 .
 

 
 Injurious. The word thus translated includes the sense of violence and outrage.
 

 
 In unbelief. Paul felt his humiliation not less because his persecutions had been carried on with a good conscience in ignorance.  See  Acts 23:1 .

title: I Timothy 1:15
text: The saying. See  Mark 2:17 .

title: I Timothy 1:16
text: An ensample. Paul regarded himself as the chief of sinners ( I Timothy 1:15 ), and as having received the most abounding forgiveness in the trust committed to him.  ( I Timothy 1:11 ) in the great ministry to the Gentile world.

title: I Timothy 1:17
text: King. This title as applied to God occurs only here, in  I Timothy 6:15 , and in  Matthew 5:35 .  See also  Revelation of John 19:16 .

title: I Timothy 1:18
text: Prophecies. Timothy's special fitness for the work before him was discerned by other disciples who recommended him to Paul ( Acts 16:2 ).  In the light of his achievements their words have proved to be prophetic.

title: I Timothy 1:20
text:
Hymenaeus and Alexander. It is generally accepted that Hymenaeus was the person mentioned in  II Timothy 2:17 II Timothy 2:18 , as teaching false doctrine.  Alexander was probably 'the coppersmith' spoken of in  II Timothy 4:14 II Timothy 4:15 .
 

 
 Delivered unto Satan. That is, to the ever-increasing darkness of their own erroneous beliefs.  See  Romans 1:21 Romans 1:24 Romans 1:28 Ephesians 4:18 ; also  I Corinthians 5:5 .

title: I Timothy 2:1
text: For all men. A declaration of the virtual unity of all men in one brotherhood.  See  I Timothy 2:4 I Timothy 2:6 Galatians 6:10 Colossians 3:11 .

title: I Timothy 2:7
text: I speak the truth. Paul was recognized as an apostle by the original twelve apostles ( Acts 14:14 ), although some of his enemies denied his claim.  See  I Corinthians 9:1 I Corinthians 9:2 II Corinthians 12:12 I Thessalonians 2:6 .

title: I Timothy 2:12
text: I permit not a woman to teach. Evidently this prohibition refers only to the public assembly of the churches ( I Corinthians 14:34 ); for several passages show that women were active in the gospel work of that period.  See  Acts 18:26 Acts 21:9 Romans 16:1-3 Philippians 4:3 .  In making this prohibitions Paul doubtless had in mind the women spoken of in  I Timothy 5:15 , and in  II Timothy 3:6 .

title: I Timothy 2:15
text: Her childbearing. By some commentators this is regarded as referring to Mary's bearing of Jesus, the Saviour of men.  See  Galatians 4:4 .  Also  Galatians 3:19 .

title: I Timothy 3:2
text:
Of one wife. Various interpretations have been placed upon this phrase.  In view of the ease with which divorce was accomplished in those days it was not unusual that a man might have had several wives, in succession.  It is quite probable that Paul's prohibition was directed against men of this character.
 

 
 Given to hospitality. Evidently this was not a common grace, though of great moment in a dispensation of brotherly love.  See  Titus 1:8 .

title: I Timothy 3:6
text: Puffed up. A condition of pride fatal to spiritual growth.  See  I Timothy 6:4 Romans 1:21 Romans 1:22 I Corinthians 3:18-20 Galatians 6:3 II Timothy 3:4 .

title: I Timothy 3:7
text: Them that are without. The importance of the good opinion of outsiders is here insisted on.  Paul urged the same conduct upon the Colossians ( Colossians 4:5 ), and the Thessalonians ( I Thessalonians 4:12 ).

title: I Timothy 3:9
text: The mystery. That the Gentiles-that is, the whole world-should be saved not under the covenant of the Jewish law, but through simple faith in Christ.  See  Romans 16:25 I Corinthians 2:7 Ephesians 1:9 Ephesians 3:3-5 .

title: I Timothy 3:11
text: Women. Some of the foremost scholars regard these as the deaconesses, who were appointed to minister to the women of the church under the separation of the sexes which was then a custom.

title: I Timothy 3:12
text: Of one wife. See note on  I Timothy 3:2 .

title: I Timothy 4:1
text:
The spirit saith. Some of the early Christians had the spiritual gift of prophetic utterance ( I Corinthians 12:10 ).  See  John 16:13 Acts 20:23 Acts 21:11 I Corinthians 2:9 I Corinthians 2:10 .
 

 
 Doctrines of demons. The 'wisdom' which James denounced as 'earthly, sensual, devilish' ( James 3:15 ).  See  II Thessalonians 2:9 II Thessalonians 2:10 Revelation of John 2:24 .

title: I Timothy 4:3
text: Abstain from meats. Paul here denounces those who, by forbidding what is acceptable to God, would encourage a false self-denial leading to harmful results.

title: I Timothy 4:4
text: With thanksgiving. As filling a real and present need.

title: I Timothy 4:7
text: Fables. See note  I Timothy 1:4 .

title: I Timothy 4:8
text: Bodily exercise. There was a faction in the early church which sought to control the appetites of the flesh by inflicting injuries upon the body, instead of through the regeneration of the spirit.  Paul urges that exercise be 'unto godliness' ( I Timothy 4:7 ).  See  Colossians 2:23 .

title: I Timothy 4:12
text: Thy youth. Timothy was between 36 and 40; young for a presbyter.

title: I Timothy 4:14
text: The gift. Probably the gift of inspirational teaching.  See  I Corinthians 12:28 Ephesians 4:11 ; also  Acts 13:1-3 Romans 12:6-8 .

title: I Timothy 5:3
text: Widows indeed. Evidently those without relatives to support them ( I Timothy 5:4 ).  See  Acts 6:1 Acts 9:39 .

title: I Timothy 5:4
text: Let them learn. 'Them' refers to the children and grandchildren who are to requite the care they received in childhood.

title: I Timothy 5:6
text:
Pleasure. Satisfying oneself with worldly things.  See  Luke 8:14 II Timothy 3:4 James 5:5 .
 

 
 Dead. Spiritually dead.  See  Romans 4:17 Romans 8:13 Revelation of John 3:1 .

title: I Timothy 5:10
text: Washed the saints' feet. This service was a ministration in the life of the home.  See  Luke 7:44 John 13:14 .

title: I Timothy 5:11
text: Wanton. The sense is more exactly expressed by the word 'luxurious.' See  Revelation of John 18:7 Revelation of John 18:9 .

title: I Timothy 5:12
text: Their first pledge. When a widow was enrolled among the church widows it was with the pledge that she would devote her life to the work assigned her by the church.

title: I Timothy 5:15
text: Turned aside. Probably to the false teachers mentioned in  I Timothy 1:20 .  See  II Timothy 3:3 .

title: I Timothy 5:16
text:
Hath widows. Among her relatives.
 

 
 Widows indeed. Those without any means of support.  See note  I Timothy 5:3 .

title: I Timothy 5:17
text: Double honor. The elders, or aged men, among the Jews received honor.  When fulfilling faithfully their appointed duties as elders in the Christian church ( Acts 14:23 ), they were worthy of double honor.

title: I Timothy 5:18
text: Worthy of his hire. See  Luke 10:7 .

title: I Timothy 5:22
text:
Lay hands.  In the sense of to ordain to church office.  See  Acts 6:6 Acts 8:17 Acts 13:3 Acts 19:6 .
 

 
 Be partaker. By the hasty ordination of an unfit person, Timothy would be responsible for his errors.

title: I Timothy 5:23
text: Use a little wine. In his desire to give no man offense ( Romans 14:3 Romans 14:21 ), Timothy had denied himself needed tonic.

title: I Timothy 5:24
text: Follow after. Are not immediately uncovered.

title: I Timothy 6:1
text:
Under the yoke. As slaves; many of whom embraced Christianity.  The gospel elevated slavery into the fellowship of brotherhood. However, the slave was not to presume upon this new relation, but to render his service with honor.  See  Ephesians 6:5 Titus 2:9 I Peter 2:18 .
 

 
 Be not blasphemed. The profession of a belief in Christ which did not include brotherly love expressed in cheerful service, was considered blasphemy by Paul.  See  John 13:34 Romans 12:10 I Thessalonians 4:9 I Peter 1:22 .

title: I Timothy 6:4
text: Doting. Having an unwholesome appetite for controversy.  See  I Timothy 1:4 II Timothy 2:14 .

title: I Timothy 6:5
text: A way of gain. The teaching of Jesus had been, 'Seek ya first his kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things shall be added unto you' ( Matthew 6:33 ).  There were some whose corrupted minds led them to embrace Christianity for the sake of the things they desired, and hoped would be added.

title: I Timothy 6:6
text: Godliness with contentment. That is, contentment with the godliness for its own sake.

title: I Timothy 6:10
text: Money. The term includes the love of, or desire for, those things of the world which money will buy.

title: I Timothy 6:12
text:
The good confession. The confession of faith in the gospel of Christ.  See  II Corinthians 9:13 .
 

 
 Many witnesses. See  Acts 16:2 II Timothy 2:2 ; also  Romans 10:9 Romans 10:10 .

title: I Timothy 6:14
text: The commandment. Th end to be achieved is 'love out of a pure heart and a good conscience and faith unfeigned' ( I Timothy 1:5 ).

title: I Timothy 6:15
text: King of kings. See note  I Timothy 1:17 .

title: I Timothy 6:16
text:
Who only. God alone has immortality as the essence of His being.  Those who inherit eternal life do so through faith in His only begotten Son ( John 3:16 ), through whom we become 'heirs of God and joint-heirs with Christ' ( Romans 8:17 ).
 

 
 No man hath seen. See  John 1:18 Colossians 1:15 I John 4:12 .

title: I Timothy 6:17
text: In this present world. IN the things of this life in the flesh.

title: I Timothy 6:19
text: A good foundation. 'Treasures in heaven' ( Matthew 6:20 ). See  Matthew 19:21 Luke 12:33 .

title: I Timothy 6:20
text: The knowledge. From the beginning the church has been the prey of those who distort the simple truth as given by Jesus into systems formed of their own vain imaginings.  See  Romans 1:21 Ephesians 4:17 Colossians 2:18 Colossians 2:23 .

title: II Timothy 1:1
text: The life. The spiritual life, or life eternal.  See  Matthew 25:46 Mark 10:30 John 3:15 John 3:16 John 6:53-57

title: II Timothy 1:3
text: In a pure conscience.  However far from the truth Paul had been before his conversion he had lived up to the best that he knew, under the guidance of a pure conscience.  See  Acts 23:1 Acts 24:14-16 II Corinthians 1:12 .

title: II Timothy 1:5
text: Eunice. 'A Jewess that believed' ( Acts 16:1 ).  See  II Timothy 3:15 .

title: II Timothy 1:6
text: Laying on of my hands. See note  I Timothy 4:14 ; also  Acts 8:17-20 .

title: II Timothy 1:7
text: Fearfulness.  Perhaps referring to the authority of the Jewish law which was upheld by fear of the penalties threatened.  In a wider sense it may be taken as the fear of the powers of darkness ( Ephesians 6:12 ), as opposed to the power of God.  See  Romans 15:19 I Corinthians 2:4 I Corinthians 2:5 II Corinthians 6:7 II Corinthians 13:4 .

title: II Timothy 1:8
text:
Testimony of our Lord. Bearing witness to faith in Christ.
 

 
 His prisoner. Paul was suffering his second imprisonment at Rome at the time this epistle was written.

title: II Timothy 1:9
text: Before times eternal. The grace of Christ was really bestowed upon mankind under the old covenant, but became manifest only under the new covenant of the gospel.  See  Titus 1:2 Titus 1:3 .

title: II Timothy 1:10
text: Abolished death. By his resurrection in the body Christ had proved death conquerable.  See  I Corinthians 15:20 I Corinthians 15:23 I Corinthians 15:26 Hebrews 2:14 .

title: II Timothy 1:12
text:
That which I have committed. The great desire of the Jews was for eternal life ( Mark 10:17 Luke 10:25 Acts 20:32 ), and in the faith that Christ was the way ( John 14:6 ), he committed his life here and hereafter wholly and unreservedly to his service.
 

 
 That day. The day of Christ's coming.  See  I Thessalonians 1:10 .

title: II Timothy 1:13
text: The pattern. The oft-repeated injunction of Paul to cling to the original teachings of the gospel, indicates the great variance which seemed to be continually leading would-be followers into fatal error.  See  II Peter 2:18 II Peter 3:16 II Peter 3:17 .

title: II Timothy 1:15
text: Asia. See note on  Acts 19:10 .

title: II Timothy 1:16
text: The house of Onesiphorus. As only his house is mentioned it must be concluded that Onesiphorus himself had passed away.  See  II Timothy 4:19 .

title: II Timothy 1:18
text: Thou knowest. Timothy had spent more time than Paul had at Ephesus.

title: II Timothy 2:4
text: Who enrolled him. The soldier's allegiance is to his commander and his cause.  Paul urges an undivided allegiance upon Timothy.

title: II Timothy 2:5
text: Lawfully. According to the rules of the game.  Hardships are a part of the soldier's service.

title: II Timothy 2:8
