text: Of the seed of David. That is, Christ, a man in the flesh, and risen from the dead in the flesh.

title: II Timothy 2:9
text:
As a malefactor. Subject to the indignity of being chained to a soldier.
 

 
 The word of God is not bound. Even in his imprisonment Paul preached the truth to the soldiers of the guard ( Philippians 1:13 Philippians 4:22 ), and by his letters reached a larger congregation than he could have done with his preaching.

title: II Timothy 2:11
text: Died with him. As to the desires of the flesh.  See  Romans 6:5 Romans 6:6 .

title: II Timothy 2:12
text: Reign with him. See  Romans 5:17 Romans 8:17 .

title: II Timothy 2:13
text: He abideth faithful. He cannot deny his own nature; he must deny everything unlike himself.  If we do not accept him we place ourselves under condemnation.

title: II Timothy 2:14
text: About words. The warning here is against giving such attention to the words in which the gospel is presented that its vital truth is entirely lost.  The letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life ( II Corinthians 3:6 ).  See  I Timothy 6:4 Titus 3:9 .

title: II Timothy 2:19
text: The firm foundation. The unchanging truth of God, 'with whom can be no variation, neither shadow that is cast by turning' ( James 1:17 ).  In this connection Paul was probably speaking of the resurrection of Jesus as the foundation upon which Christianity was built.  See  I Corinthians 15:14 .

title: II Timothy 2:20
text: A great house. The parallel is drawn with the church.  Not all receive the gifts of grace in equal measure.  See  Romans 12:4-8 .

title: II Timothy 2:21
text: From these. Probably the false teachings spoken of in  II Timothy 2:16 . See  II Peter 2:1 II Peter 2:2 .

title: II Timothy 2:23
text: Ignorant questionings. Questions which arise in a mind lacking in understanding.

title: II Timothy 2:25
text: Give them repentance. The consequences to those who oppose teaching, and who wilfully 'refuse to have God in their knowledge,' are described in  Romans 1:21-32 .  Repentance to such as these comes as the mercy of God.  See  I Timothy 1:13 I Timothy 1:16 .

title: II Timothy 2:26
text: The snare of the devil. in this connection the snare operated through the distorting of doctrine in men's minds, leading them through a maze of reasonings having the form of godliness but not the reality ( II Timothy 3:5 ).  See  Ephesians 4:14 Ephesians 6:11 ; also  Romans 1:21 Romans 1:25 I Corinthians 8:13 II Corinthians 10:5 .

title: II Timothy 3:1
text: The last days. The apostles seem to have expected the immediate return of Christ in glory-the second coming-in their own generation.  They did not foresee the long and painful spread of the leaven of Christianity, although Jesus had warned them that only the Father had this knowledge.  See  Matthew 24:36 II Peter 3:3 .

title: II Timothy 3:6
text:
Take captive. See note on  II Timothy 2:26 .
 

 
 Silly women. See  I Timothy 5:6 I Timothy 5:13 .

title: II Timothy 3:8
text: Jannes and Jambres.  The names handed down by the Jewish traditions as those of the Egyptian sorcerers who wrought wonders in opposition to Moses and Aaron.  See  Exodus 7:11 Exodus 7:12 Exodus 7:22 Exodus 8:7 .

title: II Timothy 3:11
text:
Antioch. Antioch of Pisidia.
 

 
 Iconium. ( Acts 14:5 ).
 

 
 Lystra. ( Acts 14:19 ).
 

 
 Persecutions. ( II Corinthians 11:23-27 ).

title: II Timothy 3:13
text: Being deceived. A false teacher who is himself a victim of his own delusions Is the most dangerous of all, having the power added by sincerity.  See  Romans 1:21 II Corinthians 11:13 Galatians 1:7 II Thessalonians 2:10 Titus 1:10 II Peter 2:1 II Peter 2:19 Revelation of John 2:2 .

title: II Timothy 3:15
text: From a babe. See  II Timothy 1:5 .

title: II Timothy 3:16
text: Every scripture. The writings of the Old testament.  See  Romans 15:4 II Peter 1:21 .

title: II Timothy 4:3
text: Itching ears. Anxious to hear teaching in accordance with their desires.  See  Romans 1:24 James 1:14 James 1:15 .

title: II Timothy 4:6
text: The time of my departure. Tradition records the death of Paul by execution in the early summer of the year 68 A.D.  This second epistle to Timothy was written but a few weeks previous.  It is probable that Paul had  a clear premonition of his approaching end.

title: II Timothy 4:8
text: That day. See last note  II Timothy 1:12 .

title: II Timothy 4:10
text:
Forsook me. It would seem that as the execution of Paul became certain, their was a scattering of some of his associates at Rome, lest they might suffer a like fate.  Demas and Luke had been with Paul when he wrote the letter to the Colossians about six years previous.  This was during Paul's first imprisonment.  See  Colossians 4:14 Philemon 1:24 .
 

 
 Loved this present world. Did not desire to suffer martyrdom.
 

 
 Dalmatia. A district of Roman Illyricum lying north of Macedonia.  It was a wild and barbarous country.

title: II Timothy 4:14
text: Did me much evil. This apparently refers to Paul's 'first defence' ( II Timothy 4:16 ), where Alexander may have appeared as the accuser.  It is supposed by some commentators that this Alexander is the person mentioned in  I Timothy 1:20 .

title: II Timothy 4:16
text: No one took my part. It was a custom in both the Roman and Greek courts to allow the friends of the accused to intercede with pleas and prayers for mercy.

title: II Timothy 4:17
text: The mouth of the lion. This expression may refer to the practice of throwing Christians to the wild beasts in the arena, a common penalty under Nero's rule.

title: II Timothy 4:19
text:
Prisca. See  Acts 18:2 .
 

 
 Onesiphorus. See note on  II Timothy 1:16 .

title: II Timothy 4:20
text:
Erastus. See  Romans 16:23 .
 

 
 Trophimus. See  Acts 20:4 Acts 21:29 .

title: Titus 1:1
text: God's elect. Those whom God sealed with the earnest of the dwelling Spirit ( II Corinthians 1:22 ).  See  Colossians 3:12-15 .

title: Titus 1:4
text: My true child.  Titus was a Greek ( Galatians 2:3 ) who had been converted by the teaching of Paul; as also Timothy.  Titus is mentioned frequently in second Corinthians with expressions of approbation and regard.

title: Titus 1:5
text: Crete. An island in the Mediterranean Sea southeas of Greece.  Paul's experience there is recorded in  Acts 27:7 Acts 27:8 .  The visit at the time he left Titus there is not recorded.

title: Titus 1:6
text:
Of one wife. Of not more than one wife.  See note  I Timothy 3:2 .
 

 
 Or unruly. The behavior of a man's children would be a good indication of his capacity to occupy a larger position of rule in the church.  See  I Timothy 3:12 .

title: Titus 1:8
text: Hospitality. Perhaps more readily by hospitality than in any other way, the 'unfeigned love of the brethren' ( I Peter 1:22 ) was manifested.  See  Galatians 6:10 I John 3:14 III John 1:5 III John 1:6 .

title: Titus 1:10
text: They of the circumcision. That faction which taught that the Gentiles must come under the Jewish law before they could receive the benefits of the gospel of Christ.  See  Acts 10:45 Acts 11:2 .

title: Titus 1:12
text: One of themselves. Epimenides, a poet, who was regarded as an oracle.  He lived about 600 B.C.

title: Titus 1:15
text: All things are pure. The Jews 'of the circumcision' (Note on  Titus 1:10 ) taught the Jewish rules against eating animals which were unclean under the law.  See  Leviticus 11:1-43 .  Paul goes beyond these ceremonial observances and declares that to those already defiled in mind, nothing is pure.  See  Romans 14:14 Romans 14:20 Romans 14:23 .

title: Titus 1:16
text: They profess. The meaning is not that of hypocritical pretense.  These teachers insisted that they knew God; but their contentions were proved false by their works.  See  Matthew 15:8 I John 2:4 .

title: Titus 2:1
text: The sound doctrine. The very simplicity of faith in Christ seems to have been a stumbling block to the Jews, accustomed as they were to an elaborate ritual.  Perhaps it was for this reason that so many 'teachers' flourished, each trying to establish a system of Christianity embodying his own imaginations.  See  Romans 1:21 II Timothy 3:13 II Peter 2:1 .

title: Titus 2:5
text: Blasphemed. See note  II Timothy 4:22 .

title: Titus 2:8
text: To say of us. Paul's exhortation to give due regard to the opinions of the non-Christian people, was to preserve the name of Christ free from any reproach.  In this, Peter was in accord with Paul.  See  I Peter 2:12 ; also  Acts 28:22 .

title: Titus 2:9
text: Not gainsaving. The Christian attitude is that of lowliness of mind and loving service.  The apprehension of the truth as it is in Christ did not give the bondservant dominion over his master in the flesh, but inspired him to a more consecrated service, 'as unto the Lord' ( Ephesians 6:7 ).  See  Matthew 11:29 ;  Ephesians 4:2 .

title: Titus 2:11
text: To all men. This declaration has been accepted as a contradiction of the factional doctrine that only the enlightened would receive salvation.  See  I Timothy 2:4 .

title: Titus 2:14
text: Purify unto himself. The language of this verse relates to the Jewish ceremonial of sacrifice.  See  Exodus 19:5 Deuteronomy 14:2 I Peter 2:5 .  The idea is expanded in  Hebrews 9:11-14 .  See also  Hebrews 9:23 Hebrews 10:9 Hebrews 10:10 Hebrews 10:14 .

title: Titus 3:1
text: In subjection to rulers. Through a misapprehension as to the kind of freedom conferred by the gospel, some of the Jews became unruly and disposed to rebellion against the Roman authorities.

title: Titus 3:5
text: Washing of regeneration. A reference to the symbolism of baptism, which is a setting apart unto regeneration, a step preparatory to the 'renewing of the Holy Spirit.' See  John 3:5 Acts 22:16 I Corinthians 6:11 Ephesians 5:26 .

title: Titus 3:9
text: The law. The Jewish ceremonial law.  The Jew had been trained for centuries to the observance of this law and clung to its ceremonies. Much fruitless argument arose in the effort to preserve the law intact and graft Christianity upon it.

title: Titus 3:11
text: Perverted. The persistence in error after two admonishing showed that it sprang from inward moral darkness.  The man was 'self condemned' by his love for the cord; for the true spirit of the church was unity.  See  I Corinthians 12:20 ; also  Romans 2:8 II Corinthians 12:20 Galatians 5:20 .

title: Titus 3:12
text: Nicopolis. The city of that name in Epirus, founded by Augustus in memory of the victory of Actium.

title: Titus 3:13
text: Apollos. See  Acts 18:24-28 .  It is supposed that Zenas and Apollos were the bearers of this epistle to Titus.

title: Philemon 1:1
text:
A prisoner. This epistle was written at Rome during Paul's first imprisonment, nearly four years after his arrest at Jerusalem ( Acts 21:33 ), during all of which time he had been in bonds, but permitted to preach.  See  Acts 28:31 .
 

 
 Philemon. A member of the Christian church at Colossae.
 

 
 Apphia. Believed to have been the wife of Philemon.
 

 
 Archippus. Probably an evangelist, and Philemon's son.

title: Philemon 1:8
text: To enjoin thee. Under his apostlic authority Paul might have advised Philemon; but 'for love's sake,' he offers his request as a suppliant ( Philemon 1:9 ).

title: Philemon 1:10
text: Onesimus. A fugitive Asiatic slave, owned by Philemon.  From  Philemon 1:18 , it had been thought that he robbed his master before running away.  He was converted  at Rome under the preaching of Paul, who seems to have so lightly esteemed his character and capacity, that he wished to keep him at Rome in gospel work ( Philemon 1:13 ).

title: Philemon 1:15
text: For ever. Having accepted Christianity, Onesimus would never again desert his master, but serve him 'as unto the Lord' ( Ephesians 6:7 ).  See note on  Titus 2:9 .

title: Philemon 1:18
text: Oweth thee. Perhaps because of absence from his duties.  See also note on  Philemon 1:10 .

title: Philemon 1:19
text: Thine own self besides. A reminder that Philemon owes his knowledge of Christ to Paul, a much greater boon than he now asks for Onesimus.

title: Philemon 1:23
text: Epaphras. A Colossian, imprisoned with Paul.  See  Colossians 1:7 .

title: Philemon 1:24
text:
Aristarchus. A Thessalonian, also a prisoner with Paul.  See  Colossians 4:10 Acts 19:29 Acts 20:4 .
 

 
 Demas. See  Colossians 4:14 II Timothy 4:10 .
 

 
 Luke. See  Colossians 4:14 II Timothy 4:11 .

title: Hebrews 1:1
text:
Divers portions. The Old Testament prophets received only partial revelations from God; to none of them was given a vision of all the truth.
 

 
 Divers manners. The truth being many-sided came in many ways, directly from God or through holy men and women of different capabilities. It was revealed in dream, vision, command, prophecy, or through the instrumentality of a legal code.  It sometimes came in the form of promised blessings, and of warnings.  Its human agents were taken from many different positions and occupations.

title: Hebrews 1:2
text:
End of these days. The beginning of the Christian, the ushering in of the true Messianic kingdom.
 

 
 Worlds.  All things; the material universe.

title: Hebrews 1:3
text:
Effulgence of his glory. A new vision of the glory of God, as sunlight proceeding from the sun.
 

 
 Very image of his substance. The exact reproduction of the divine nature.
 

 
 Purification. Washing away, cleansing.  See  Leviticus 16:30 Hebrews 9:12 Hebrews 10:12 I Peter 2:24 .

title: Hebrews 1:5
text: Son. No angel is ever spoken of in either the Old or the New Testament in the sense here meant in the quotation from  Psalms 2:7 , which applies to the messiah, the Son of God.  On the contrary, angels are commanded to worship the Son.

title: Hebrews 1:8
text: Thy throne, O God, is for ever. In this quotation from  Psalms 45:1-17 Jesus Christ is addressed as God, and the eternity of his dominion is contrasted with that of angels.

title: Hebrews 1:9
text:
Anointed. As a king.
 

 
 Thy fellows. The angels.

title: Hebrews 1:12
text: Thy years shall not fail. Thou are eternal and everlasting.

title: Hebrews 1:14
text: Ministering spirits. Servants of God and of Christ, in behalf of those who accept salvation.

title: Hebrews 2:1
text:
Therefore, etc.  That is, since it is the revelation of God in Christ, which now concerns us instead of the former dispensation in which angels were employed as His ministers, let us give the more earnest heed.
 

 
 To the things that were heard. The gospel truths.

title: Hebrews 2:2
text: Spoken through angels. The Jews considered the word of God in the Old Testament as having been spoken through angels as mediators.  See  Deuteronomy 33:2 Acts 7:53 .  The tradition of the rabbis was that the law came through angels.

title: Hebrews 2:3
text: them that heard. The chosen witnesses.  See  Luke 24:48 Acts 1:8 Acts 1:22 .

title: Hebrews 2:4
text: God also bearing witness. The divine power was manifested through the human agent so that the truth of the message was attested by miracles, gifts of healing, etc.  See  Mark 16:20 Acts 2:43 Acts 19:11 Romans 15:18 Romans 15:19 .

title: Hebrews 2:5
text: The world to come. The new era, the Christian ages ushered in by the life, death, and resurrection of Jesus.

title: Hebrews 2:7
text: A little lower. Man, living in a world of trial and temptation, is for a little while lower than the angels.

title: Hebrews 2:9
text:
A little lower than the angels, even Jesus. Implying the fact of the incarnation of Christ.
 

 
 Taste of death. Through  the bitterness of death Jesus became complete in his sympathy with suffering humanity.

title: Hebrews 2:10
text: It became him, etc.  It was in harmony with the purpose of God that Christ should become the perfect Saviour of mankind through suffering.

title: Hebrews 2:11
text: All of one. God. Jesus, by nature the Son of God, and Christians, made holy through Christ, have one spiritual Father.

title: Hebrews 2:14
text: Had the power of death. Satan has the permitted, subordinate power of death in so far as he tempts men to sin, which ends in death.  ( Romans 5:12 Romans 6:23 I Corinthians 15:56 ).

title: Hebrews 2:16
text: Help to the seed of Abraham. But not because help as to be denied to the Gentiles.  'Help' means here that the Jews were favored by the fact that Jesus was born of their race.

title: Hebrews 2:17
text: Merciful and faithful high priest. When he offered himself as a voluntary sacrifice upon the cross.  See  Hebrews 9:24 Hebrews 9:25  and notes thereon; also the high-priestly prayer of Jesus ( John 17:1-26 ).

title: Hebrews 3:1
text:
Wherefore. That is, in view of what has been already said.
 

 
 Holy brethren. See note  Hebrews 2:11 .
 

 
 Heavenly calling.  To the higher life of the spirit. ( Philippians 3:14 I Thessalonians 4:7 .)
 

 
 Apostle and High Priest. Jesus Christ was both the Apostle , or one sent, from God to man, and the High Priest, or representative, in behalf of man before God.

title: Hebrews 3:2
text: His house. God's house, which in the broadest sense may be taken to mean the Church of God, the community of saints through faith in Christ. 'God's house' conveyed a familiar and suggestive meaning to the Jews, who inherited the patriarchal tradition according to which every Hebrew was named according to his father's house; for example, son of Levi.  The revelation which was given through Moses to Israel as a discipline preparation was known as the old covenant; that which came through Christ is the new covenant.  Israel entered God's house through the revelation to Moses; we must enter through Christ ( John 10:9 ).

title: Hebrews 3:5
text:
Servant. Not to be taken in the sense of slave.  It means one who willingly renders service.
 

 
 Testimony. To be a witness to the revelation made by God through the law; also as one who typified and foreshadowed the fuller revelation that was to come.

title: Hebrews 3:6
text:
Christ as a son. Showing Christ's supremacy; the contrast is between the authority of a son, set over a house, and the dependence of a servant.
 

 
 Glorying of our hope. The Jewish converts to whom this epistle was written were in the deepest despondency and needed encouragement.  The 'Hope' was that Christ would soon come again.

title: Hebrews 3:7
text: The Holy Spirit saith. See  Mark 12:36 Acts 1:16 II Peter 1:21 .

title: Hebrews 3:8
text:
Provocation. As at Meribah ( Exodus 17:1-7 ).
 

 
 Trial. As at Massah ( Numbers 20:1-13 ).

title: Hebrews 3:11
text: My rest. The rest promised by God to Israel in its earthly pilgrimage was the land of Canaan, though the spiritual rest for which God intended his people.

title: Hebrews 3:13
text:
To-day. The day of opportunity.
 

 
 Deceitfulness of sin. The false though plausible reasons by which the Jewish converts were in danger of being beguiled from their belief in Christ.

title: Hebrews 3:16
text: All they that come. Caleb, Joshua, Levites-all these entered into the promised land.  Here they are overlooked, being so few among the many who failed.

title: Hebrews 3:19
text: Unbelief.  Which resulted in disobedience.

title: Hebrews 4:1
text: A promise being left. That is, a promise of whose benefits advantage may be taken by those who will.

title: Hebrews 4:2
text:
Good tidings. The promise of rest for Christian souls; not the rest of inactivity but of soul peace in the midst of world-strife; the peace which Christians have learned to make in and for themselves, and which depends upon the peace of God.  See note on  Matthew 5:9 .
 

 
 Not united by faith. The word of God was not assimilated by them as spiritual food, and therefore did not strengthen or 'profit' them.

title: Hebrews 4:3
text: Works were finished. See  Genesis 2:2 .

title: Hebrews 4:8
text: If Joshua had given them rest, etc.  If the land of Canaan had been all that was promised, David would not have spoken of a rest.

title: Hebrews 4:9
text: A Sabbath rest. That is, there remains a rest unexhausted and unrealized, a rest of which the land of Canaan and the Sabbath are types.  It begins with the spiritual peace which comes from God through faith in Christ.

title: Hebrews 4:12
text: Word of God. Not merely the written law, no the 'Word'  as described by the apostle John ( Hebrews 1:1 ), but the spiritual power proceeding from God and speaking in and to the hearts of men, as actively in the world to-day as in olden times.  Like a two-edged sword it pierces through outer appearances and lays bare the inmost motives, intentions and feelings.  The reading of a single verse or of one of the gospel narratives has often changed a life.

title: Hebrews 4:14
text: The heavens. According to Jewish belief the blue dome of the heavens was a curtain spread over the earth; beyond  this were other heavens and the throne of the Almighty.  Jesus, our high priest, is here declared to have passed through the heavens, that is, into the presence of God ( Hebrews 9:24 II Corinthians 12:2 ).

title: Hebrews 4:15
text: Our infirmities. However exalted in glory, Jesus, our great high priest, is near to us in his love and sympathy and bears with our weaknesses, if we are trying to grow stronger.

title: Hebrews 4:16
text: Boldness. A rebuke to the timid who pray for much while expecting little, and who at times are not willing to make the sacrifice to be all that we ask God to make us.

title: Hebrews 5:1
text:
High priest. In Old Testament times, the priest represented the people before God.  He alone entered the Holy of Holies.  In like manner Jesus Christ represents and intercedes for us, having entered into the immediate presence of God.
 

 
 Among men.  The feeling of human brotherhood was the first necessary qualification of a Jewish high priest.  In this and subsequent chapters of this epistle, the Levitical high-priesthood is compared with the eternal high-priesthood of Christ.
 

 
 For men. For the benefit of men in all that pertains to spiritual welfare.

title: Hebrews 5:4
text: No man taketh the honor. The sons of Aaron were priests by hereditary right.  Aaron did not assume the duties of his office until he was called of God.

title: Hebrews 5:6
text:
Thou art a priest. God ordained Jesus to his work.
 

 
 After the order of Melchizedek. This mysterious person appears but once in ancient history as both a  king and a priest.  He was not a Hebrew; so that his priesthood was by special divine appointment.

title: Hebrews 5:8
text: Obedience. Through all the experiences of his life, Christ manifested the obedience of a son who gladly surrenders his will to the will of his father ( Luke 22:42 ).

title: Hebrews 5:9
text: Eternal salvation. Jesus perfectly identified himself with us in all that we must endure, yet he sinned not.  Hence he becomes the Saviour to give us help continually in every time of need.  The Levitical priest could offer but momentary relief by repeated sacrifices.  See  Hebrews 9:12  and note thereon.

title: Hebrews 5:12
text:
By reason of the time. That is, considering the length of time they had been Christians.  Christ requires growth in personal religion. If we do not progress, our sincerity may well be doubted.
 

 
 Oracles of God. The truth as given to man by Christ and his apostles.

title: Hebrews 5:13
text: Babe. Those to whom the epistle was written had remained in spiritual infancy when they should have become full-grown Christians, able to instruct others.

title: Hebrews 6:1
text:
Not laying again a foundation. Do not be content to live continually in the basement of Christian experience.  Ascend the heights of faith and spiritual fruitfulness.  The foundation, though necessary, is not the most useful or beautiful part of a building, and this is equally true of Christian character.
 

 
 Dead works. Without the living spirit of love; mere formal actions.

title: Hebrews 6:4
text: Tasted of the heavenly gift. Made it a spiritual possession by experience.

title: Hebrews 6:5
text: The age to come. Referring to those who had had a foretaste of the spiritual fruition to which continual faith in God's promises would have led them.

title: Hebrews 6:6
text: Crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh. The actual crucifiers of Christ condemned him as a deceiver; they who continuously reject him confirm the judgment of his hating and unbelieving murderers.

title: Hebrews 6:7
text: Bringeth forth herbs. The fruitful field, like the fruitful Christian character, is blessed of God.  Fruitfulness in scripture is ever a symbol of blessedness.

title: Hebrews 6:8
text: Thorns and thistles. better no labor and no rain than to have turned all good received to evil ends.   Hebrews 6:7 Hebrews 6:8  contain the blessing and the warning concerning the use and misuse respectively of the gifts mentioned in  Hebrews 6:4 Hebrews 6:5 .  See  Romans 2:4-9 .

title: Hebrews 6:9
text:
Beloved. A warmly affectionate greeting given to remind the readers of the epistle that the rebukes and warnings were only meant to bring back erring Christians to their first faith.
 

 
 Accompany salvation. Spiritual aids to salvation; the humility and obedience that lead through faith to salvation.

title: Hebrews 6:10
text: God is not unrighteous to forget, etc.  He holds in loving remembrance the deeds done in obedience to Him.  There is a conservation of virtue in the spiritual world, even as there is a conservation of energy in the natural world.  See  II Corinthians 8:24 Colossians 1:4 .

title: Hebrews 6:11
text: Fulness of hope. Let your anxiety to attain fulness of spiritual maturity in your own experience equal that eagerness you have shown in ministering to others.

title: Hebrews 6:13
text: Abraham. See  Genesis 22:16 .

title: Hebrews 6:15
text: Obtained the promise. See  Genesis 22:16-18 .

title: Hebrews 6:18
text: Immutable things.  God's promise and God's oath ( Hebrews 6:13 Hebrews 6:17 ).

title: Hebrews 6:19
text:
Anchor of the soul. The symbol of hope.
 

 
 Within the veil. Just as the anchor has its holding ground in unseen depths, so the Christian's hope, his anchor, is flung out into the unseen region of eternal things.  Between us and the fulfillment of our hopes there is a veil, as there was in the tabernacle of the Old Testament, beyond which the high priest passed on the Day of Atonement ( Leviticus 16:2 Leviticus 16:12-17 ).  So Jesus Christ, the eternal high priest, has entered within the veil, having risen from the dead.

title: Hebrews 7:1
text:
Melchizedek. The name means King of righteousness.  A mysterious person appearing but once in the Old Testament ( Genesis 14:18-20 ), here introduced as a priest of a higher order than that of Aaron.  His priesthood was typical
 
of the eternal priesthood of Christ.

title: Hebrews 7:3
text: Without father, without mother. The priestly office of the sons of Aaron and the Levites was theirs by inheritance, not by any inherent holiness of life.  But Melchizedek had no priestly pedigree, and in this respect resembled Christ.

title: Hebrews 7:16
text:
Carnal commandment. Not according to the law of natural or physical descent, as in the Aaronic priesthood.
 

 
 Power of an endless life. A sentence implying that the priesthood of Jesus is his by virtue of his being the Son of God who liveth forever.

title: Hebrews 7:18
text: A disannulling of a foregoing commandment. The old testament was a stepping stone from discipline to something new and better.  The Mosaic code could not but fail to bring men into complete reconciliation with God.  This could only be done by spiritual contact with God through faith in Jesus Christ.

title: Hebrews 7:19
text: Better hope. Historical manifestation of Christ as spiritual Saviour of mankind.

title: Hebrews 7:24
text: Unchangeable. He ever liveth to intercede for us.  Our love and service vary; he abideth faithful.

title: Hebrews 7:25
text: The uttermost. From the lowest depths to the greatest heights; salvation from the guilt and power of sin.  See  John 6:37-39 Romans 8:34 Jude 1:24 .

title: Hebrews 7:26
text:
Became us. The Son of God met and answered the needs of those to whom he came.
 

 
 Holy. Entirely consecrated and set apart in voluntary obedience to the will of God.
 

 
 Guileless. Harmless without deceit.
 

 
 Undefiled. Pure and clean as touching the requirements of the ceremonial law.

title: Hebrews 7:28
text: Perfected.  Christ met every test and fulfilled every requirement the law could demand.  By his life, his suffering, his death, and his resurrection he became the perfect reconciler of mankind to God, and the perfect Saviour.

title: Hebrews 8:1
text: Throne of the Majesty in the heavens. An expression equivalent to 'at the right hand of God.'  'In the heavens' is 'in the highest places.' See  Luke 2:14 Ephesians 1:20 .

title: Hebrews 8:2
text: True tabernacle. The original, ideal, spiritual tabernacle, of which the tabernacle of the Old Testament was but a type, a symbol, or a shadow.  God prepared the Hebrew mind for the conception of a spiritual household by a material symbol thereof.

title: Hebrews 8:6
text: Better covenant. A covenant of universal forgiveness for mankind, and written in the human heart, as contrasted with a covenant of strict obedience embodied in commandments written on tables of stone.  Under the new covenant, love to God as revealed in Christ, gives life to Christian service.  The letter of the old law led to dead formalism.

title: Hebrews 8:8
text: He saith, etc.  God speaking through his prophet Jeremiah ( Jeremiah 31:31-34 ).

title: Hebrews 8:10
text:
After those days. After the old had been done away and Christ had ushered in the new.
 

 
 My laws into their mind. No longer a formal code commanding obedience, but an inner spirit of life.  There shall be an inspiration born of love rather than a command.

title: Hebrews 8:11
text: They shall not teach every man. The old covenant was national; the new shall be individual.  Every man shall have the new life in his heart by faith in Jesus Christ.

title: Hebrews 8:12
text: I will be merciful, etc.  A gracious and free forgiveness of sins, even the blotting out of the remembrance of them.  See  Romans 11:27 Romans 11:32 .

title: Hebrews 8:13
text: A new covenant. The prophet saw in vision a better day, with the old legal covenant superseded, and the new covenant of God's grace begun.

title: Hebrews 9:1
text: Sanctuary of this world. The holy tent of the tabernacle was an earthly sign of the heavenly, and was to symbolize divine truths.  In  Hebrews 9:1-28  and  Hebrews 10:1-38  the contrast between the old and new covenants is further heightened.

title: Hebrews 9:2
text:
Tabernacle. Tent.  The tabernacle had an outer chamber, the Holy Place; and an inner chamber, the Holy of Holies ( Exodus 26:1-37 ). Before each chamber there was a curtain.
 

 
 Candlestick. Lampstand ( Exodus 25:31-40 ).
 

 
 Table.  Exodus 25:23-30 .
 

 
 Showbread. Bread set before the presence of God ( Exodus 25:30 ).

title: Hebrews 9:3
text: Second veil. The second curtain.  The first curtain being before the Holy Place.

title: Hebrews 9:4
text:
Altar of incense. On this the high priest burned incense, without which he could not enter the Holy of Holies ( Leviticus 16:12 ).
 

 
 Ark of the covenant. See  Exodus 25:10-22 .
 

 
 Pot holding the manna. See  Exodus 16:32-34 .
 

 
 Aaron's rod. See  Numbers 17:1-10 .

title: Hebrews 9:5
text: Cherubim. Winged figures symbolical of God's presence, which guard the place of Jehovah's glory.  See  Exodus 25:17-22 .

title: Hebrews 9:6
text: First tabernacle. See note on  Hebrews 9:2 .  Into the Holy Place the people could not enter, so that men were denied access to God except through priests.

title: Hebrews 9:7
text: High Priest alone. To one man, the high priest, was given the privilege of beholding the Glory of God.  How far separated were the common people from their God!

title: Hebrews 9:9
text: Figure. In time the Jews realized that all the machinery of their ritual was but a preparation for spiritual realities.

title: Hebrews 9:11
text:
Good things to come. The eternal realities of which the old covenant was the shadow.
 

 
 Not of this creation. The tent or sanctuary was earthly, of human manufacture.

title: Hebrews 9:12
text: His own blood. The high priest, cleanses symbolically by the blood of animals, entered the Holy of Holies to atone for the people.  Christ by his voluntary sacrifice on the cross entered heaven, having made atonement once for all for sin. See  Ephesians 1:7 .

title: Hebrews 9:14
text: Dead works. All works done in a slavish spirit, merely to comply with legal requirements, are dead.

title: Hebrews 9:15
text: Transgressions that were under the first covenant. God was merciful to those who died before Christ came.  The virtue of his reconciling sacrifice extends back to the Old Testament saints who lived in faith, looking forward to a perfect revelation of God's love in Christ.

title: Hebrews 9:16
text: Testament. A will.

title: Hebrews 9:20
text: Blood of the covenant. Covenants sealed with blood were common in the early age of the Jewish people.  Often in the Middle Ages of Europe men signed covenants with their blood. This added to the sacredness and surety of the contract.  So God's covenant with his people was sealed with the blood of clean animals, symbolizing the voluntary sacrifice of Christ which sealed his final covenant with man.

title: Hebrews 9:22
text: Shedding of blood. Blood was the symbol of life, and underneath the whole Jewish ritual was the idea that the life of men was forfeited to God because of sin. Blood, representing life, was therefore offered in sacrifice as an atonement for sins.  See  Leviticus 17:11 Luke 22:20 .

title: Hebrews 9:23
text: Heavenly things. The spiritual sanctuary into which Christ has gone, with its heavenly realities corresponding to the symbols of the Levitical sanctuary.

title: Hebrews 9:24
text: Before the face of God. That is, in the immediate presence of God instead of in the Holy of Holies of an earthly and temporary tabernacle, which was only a symbol of that presence.  Moreover, Christ's mediation for all mankind is continuous, eternal (Heb 7.25); the Levitical high priest appeared in behalf of the Jewish people only once a year.  Humanity, therefore, is ever present in the compassionate mind of the risen Christ, who is in the eternal presence of the father.

title: Hebrews 9:26
text: End of the ages. The expiration of the time during which the Levitical priesthood served as a mediator between God and the chosen people; or, from a more comprehensive point of view, the beginning of the new time when God revealed himself in Jesus Christ to mankind ( Hebrews 1:1 Hebrews 1:2 I Corinthians 10:11 ).

title: Hebrews 9:27
text: Once to die. Death ends the probationary  or preparatory stage of man's career; then comes his judgment, which is here to be distinguished from the judgment of the world, mentioned in  Acts 17:31 .

title: Hebrews 9:28
text: So Christ also. Death also ended the earthly part of Christ's mission as the revealer of God to mankind and the Saviour from sin, he awaits the fruits of his work, the people, and so apart from sin he shall come again.

title: Hebrews 10:1
text: Shadow. The law was a preparation for Christ.  It instilled into the minds of the Jewish people religious conceptions on which Christ could build.  It was not final but a shadow, a foretaste, a beginning that was to lead men to the truth as revealed in Jesus Christ.

title: Hebrews 10:10
text:
Sanctified. Cleansed from the impurity of sin. All believers are saints, holy, or sanctified, if considered as set apart or consecrated to the service of God ( John 17:19 Ephesians 1:4 ); but from the point of view of growth in spiritual power, sanctification is progress toward perfection, and a process due to the indwelling of the Holy Spirit ( Romans 15:16 ).
 

 
 Through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ. This points out the reason why we also should offer our bodies 'a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your spiritual service' ( Romans 12:1 ).

title: Hebrews 10:11
text: Day by day. The long-continued, wearisome routine of the sacrificial system was spiritually impotent for the eradication of sin.  The clear perception of this caused Paul to cry out, 'Wretched man that I am! Who shall deliver me out of the body of this death?' ( Romans 7:24 ).

title: Hebrews 10:12
text: One sacrifice for sins. A sacrifice which is pure, holy and effectual for all who accept it.

title: Hebrews 10:14
text: Perfected. The offering under the Levitical law was an act at a definite, prescribed time.  The perfecting of men is gradual, progressing from age to age under the guidance of the Holy Spirit.  See  Hebrews 7:11 Hebrews 7:25 .

title: Hebrews 10:16
text: My laws on their heart. Which could only be under the covenant of forgiveness.  When the laws of God are written on, and are active in, the hearts of mankind, obedience is glad and willing.

title: Hebrews 10:19
text: Boldness. How much of fear and trembling before God there was in the Old Testament! Mount Sinai, the place of His appearing, was wrapped in thunder clouds and illumined by lightnings. God was distant and terrible.  Under the Levitical law the worshipper was not allowed to enter the Holy of Holies in the tabernacle; but the voluntary sacrifice of Jesus Christ has procured for the believer the privilege of entering, and with boldness, the Holy Place of God's presence.

title: Hebrews 10:22
text: Our hearts sprinkled. A sprinkling of spiritual power in contrast to the outward sprinkling of the body.  The writer of the epistle here speaks as if the age of ceremonial purity in religion had passed away and a new era of inward purity had begun.  See  Exodus 29:21 Leviticus 8:30 I Peter 1:2 .

title: Hebrews 10:23
text: The confession of our hope. The hope of eternal salvation by faith in Jesus Christ.

title: Hebrews 10:25
text:
Assembling together.  Words which suggest that public worship is a privilege, and that Christianity is a religion for society, not thriving best in isolated lives.
 

 
 The day. The expected second coming of Christ.

title: Hebrews 10:26
text: Sin wilfully. The deliberate choice of sin and a persistent life of sin, which ultimately prevent the indwelling of the Holy Spirit.  The words do not refer to sins done wilfully, but of which the sinner afterward repents.

title: Hebrews 10:29
text:
Trodden underfoot. The strongest figurative expression to an oriental mind.
 

 
 Done despite. Insulted.

title: Hebrews 10:30
text: Vengeance belongeth unto me. God alone can punish justly.  Human vengeance is often based on pride, or selfishness, or prejudice.  The certainty and justice of the punishment are based on the righteous nature of God.

title: Hebrews 10:32
text: Former days. An appeal to what is best and most praiseworthy in a man's past is the best incentive to a worthy present and future.

title: Hebrews 10:33
text: Partakers. Sympathy and love for one another were so strong in the early church that when one suffered all suffered.

title: Hebrews 10:37
text: Very little while. The prophet preached that only firm confidence in God could enable a righteous man to confront life's difficulties. Here the writer of this epistle quotes from Habakkuk in order to strengthen the faith of his readers.  He says in effect: As faith in God was necessary in the prophet's time, so it is now; but you have the hope of the near coming of Christ to help you to remain stedfast.

title: Hebrews 11:1
text:
Assurance. Faith, the root and inspiring principle of all true religion, is an internal confidence of the truth and reality of things hoped for.
 

 
 Conviction. Faith, or the spiritual acceptance of unseen realities, amounts to a conviction of their existence.  Progress in faith intensifies this conviction of their existence. After faith has been triumphantly tested by experience, the believer has new evidence, as it were, of unseen things.  In this chapter the writer of the epistle shows how faith had been the great factor of spiritual life in the history of Israel.

title: Hebrews 11:2
text:
Elders. The early Jewish fathers and patriarchs ( Hebrews 1:1 ).
 

 
 Had witness. Commendation from God and their fellow-men.

title: Hebrews 11:4
text: Abel. Whose sacrifice was acceptable because it was offered in the right spirit ( Genesis 4:4-7 ).

title: Hebrews 11:5
text: Enoch. Whose faith was mature-full and rich by reason of his constant communion with God.

title: Hebrews 11:7
text:
Noah. His faith was founded on a reverential heed to God's word; it was the faith of godly fear.  See  Genesis 6:14-22 .
 

 
 Condemned the world. By his righteous obedience, which reproved the wicked.

title: Hebrews 11:8
text: Abraham. His was the childlike faith of implicit trust, which grew and expanded with each new experience.

title: Hebrews 11:9
text: Sojourner. Realizing that he was called to a land of promise, he did not settle down and build a city.

title: Hebrews 11:13
text: Died in faith. Their faith remained stedfast in the hour of death, even although they had not yet received the promised fruition.

title: Hebrews 11:16
text: Not ashamed of them. On the contrary, God called himself the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

title: Hebrews 11:17
text: Abraham, being tried. Apparently to the last point of human capacity and endurance.  Without this test triumphantly met he would not have been called 'father of the faithful.' His faith, at first ready and childlike, after this grew to be mature and fearless.

title: Hebrews 11:19
text: In a figure.  Isaac was actually surrendered to death; actual death could not have increased the trial of his father's faith.  Figuratively he was dead, and from death he returned.

title: Hebrews 11:21
text: Jacob, when he was dying. Even in extreme physical weakness his spirit, through faith, was strong and hopeful.  Because of this he could transmit to his sons the blessing of God's promise not realized in his life.  Three generations had elapsed since God had made this promise; no possibility of a present fulfilment appeared, and yet these faithful ones passed on to their children the blessing of the promise as of greater value than their gold and silver.

title: Hebrews 11:23
text: A goodly child. Because of the beauty and manifest promise of their child the parents felt that God had something great in store for him; so they dared to disobey the king.

title: Hebrews 11:24
text: Moses. His faith was proved by his actions. Because Israel was God's chosen people, he resigned all his honors as an Egyptian prince, and all the pleasures of a life of ease.  He chose to suffer a reproach similar to that which Christ endured for the sake of saving his people.  See  Hebrews 13:13 Romans 15:3 .

title: Hebrews 11:28
text: Passover. See note on  Matthew 26:17 .  Moses knew that the sprinkling of blood had no power to deliver from death, yet he obeyed God's command, believing that He would deliver his people.

title: Hebrews 11:31
text: Rahab. See  Joshua 2:1-21 Joshua 6:23 .

title: Hebrews 11:32
Hebrews 11:35
text:
Resurrection.  The widow of Sarepta ( I Kings 17:17-24 ) and the Shunamite ( II Kings 4:32-37 ) both received their dead back to life because of their faith.
 

 
 Others were tortured. The writer now has in view the sufferings of the age after the Old Testament history was closed.
 

 
 A better resurrection. To eternal life, as contrasted with the resurrection to an earthly life, previously mentioned in this verse.

title: Hebrews 11:37
text: They were stoned. Stoning was a common Jewish method of punishing heretics.  Stephen was stoned.  According to tradition Jeremiah was stoned.

title: Hebrews 12:1
text: Compassed about. Referring to the illustrious heroes of faith spoken of in the preceding chapter.  They had borne witness to the truth in their earthly life; they had now become heavenly witnesses, or spectators, or the struggles of those who were contending for the eternal reward.

title: Hebrews 12:2
text: Looking unto Jesus. Faithfully modeling character after the perfect example of Jesus.

title: Hebrews 12:4
text: Resisted into blood. They had not yet faced death for the sake of holiness.  Nor do men to-day face death, as Christ did, for the sake of truth.  Conditions have changed.  The usual results of truth-speaking and of action in conformity to unwelcome truth are now ridicule, unpopularity, loss of reputation, business, wealth, social standing.

title: Hebrews 12:7
text: Chastening. The discipline of suffering, patiently endured and hence leading to richer and nobler character.

title: Hebrews 12:9
text:
Father of Spirits. God, the Father of our spirits.
 

 
 And live.  Obedience to God is life.

title: Hebrews 12:12
text: Lift up. Comfort and cheer the downcast and sorrowing.

title: Hebrews 12:13
text: Make straight paths. Smooth, level paths, free from obstructions that may cause to stumble those who are weaker than ourselves.

title: Hebrews 12:15
text: Root of bitterness.  See  Deuteronomy 29:18 .

title: Hebrews 12:16
text: Profane person, as Esau. Esau had no proper appreciation of his birthright, inasmuch as he had not thought of the spiritual blessing that accompanied it.

title: Hebrews 12:18
text: Mount that might be touched. Mount Sinai.  See  Exodus 19:12 Exodus 19:1 Exodus 18:1-27 Exodus 18:19 Exodus 20:18 Deuteronomy 4:11 . The mount that might be touched was Mount Sinai on earth.  Here God was distant, fearful, the God of the thunder and the black clouds.  We are come up to a mountain invisible yet real, where heaven meets earth and God communes with his people.

title: Hebrews 12:20
text: If even a best touch the mountain, etc. A fact which illustrated the rigor necessary in compelling reverence for sacred things, and affording a contrast between the Mosaic law and the grace and freedom which came through Christ.

title: Hebrews 12:21
text: So fearful. 'Fearful' is an accurate description of the Hebrew mind in its attitude toward God as revealed in the early history of Israel.

title: Hebrews 12:22
text: Mount Zion. The great contrast to Mount Sinai.  Mount Zion is the mount of the New Testament age, and an emblem of all its spiritual blessings.

title: Hebrews 12:23
text: General assembly and church, etc.  The gathering of all God's children, including those in the visible church on earth and the church invisible in heaven.

title: Hebrews 12:24
text: Better than that of Abel. The blood of Abel spoke from the ground with a cry for vengeance; Christ's blood speaks of love, mercy, and pardon.

title: Hebrews 12:27
text: Yet once more, etc.  The temporal things shall pass away.  The eternal shall remain.

title: Hebrews 12:28
text: Let us have grace. Feel and express thankfulness.

title: Hebrews 13:2
text:
Strangers. There was then no feeling of international brotherhood  such as has since been manifested; but there was a solid preparation for it in Roman citizenship, which created a community of interest throughout that vast empire.
 

 
 Angels unawares. See  Genesis 18:2-22 Judges 6:11 .

title: Hebrews 13:3
text: Bonds. Already the Christians were suffering persecution.

title: Hebrews 13:4
text: God will judge. Alluding to the impossibility of escaping punishment for a sin which human judgment and penalty so often fail to overtake because of its secrecy.

title: Hebrews 13:5
text: Content. This is no condoning of indolence or lack of rightful ambition.  But even trifling discontent may blind one to God's blessings, and rob one of all enjoyment.

title: Hebrews 13:7
text: Issue of their life. The way they kept their faith and holy living even until death.

title: Hebrews 13:9
text: Strange teachings. The doctrines of those who were trying to establish in the early church certain ceremonial practices of the Mosaic law.  They were probably connected with the sacrificial meals ( Hebrews 13:10 ).

title: Hebrews 13:10
text: No right to eat. Referring to those who sought spiritual strength by sacrificial offerings or ceremonial purity, according to the old and superseded service of the tabernacle.  These had no right to eat at the Christian altar; that is, they had not accepted the salvation by faith which came to them by the voluntary sacrifice of Christ.

title: Hebrews 13:12
text: Without the gate. See  John 19:17 .

title: Hebrews 13:15
text: A sacrifice of praise. See  Psalms 116:17 I Peter 2:3 I Peter 2:11 .

title: Hebrews 13:16
text: Communicate. Contribute, be generous in ministering to the necessities of the saints ( Romans 15:26 ).

title: Hebrews 13:19
text: Be restored. That the present exile of the writer of the epistle from his readers may soon end.

title: Hebrews 13:20
text:
God of peace. The God Who alone can give spiritual peace.
 

 
 Brought again from the dead. The resurrection of Jesus Christ.
 

 
 With the blood of an eternal covenant. See  Hebrews 9:15-18 .

title: Hebrews 13:22
text: Bear with the word of exhortation. Read and ponder patiently and prayerfully the words of this epistle.

title: Hebrews 13:23
text: Timothy. This is the only reference which proves that Timothy was ever imprisoned.

title: Hebrews 13:24
text:
All them. The epistle was addressed to certain Christian communities as a whole, not to their rulers.
 

 
 They of Italy. Italian residents in the place where the writer of the epistle lived.

title: James 1:2
text: Count it all joy. The true view of temptation or trial is that it is an opportunity to gain new strength through overcoming.

title: James 1:3
text: The proving of your faith worketh patience. Here proving has the sense of testing; and patience implies not a mere wilted submission, but the cheerful turning to good account of every untoward circumstance and event.

title: James 1:4
text: Perfect and entire. The work of patience is toward completeness, as expressed in a well-rounded character.

title: James 1:5
text:
Wisdom. The wisdom here designated is the understanding of the things of God, as distinguished from that wisdom of the world which is foolishness with God ( I Corinthians 3:19 ).
 

 
 And upbraideth not. The text here expresses the great long-suffering of God whose giving must be limited by the degree of desire and willingness to accept on the part of those who ask.

title: James 1:6
text: Nothing doubting. Doubt, either as to the value of the gift or the power of the Giver, must weaken faith.

title: James 1:9
text: Glory in his high estate. The condition of freedom from the distractions of great possessions ( Matthew 19:22 ), becomes a high estate through singleness of heart and purpose.

title: James 1:10
text: And the rich, in that he is made low. The empty vessel is prepared to receive the larger blessing.

title: James 1:11
text: So also shall the rich man fade away in his goings. The idea of possession cannot endure longer than the riches upon which it is based, and which are here compared to the grass that withereth.  With the perception that his possessions are not enduring riches, the belief that he is a rich man fadeth away.

title: James 1:12
text: The crown of life. Life here is used in the same sense as in  John 17:3 : 'And this is life eternal, that they should know thee the only true God, and him whom thou didst send, even Jesus Christ.' The enduring of temptation advances the knowledge of God through the confirming of faith in His righteousness.

title: James 1:13
text:
A Servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ. The term servant is used not in any sense of servitude, but rather as expressing consecrated devotion, springing from the full acceptance of the gospel as the truth.
 

 
 Despersion. The body of the Jews then scattered throughout the Roman Empire.

title: James 1:14
text: Drawn away by his own lust. The word lust ahs here its wider significance, of all desire toward sense gratification as used in  I John 2:16 I John 2:17 : 'For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh and the lust of the eyes and the vainglory of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.  And the world passeth away and the lust thereof.'

title: James 1:17
text: The Father of lights. The source of all intelligence.

title: James 1:18
text: A kind of firstfruits of his creatures. In the old Jewish worship the firstfruits of the harvest were consecrated to God ( Leviticus 23:10 ).  Being brought forth by the word of truth, we are the first of God's creatures to know ourselves His children and voluntarily to consecrate ourselves the firstfruits of understanding.

title: James 1:25
text: The law of liberty. This distinction is more clearly stated by Paul in  Romans 8:2 : 'For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus made me free from the law of sin and death.'

title: James 2:1
text: The Lord of glory. In the presence of the very Lord of glory, how utterly vain and foolish appear the honors conferred through respect of persons.

title: James 2:2
text: A man with a gold ring. This was a fashion borrowed from the luxurious Romans, and aping their vanity and self-importance.

title: James 2:5
text: Poor as to the world. The phrase means more than the mere accident of temporal poverty.  It relates rather to indifferences as to worldly possessions, and is qualified by the final words of the verse; 'them that love him.'

title: James 2:16
text: Be ye warmed and filled; and yet ye give them not the things needful. This is a condemnation of the prayer of mere words, which stops short of the practical, effectual prayer expressed in deeds.

title: James 2:21
text: Was not Abraham our father justified by works? Compare  Genesis 22:1-13 .

title: James 2:25
text: And in like manner was not also Rahab the harlot justified? See  Joshua 2:1-21 Joshua 6:22-25 .

title: James 3:6
text: Which defileth the whole body. Compare the words of Jesus (Mt 15.18-20): 'But the things which proceed out of the mouth come forth out of the heart; and they defile the man.  For out of the heart come forth evil thoughts, murder, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, railings: these are the things which defile the man.

title: James 4:2
text: Ye kill, and covet. The word 'kill' is to be taken in the sense of the hatred proceeding from envy, as in  I John 3:15 : 'whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer.'

title: James 5:3
text: Your gold and your silver are rusted; and their rust shall be for a testimony against you.  The picture is drawn prophetically.  The treasures of earth are described as already perished and their very corruption as evidence that they were wrongly chosen - in that they were not of the 'perfect gifts from above.'

title: James 5:7
text: Be patient, therefore, brethren. In this verse James turns from his accusation of the rich to exhort his fellow Christians to patience even in the face of evil conditions, which the coming of the Lord will change.

title: James 5:12
text: But above all things, my brethren, swear not. The injunction here is against a habit prevailing among the Jews of attempting to establish truth, or the appearance of truth, by an oath.  See  Matthew 23:16-22 Mark 14:71 .  The indwelling Spirit of truth ( I John 4:6 ) is the only and the sufficient source of right speaking.

title: James 5:14
text: Anointing him with oil, in the name of the Lord. The use of oil in ancient times was very common as a remedy in sickness.

title: James 5:16
text: Pray one for another, that ye may be healed. Lest there be any doubt as to the answering of the prayer of the righteous man, James cites the power of Elijah ( I Kings 17:1 I Kings 18:1 I Kings 18:42-45 ).

title: I Peter 1:1
text:
Elect. Christians, or saints ( Acts 19:3 ), because chosen or called out from the world.  See  Matthew 24:22 Matthew 24:24 Romans 8:33 II Timothy 2:10 .
 

 
 Sojourners of dispersion. An expression applied originally to Jews outside of Palestine, but in this passage referring to Christians, whether Jews or Gentiles, who had become strangers in every land.
 

 
 Pontus. A Roman province of Asia Minor, lying along the coast of the Black Sea.
 

 
 Galatia. A Roman province in the central part of Asia Minor.
 

 
 Cappadocia. An inland Roman province of Asia Minor, lying east of Galatia and south of Pontus.
 

 
 Asia. The Roman province of that name, governed by a proconsul.  It lay along the coast of the Mediterranean Sea and of the Aegean Sea, and included the districts of Mysia, Lydia and Carla, together with the greater part of Phrygia.  Asia contained the cities of Ephesus, Smyrna and Pergamos; and in it were the 'seven churches' mentioned in Re 1.4.
 

 
 Bithynia. A Roman province lying along the coast of the Black Sea, and west of Pontus.

title: I Peter 1:2
text:
According to the foreknowledge of God the Father. These words qualify 'elect' in  I Peter 1:1 .  The election or choice of the 'sojourners of the Dispersion' was according to the foreknowledge of God, to Whom all the events of human history, and of his universe, are known from eternity.  Also Peter declared on the day of Pentecost that Jesus was 'delivered up by the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God' ( Acts 2:23 ).  There is nothing to show that the word 'foreknowledge' had any doubtful or forbidding meaning to the early Christians, nor can it have such meaning in view of the fact that God is love ( I John 4:8 ).  The foreknowledge of God is that of the Father Whose purpose from the beginning is to love and have mercy upon mankind.
 

 
 In sanctification of the Spirit. Set apart or consecrated by the Holy Spirit.  See note on  Hebrews 10:10 .  Viewed with reference to perfect holiness, sanctification is a daily growth or process.  We are transformed by the renewing of our minds ( Romans 12:2 ), which involves obedience to Christ's commands, complete self-surrender and the indwelling of the Holy Spirit.
 

 
 Sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ. This refers to the voluntary sacrifice of Jesus Christ on the cross, where his blood was shed for the remission of sins ( Hebrews 12:24 ).

title: I Peter 1:3
text: Begat us again unto a living hope by the resurrection. Regenerated us in the heart by the completed work of Christ.  It is declared that whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is begotten of God ( I John 5:1 ).  Paul's definition of the gospel is, 'that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; and that he was buried and that he hath been raised on the third day according to the scriptures' ( I Corinthians 15:3 I Corinthians 15:4 ).  The resurrection of Jesus Christ is the basic fact of the gospel, which is the seed sown.  See  I Peter 1:23 .

title: I Peter 1:5
text:
Who by the power of God are guarded through faith. See notes on  Hebrews 11:1 .
 

 
 Unto a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time. 'Salvation' probably includes two ideas; (1) It is that salvation on which Paul had not yet laid hold ( Philippians 3:12 Romans 13:11 I Thessalonians 5:8 ), a complete victory over the lower self or the flesh; (2) a deliverance from trial, persecution and sorrow.

title: I Peter 1:7
text: Gold that perisheth though it is proved by fire.  Gold is purified by fire until the dross is burned out; Christians are thus purified by suffering and trials.

title: I Peter 1:10
text:
Salvation the prophets sought. The Old Testament predictions of deliverance, glory and prosperity for Israel as found in the prophets are shown in the New Testament to refer to the salvation and blessedness of believers.
 

 
 Grace that should come unto you. The salvation through Jesus Christ.

title: I Peter 1:11
text:
What time or what manner of time. That is, when Christ should appear and suffer.
 

 
 The Spirit of Christ which was in them. The Holy Spirit.
 

 
 When it testified beforehand the sufferings of Christ. See  Isaiah 53:1-12 Matthew 8:17 I Peter 2:22-24 .

title: I Peter 1:12
text:
To whom it was revealed, etc.  The prophets looked for a Messiah -a suffering Servant- and deliverance and prosperity; but they did not understand how these things were to come to pass. It remained for Jesus and his apostles to show that Jesus and his kingdom were the fulfilment of these prophecies.  Thus they did not minister unto themselves but unto coming ages, even unto the present time.  One of the strongest arguments for the divinity of Jesus is that he fulfilled these prophecies spoken centuries before his coming.  Peter here shows the advantages which Christians had over the prophets of former ages.
 

 
 Which things. The things of which Peter had just written- the suffering and death of Jesus, the salvation of Jew and Gentile, etc.

title: I Peter 1:13
text: The revelation of Jesus Christ. At his final advent, or, the continual revealing or unveiling of the character and glory of Jesus.

title: I Peter 1:18
text: Vain manner of life handed down from your fathers. This life was a consequence of the vanity of an understanding darkened by ignorance and the hardening of the heart for many generations ( Ephesians 4:18 ).

title: I Peter 1:19
text: Lamb without blemish. The reference here is to the Paschal lamb whose blood was sprinkled upon the door posts as a testimony of obedience to the command of Jehovah, and thus a protection from the death which fell upon the Egyptians ( Exodus 12:5 ).

title: I Peter 1:20
text:
Who was foreknown, etc.  See notes on  I Peter 1:2 .
 

 
 At the end of the times. The former times are now at an end because of the 'revelation of Jesus Christ' ( I Peter 1:13 ).  'The old times are passed away' ( II Corinthians 5:17 ).

title: I Peter 1:22
text:
Unfeigned. Genuine; without pretense.
 

 
 The truth. The example and teaching of Jesus and his apostles.

title: I Peter 2:2
text:
Spiritual milk. In the explanatory rendering of the word here translated 'spiritual' the meaning is shown to be 'intellectual' ; that is, appealing to the understanding.
 

 
 Unto salvation. See  I Peter 1:5  and note thereon.

title: I Peter 2:4
text: Living stone. In Peter's defence before the chief priests at Jerusalem ( Acts 4:5-12 ) he spoke of Christ as 'the stone which was set at nought of you, the builders,' in the construction of the Jewish creed.  See also  Matthew 21:42 Ephesians 2:20-22 .

title: I Peter 2:7
text: For such a disbelieve, etc.  In further illustration of the contrast in this verse between those who accept and those who reject the gospel, see  II Corinthians 2:15 II Corinthians 2:16 .

title: I Peter 2:8
text: Stumble at the word, being disobedient 'Word' here signifies the truth as it is in Christ.  Disobedience  is practically denial of the truth, which remains unchangeable. It must humble the proud who are its enemies ( Proverbs 16:18 ).

title: I Peter 2:10
text: Who in time past were no people. The Christians for whom the epistle is written are here reminded that they were once like Israel in the time of its alienation from God; or like Gentiles before they accepted Christ.  See  Hosea 1:6-9 Hosea 2:1 Hosea 2:23 .

title: I Peter 2:16
text: As free. That is, free from the law of Moses and the tradition of the elders, because not under the old covenant.  Peter cautioned them not to use their freedom as license, since they were under the obligation of the higher law of loyalty to their master.

title: I Peter 2:18
text: With all fear. Here fear does not mean terror, but deep anxiety lest in some respect service might fall short of a perfect fulfilment of each duty.

title: I Peter 2:24
text:
Bare our sins in his body upon the tree. This refers to the death of Jesus on the cross for the sins of the world.  See  Colossians 1:21 Colossians 1:22 Isaiah 53:12 Hebrews 9:28 .
 

 
 Having died unto sins. The phrase signifies the passing into a new life ( John 5:24 Romans 6:2 Romans 6:10 I John 3:14 ).

title: I Peter 3:2
text: Coupled with fear See note on  I Peter 2:18 .

title: I Peter 3:3
text: Braiding the hair, etc.  This was a warning against the extravagant fashions in hair-dressing and decoration with costly jewels, prevailing among the Greeks and Romans at that period; also a reminder that the true adornment is from within.

title: I Peter 3:4
text: Meek and quiet spirit. This implies meekness as toward God, the fountain of all knowledge; and perfect calmness in that knowledge, as toward men.

title: I Peter 3:7
text: That your prayers be not hindered. Lest your approach to God in prayer lack humility and prove unacceptable by reason of your overbearing conduct to those who are weaker than you.

title: I Peter 3:15
text:
Ready always to give answer. This is an admonition toward understanding; something more than blind faith was required.
 

 
 With meekness and fear. The attitude here urged by the apostle is one devoid of boastfulness, and at the same time guarded by an anxious fear lest in the smallest particular we fail to meet fully the situation.

title: I Peter 3:19
text:
, 20
 
 In which also he went and preached, etc.  The interpretation of these two verses depends on whether the word 'spirit' in 1Pe 3.18 refers to the Holy Spirit, or to the eternal element in man which Jesus shared in his human nature.  There are several interpretations, of which the two most important are: (1) that Christ actually descended into Hades and preached to the people who had lived in the days of Noah but were now in Hades; (2) that the Spirit of Christ preached through Noah to those who lived in Noah's time but who were in prison at the time of the writing of this epistle.  Commentators differ widely as to the correct interpretation.

title: I Peter 3:21
text:
Doth now save you, even baptism. Noah's experience in the flood is made a type of baptism.  Through faith Noah obeyed God and was saved when others were lost. Some would interpret this experience  as being typical of the symbolism of baptism, while others would interpret it as meaning that we are actually saved through baptism. The verse must be interpreted in connection with other passages of scripture.
 

 
 Not the putting away, etc.  The interpretation of this passage is unusually difficult.  What is the first question that a newly made believer asks? Paul asked, What shall I do, Lord? ( Acts 22:10 ).  The answer to this question is, Surrender yourself to Christ; become dead to the world and the old life.  Baptism is a symbol of this surrender; it is an act of obedience.  Peter emphasizes this by showing the difference between Christian baptism and the Jewish washings.  The latter were for the removal of outward impurities; Christian baptism is a means ordained of God through which we testify to our faith in the resurrection ( Romans 6:2-11 ).

title: I Peter 4:1
text:
With the same mind. Most probably this means, Look on suffering as Christ did, who was made perfect through suffering ( Hebrews 2:10 ).
 

 
 He that hath suffered in the flesh hath ceased from sin. This teaches the moral value of suffering, in that those who have fellowship with Christ's suffering are weaned from the love of sin.

title: I Peter 4:7
text: The end of all things is at hand. This refers to the second coming of Christ.

title: I Peter 4:10
text: A gift. Probably some gift of the Spirit. See  I Corinthians 12:4-10 .

title: I Peter 4:12
text: The fiery trial Imminent persecution because of their faith in Christ.

title: I Peter 4:17
text: For judgment to begin at the house of God. The sufferings of persecuted Christians were the beginning of judgment.

title: I Peter 5:2
text: Nor yet for filthy lucre.  This injunction implies that even in the earliest days it was the custom with some of the elders to demand, or at least to accept, money in payment for such services as they rendered to the other brethren.

title: I Peter 5:12
text: Silvanus. It is generally accepted that this was Silas, the companion of Paul in some of his journeyings, and his fellow-prisoner at Philippi ( Acts 16:25 ).

title: I Peter 5:13
text: Mark my son. The Mark here mentioned is believed to be the 'John whose surname was Mark' ( Acts 12:12 ), the writer of the second gospel narrative.

title: II Peter 1:1
text: To them that have obtained a like precious faith with us.  Those who, whether Jews or Gentiles, held a faith like that held by Peter.

title: II Peter 1:2
text: Knowledge of God. In the original the word here translated 'knowledge' (epignosis) has the deeper meaning of that understanding which is developed through love.  The same word occurs in  II Peter 1:3 .

title: II Peter 1:9
text: Blind, seeing only what is near. This phrase implies a lack of perception as to spiritual things and undue attention to the allurements of the world.

title: II Peter 1:10
text: Your calling and election sure. All Christians have been called, but they must work out their salvation.

title: II Peter 1:13
text: This tabernacle. The body.  See  John 1:14 II Corinthians 5:1 .

title: II Peter 1:17
text:
, 18
 
 The Majestic Glory, etc. Peter here refers to the transfiguration, of which he was an eye-witness ( Matthew 17:5 ).

title: II Peter 1:19
text: And we have the world of prophecy made more sure. All question as to the fulfilment of the prophecies as to the coming of the Messiah in the person of Jesus were removed for Peter by the wonders of which he had been an eye-witness (2Pe 1.16-18).

title: II Peter 2:4
text: Hell. This is the only place in the New Testament where the word 'hell' is given as a translation of the Greek word 'Tartarus,' which means the lowest depth.

title: II Peter 2:9
text:
And to keep the unrighteous under punishment. Implying that the unrighteousness are always under punishment from the time that sin is committed, both before the judgment and after.
 

 
 Day of judgment. At the second coming of Christ. See  Matthew 10:15 Matthew 11:22 Matthew 11:24 I John 4:17 . Even between death and the judgment there is apparently a division between the righteous and the wicked.  See notes on  Luke 16:19-21 Luke 22:31 .

title: II Peter 2:11
text: Railing judgment. The phrase refers to the scornful condemnation which comes only from the presumptuousness of unreason and ignorance.

title: II Peter 2:12
text: In their destroying surely be destroyed. In destroying, or attempting to destroy, the church by their false teachings they would  surely destroy themselves.

title: II Peter 2:13
text: Spots and blemishes. Referring to professing Christians who by their impure lives and their resulting bad behavior, at the love-feasts or other Christian means of grace, disgraced the name they bore.

title: II Peter 2:15
text: The way of Balaam. The perverse and disobedient way.  See  Numbers 22:7 Numbers 31:8 Revelation of John 2:14 .

title: II Peter 2:17
text: Blackness of darkness. This expression pictures the condition produced by the vanity  of the thoughts of man ( Psalms 94:11 ), as contrasted with the attitude of the meek to whom Jehovah will teach his way ( Psalms 25:9 ).

title: II Peter 2:19
text: Brought into bondage. Paul says in the same sense, 'His servants ye are whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness' ( Romans 6:16 ).

title: II Peter 2:20
text: The last state is become worse, etc. See  Matthew 12:43-45 .

title: II Peter 3:1
text: By putting you in remembrance. It is evident that even at this early period false teachings were so rife that Peter felt constrained to turn back the thought of the brethren to the purity of the original word.

title: II Peter 3:7
text: Stored up for fire. This verse taken with  II Peter 3:10 II Peter 3:12  foretell the dissolution of the earth and the heavens by the agency of heat.  See  Micah 1:4 .

title: II Peter 3:8
text: One day is with the Lord, etc.  Here Peter means to caution those for whom this epistle was written against fixing upon any particular time for the second coming of Christ.  The first part of  II Peter 3:10  implies the same caution.

title: II Peter 3:13
text: We look for new heavens and a new earth., This declaration doubtless refers to the prophecy of Isaiah -'For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth, and the former things shall not be remembered' ( Isaiah 65:17 ).

title: II Peter 3:17
text: The error of the wicked. As the exhortation is to stedfastness it appears that the 'wicked' referred to are the false teachers mentioned in the beginning of chapter 2.

title: II Peter 3:18
text: For ever. The glory of Christ is to be eternal.

title: I John 1:1
text:
That which. The truth and purpose of God concerning the Son, Jesus Christ, who 'became flesh and dwelt among us.'
 

 
 Was. Existed from all eternity.
 

 
 From the beginning. Not the beginning of time, but before time was.  See  Genesis 1:1 .
 

 
 That which we have heard, etc.  Referring to the companionship of John and the other apostles and disciples with Jesus on earth.
 

 
 The word of life. Jesus Christ.  See notes on  John 1:1 John 1:4 .

title: I John 1:2
text:
The life, the eternal life. The eternal, life-giving power of Jesus Christ.  See  John 1:4 John 11:25-27 , with notes thereon.
 

 
 With the father.  See  John 1:2 .

title: I John 1:3
text: Fellowship with us. Share with us the work, privilege and hope of Christian believers.

title: I John 1:4
text: That our joy may be made full. The purpose of the apostle John was so to influence the Christians addressed that they would make sure their fellowship with him and the other apostles, so that all might together share the joy of being followers of Christ.

title: I John 1:5
text:
Him. Christ.
 

 
 God is light. 'Light' here is the truth of God, spiritual truth, which infallibly detects and is unalterably opposed to all evil.  The apostle intended that his words should emphasize the difference between the light which God is and purely intellectual enlightenment so-called, and which may exist in one whose heart is corrupt.  His insight into the nature of God as revealed in Christ enabled him habitually to speak of God in especially illuminating terms borrowed from external nature and the fundamental facts of spiritual life.  According to him God is spirit ( John 4:24 ) and God is love ( I John 4:8 ).  He is careful to give the many points of view from which Christ is believed in as the source and sustainer of the Christian's faith and experience.  See note on  John 8:12 .

title: I John 1:6
text: Do not the truth. Do not make the truth, as revealed in Christ, the rule of action.

title: I John 1:7
text:
Fellowship. See note on  I John 1:5 .
 

 
 Cleanseth us from all sin. Is ever able to make us spiritually pure. To 'walk in the light' does not imply that one may not fall into sin; but saving power of faith in the voluntary sacrifice of Christ is necessary to enable the believer to walk in the light without sin.

title: I John 1:8
text: We deceive ourselves. Because of a perverted will or of lack of moral discernment in not seeing what sin really is.  The apostle was thinking of those who is his day were attempting to undermine Christian truth with the doctrine that sin has no power over those who are intellectually enlightened.  See note on  I John 1:5 .

title: I John 1:9
text: Confess. To God and also to one another.  See  James 5:16 .

title: I John 2:1
text:
My little children. A term of affection and fatherly oversight for all the disciples of the apostle.
 

 
 Advocate. The literal  meaning of the word is, 'one who is called to the side of another to advise and assist.' Here it means either Christ or the Holy Spirit.  'Advocate' is rendered 'Comforter' in  John 14:16 John 14:25 John 15:26 John 16:7 .

title: I John 2:2
text: Propitiation. That which wins favor.

title: I John 2:4
text: That saith, I know him, and keepeth not, etc.  The apostle here commends only that knowledge of God which prompts to filial obedience, thereby bearing witness to the love of God in the heart.  He cannot admit that an intellectual apprehension of truth about God is really knowledge of God; he refuses to consider it apart form a consecrated life.  He even brands as a liar the man who says that he knows God but does not by obedience prove his sincerity.

title: I John 2:5
text: Word. As 'word' - the revelation of the Father's will in Christ- is here a more comprehensive term than 'commandments,' so he who keeps the 'word' of God is holier, nearer the sinlessness of Jesus Christ, than he in whose obedience there is any element of fear.  Perfect obedience is only possible to him from whom perfect love has cast out fear ( I John 4:18 ).

title: I John 2:7
text: No new commandment. 'Commandment' in this verse refers to the words of Christ, 'A new commandment I give unto you, that ye love one another.'  See  John 13:34  and note thereon.

title: I John 2:8
text:
Again, a new commandment. The apostle employs the words 'old' and 'new' according to the light in which the commandment to love one another is considered.  It was old in one sense, because Christ had spoken it many years before this epistle was written; but it was new in its constant revelations of spiritual beauty and power.
 

 
 Which thing is true. The newness of the commandment.
 

 
 in him and you. New in Christ, because it was he in whom it was first incarnated, and by whom it was first sent forth  to the world by the authority of a perfect human example; new in 'you' - that is, the individual who at any time or place makes it the rule of life - because it makes all things new, brightens all personal relations with a  new light, rules all motives and intentions by a new sanction, the love of Christ in us prompting to the love of mankind.
 

 
 The darkness is passing away. The old order of things, whether under the imperfect light and the hard discipline of the Mosaic law; or the ignorance and misery in the Gentile world.
 

 
 The true light. The salvation offered in Christ.

title: I John 2:9
text: And hateth his brother. See note on  I John 2:4 .

title: I John 2:12
text:
:14
 
 I write unto you, etc.  In these verses the reasons for writing the epistle are given.
 

 
 My little children.  See note on 1Jo 2.1.
 

 
 Because your sins are forgiven you. Through which forgiveness they had been enabled to approach God with confidence.
 

 
 For his name's  sake. For the sake of the character and work of Jesus Christ. 'Name,' when applied to Jesus Christ in the New Testament, always stands for what he was, and what he did for mankind.
 

 
 Fathers. Experienced Christians.
 

 
 Him who is from the beginning.  Jesus Christ. See note on 1Jo 1.1.
 

 
 Because ye have overcome. Have been victorious over temptation.
 

 
 Because ye know the Father.  The 'little children' here spoken of as knowing the Father are distinguished from more experienced Christians who had a deeper knowledge of Jesus Christ, the Son. The 'little children' had begun their Christian experience by being told of the Father, and how He could be approached through faith in Christ; later they would know more fully about Christ and his work.

title: I John 2:15
text:
Love not the world. That is, those elements in the life of the world that hinder or quench the life of the Spirit (Jas 1.27).  The words do not refer to the world of mankind which God so loved that He gave His only begotten Son for it (Jon 3.16); nor to the world of nature as ordinarily understood.
 

 
 The things that are in the world. That are of the same nature as the evil elements already mentioned.

title: I John 2:16
text:
Lust. See Jas 1.14.
 

 
 Of the flesh. Immoderate and wrong sensual appetites of all kinds (1Pe 2.11).
 

 
 Lust of the eyes. Wrong desire for things that appeal most strongly to human wants through the power of physical sight, morbid curiosity to see unlawful and harmful sights, for the sinful pleasure of seeing.
