 The vainglory of life. Insolent pride in the enjoyment of one's position in life or in the display of one's wealth.

title: I John 2:18
text:
The last hour. The expected immediate second coming of Christ to judge the world.  See  James 5:3 James 5:7 I Peter 4:7 ; also note on  II Peter 3:8 .
 

 
 Antichrist cometh. 'Antichrist' is one who, pretending to be Christ, yet opposes Christ.  The appearance of antichrists was regarded as a sign of the second coming of Christ.

title: I John 2:19
text:
Went out from us. These antichrists had been brought up as Christians, or had been members of the Christian community.
 

 
 Were not of us. Had not been sincere Christians.

title: I John 2:20
text:
An anointing. Which made them true Christians, as contrasted with antichrists.
 

 
 The holy one. Christ.

title: I John 2:23
text: Hath not the Father. Because the sonship necessarily implies the Fatherhood and because only the Son can reveal the Father.  See  John 15:23 II John 1:9 ; also note on  Matthew 11:27 .

title: I John 2:24
text: That. The gospel.

title: I John 2:25
text:
He. Christ.
 

 
 Promised us. 'Whosoever believeth may in him have eternal life' ( John 3:15 ).

title: I John 2:27
text: Ye need not that any one teach you. Because of the anointing by which they had become true Christians, endowed with spiritual insight. 'Ye know all things' (1Jo 2.20).  The apostle John wrote, not to teach them what they already  knew, but to confirm them in what they already believed.

title: I John 2:28
text: If he shall be manifested. That is, if the time of his appearing should come.  This does not imply any doubt of Christ's coming, but refers only to the time.

title: I John 2:29
text: If ye know that he is righteous, etc.  They would surely know, since God is righteous, that every one also that doeth righteousness, is begotten of God.

title: I John 3:1
text:
The Father. These words include in their meaning not only 'My Father,' as rightfully spoken in a special sense by Jesus Christ alone, but 'our Father' of the Lord's Prayer.
 

 
 World. The evil in the world.  See note on 1Jo 2.15.  In this and the first six verses of the succeeding chapter the main theme is the righteousness of God.

title: I John 3:2
text: What we shall be. Children of God, however blessed their condition, are privileged to reach still greater spiritual heights.  This is also clearly indicated by Paul, whose use of the words 'sons of God' (Ro 8.14) implies a matured consciousness of the filial relation impossible to children under tutelage. 'Sons of God' rejoice in the liberty and glory conferred upon them.  There is no limit to their spiritual attainment except perfect conformity to the image of the Son of God ( Romans 8:29 ).

title: I John 3:3
text:
This hope. Of becoming like God by following the example of Christ.
 

 
 Set on him. Given to him or conferred on him. Man depends upon God even for the hope of becoming like Him.

title: I John 3:4
text: Sin is lawlessness. Because it prevents obedience to God.

title: I John 3:6
text:
Sinneth not. That is, not and cannot be an habitual, confirmed sinner.  If any man professing to abide in Christ commit sin, to that extent he does not abide in him.
 

 
 Hath not seen him, neither knoweth him. Because sin is out of all harmony with him.  See notes on  I John 2:1 .

title: I John 3:7
text: Even as he. Christ.

title: I John 3:8
text:
Doeth sin. That is, sins habitually.
 

 
 Works of the devil. The sins into which mankind has been tempted.

title: I John 3:9
text:
Begotten of God. Whosoever has been made and remains a child of god.
 

 
 His seed abideth in him. The spiritual life in him grows, and becomes more active and fruitful.

title: I John 3:10
text: That loveth not his brother. Love for mankind, whether Christian believers or not, is the practical test of love to God.

title: I John 3:12
text:
Cain. See  Hebrews 11:4 Jude 1:11 .
 

 
 Of the evil one. Inspired by the evil one.

title: I John 3:14
text: Out of death into life, because, etc.  Or, out of darkness into light ( Joshua 2:9-11 ).

title: I John 3:15
text: Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer. Because murder begins, is planned and is done through hatred.  See  Matthew 5:22  and note thereon.

title: I John 3:16
text: Brethren. All mankind, especially the children of God.

title: I John 3:17
text: Beholdeth. Looks on with indifference.

title: I John 3:19
text:
Hereby. That is, because we have loved in deed and in truth (1Jo 3.18).
 

 
 Assure our heart before him. Be comforted by trusting God for forgiveness.

title: I John 3:20
text: Greater than our heart. More merciful than we are when our consciences condemn us through imperfect knowledge. 'For he knoweth our frame; he remembereth that we are dust' ( Psalms 103:14 ).

title: I John 3:22
text:
Whatsoever we ask we receive. Prayer to God is answered at the moment of asking, according to faith, but not always in the manner asked or expected.  The answer may be known or seen in an instant, or it may be given through years of waiting, though in a way which makes clear the unwisdom of the first request and enhances the goodness of God.  See  Mark 11:24  and note thereon.
 

 
 Commandments. Obedience to God, which is not perfect so long as it contains any element of fear.  See note on  I John 2:5 .
 

 
 Pleasing in his sight. Things done from love to God, a better motive than obedience strictly so called.  But love, like obedience, is imperfect so long as any fear lurks within the heart.  'He that feareth is not made perfect in love' ( I John 4:8 ).  If we are willing to hear God and to obey his voice, He will hear and grant our petition.

title: I John 3:24
text: The Spirit which he gave us. After accepting the rule of Christ in the heart.  The approval of the Spirit witnesses that God in Christ abides within us.

title: I John 4:1
text:
Prove the spirits. By bringing them to the test of confessing that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh ( I John 4:2 ).  They who would not thus confess were antichrists ( I John 2:18  and notes thereon), false prophets ( I John 4:1 ), deceivers ( II John 1:7 ).
 

 
 Whether they are of God. Spirits and spiritual influences may be either good or bad.  Here 'spirits' may refer either to spiritual influences from evil men; or to the miraculous powers claimed by sorcerers, false prophets, etc.

title: I John 4:4
text: He that is in the world. The devil ( John 8:44 John 12:31 I John 3:10 ).

title: I John 4:5
text: They... them. The false teachers.

title: I John 4:7
text: Every one that loveth is begotten of God. 'Every one' here includes all the human beings in whose nature love is or ever has been, whether they ever heard of God and Christ or not; wherever human beings have loved, the love in them has come from God.

title: I John 4:8
text: God is love. These words are the apostle's main theme from  I John 4:7-5:13 .  See notes on  I John 1:5 .

title: I John 4:9
text: The world. The evil, alienated world.  See notes on  I John 2:15 .

title: I John 4:10
text:
But that he loved us. His love first came to us and made possible our love for Him.
 

 
 Propitiation. See note on  I John 2:3 .

title: I John 4:12
text: His love. Our love to God, resulting from his love in our hearts.

title: I John 4:13
text: Hath given us of his Spirit. As a witness.  See note on  I John 3:24 .

title: I John 4:15
text:
Confess. In all sincerity.
 

 
 That Jesus is the Son of God. Which the false teachers would not confess.  See notes on  I John 4:1 .

title: I John 4:17
text:
Herein. That is, by abiding in God.
 

 
 Love. Our love for God.
 

 
 Even so are we in this world. Thus being prepared for 'boldness in the day of judgment.'

title: I John 4:18
text: Fear hath punishment. Is associated with the notion of punishment, and is itself a foretaste of punishment.

title: I John 5:1
text:
The Christ. That is, Jesus of Nazareth, the divine Messiah.
 

 
 Him that begat. God.
 

 
 Him also that is begotten. Any person who accepts Christ.

title: I John 5:3
text: His commandments are not grievous. Because love to God helps the believer to obey, and by obedience he goes on from strength unto strength.  But even obedience prompted mainly by fear is far less grievous than the penalty of sin.  See  Matthew 11:28-30  and notes thereon.

title: I John 5:4
text: Whatsoever. The spiritual power that comes from God; it is not the person who overcomes, but God in Christ within the person.  Nevertheless the person may accept or reject the grace, and therefore the power, of God unto salvation.

title: I John 5:6
text:
This is he. That is, the Jesus of whom I speak is Jesus of Nazareth, the divine Messiah.
 

 
 Water and blood. Baptism and the crucifixion.
 

 
 Not with the water only. The apostle here condemns the false teaching according to which the Christ entered the human body of Jesus of Nazareth when he was baptized by John in the river Jordan, but left it before his death on the cross.
 

 
 But with the water and with the blood. Both baptism and crucifixion were needed in Christ's redemptive work.

title: I John 5:7
text:
It is the Spirit that beareth witness. In the hearts of true believers.
 

 
 Truth. See note on  John 15:26 .

title: I John 5:8
text:
Three who bear witness. That is, bear witness to the character and work of Christ.  The three witnesses are the Spirit ( I John 5:7 ); the water, or Christ's baptism in the Jordan; and the blood, or the crucifixion.
 

 
 The three agree in one. That is, in witnessing to and confirming the teaching of Christ.

title: I John 5:14
text:
, 15
 
 If we ask anything according to his will, etc.  Such prayer is inevitably answered.  See  I John 3:22  and note thereon.

title: I John 5:16
text: Unto death. Naturally resulting in death if the sinner does not turn from his downward course.  'Unto' means a tendency which may be successfully resisted; a sin unto death does not necessarily result in death.  The apostle means persistence in sin, the habit of sin- not any particular sin.  There is no room for any division of sinful acts unto 'mortal' and 'venial.' See  Hebrews 6:4 Hebrews 6:6 Hebrews 10:26-29 .

title: I John 5:18
text:
, 19
 
 The evil one. Satan.

title: I John 5:20
text:
An understanding. Knowledge and intelligence.
 

 
 Him that is true. God.
 

 
 We are in him that is true. Here 'him' means Jesus Christ.
 

 
 This is the true God. These words also refer to Jesus Christ, and distinctly affirm his deity.

title: I John 5:21
text: Idols. Idolatry, which still existed among the communities among whom the epistle was sent, and which might have tempted the weaker disciples.

title: II John 1:1
text:
The elder. The apostle John.
 

 
 Elect lady. It is not certain whether an individual or a church is meant.
 

 
 Children. Members of a church, if the latter meaning be taken.
 

 
 Truth. The Christian teaching and practice, according to John and the other apostles.

title: II John 1:3
text: Grace, mercy, peace. For a similar formula of salutation, see  I Peter 1:2 .

title: II John 1:7
text: Deceivers. See  I John 2:18-22 , and notes thereon.

title: II John 1:8
text: Look to yourselves, etc.  A warning to the disciples against false teachers who were endeavoring to undermine the Christian faith as taught by the apostles.

title: II John 1:9
text:
Onward. Away from the Christian truth revealed and taught.
 

 
 He that abideth. He who habitually does the will of God as revealed in Christ.

title: II John 1:10
text: Receive him not, etc.  Show no hospitality to him who would insidiously beguile you away from your faith in Christ.

title: II John 1:13
text: Elect sister. Either an individual or a church.  See  II John 1:1  and notes thereon.

title: III John 1:1
text:
The elder. See note on  II John 1:1 .
 

 
 Gaius. The same as Caius, a common Roman name.  It is not certain that the Caius here addressed was the same as the Gaius in  Acts 19:29 Acts 20:4 Romans 16:23 , or in  I Corinthians 1:14 .
 

 
 Truth. See note on  II John 1:1 .

title: III John 1:5
text: Them that are brethren and strangers. Gaius is here praised for his helpfulness to Christians who were strangers, and who were comforted by his hospitality.

title: III John 1:6
text: On their journey.  The Christians aided were travelling preachers.

title: III John 1:7
text: The Name. See notes on  I John 2:12-14 .

title: III John 1:9
text: Diotrephes. A Christian of some influence and authority in the church, but who opposed the apostle John.

title: III John 1:10
text: The brethren. The itinerant preachers.

title: III John 1:12
text: Demetrius. Not elsewhere mentioned.  He was not the Demetrius of  Acts 19:24 .

title: III John 1:14
text: Friends. The adherents of the apostle in his opposition to Diotrephes.

title: Jude 1:1
text:
Jude. It is generally agreed that the writer of this epistle was one of the four brothers of Jesus, named in  Matthew 13:55 .  The similarity of many passages to the second and third chapters of the Second Epistle of Peter have led to an endeavor to discover one authorship for both, but there is no dependable evidence to support this surmise.
 

 
 Them that are called. The elect.  See note,  I Peter 1:1 .  Compare  I Timothy 6:12 .

title: Jude 1:3
text: The faith which was once for all delivered. The gospel was delivered not in part but as a complete whole- 'once for all.'  The verses following warn against the perversions of the 'faith' by 'certain men':- doubtless the 'false teachers' spoken of in  I Peter 2:1 .

title: Jude 1:5
text: To put you in remembrance, though ye know all things. Through the 'anointing from the Holy One' ( I John 2:20 ) the faithful believer needed not that any one teach him ( I John 2:27 ).  Jude's reminder of this is also an admonition to be stedfast.

title: Jude 1:6
text: Angels that kept not their own principality. It is supposed that these were the 'sons of God' mentioned in  Genesis 6:2 .  Compare  Ephesians 6:12 .

title: Jude 1:8
text: Defile the flesh, and set at nought dominion. The great error which had come into the Christian church through false teachings seems to have been a perversion of the spiritual 'fervent love' enjoined toward the brethren ( I Peter 1:22 ) into lustfulness so gross as to be comparable to the sins of Sodom and Gomorrah, and to the fall of angels from their high estate.  In this condition of 'blackness of darkness' ( Jude 1:13 ) not only was the flesh defiled, but spiritual dominion was set at nought, and its dignities (glories) held in contempt.

title: Jude 1:9
text: But Michael the archangel when contending with the devil. Jude here seems to refer to a familiar tradition, but no other record of its now remains.

title: Jude 1:11
text: Korah. See  Numbers 16:1-50 .

title: Jude 1:14
text: Enoch, the seventh from Adam. The prophecy here cited is from the Apocryphal Book of Enoch in the words of an angel who thus interpreted a vision.

title: Jude 1:23
text: And on some have mercy with fear; hating even the garment spotted by the flesh. An injunction to the same caution in the mental sphere as would be exercised toward the very garments of one having a contagious disease.

title: Revelation of John 1:1
text:
Of Jesus. From Jesus, the real author.
 

 
 Must. In order to fulfill divine purpose as foretold in prophecy.
 

 
 Signified. Revealed in signs and symbols; as in  Revelation of John 5:1-10:11 .
 

 
 John. The apostle, son of Zebedee, author of the gospel and epistles.  See  Matthew 4:21 .

title: Revelation of John 1:2
text: Word of God. As received in this revelation.

title: Revelation of John 1:3
text: He that readeth. The public reader in the assembly of the saints.

title: Revelation of John 1:4
text:
Seven churches. Those named in  Revelation of John 1:11 .  These letters were addressed to these seven churches as having individually each its own problem, and also as representative of the varying conditions and problems of the whole church.  They typify the various local churches of Christendom in all ages, with their elements of strength and weakness; and there is in the message an element of progress, which seems to make them a sort of prophecy of the whose Christian age.
 

 
 Asia. The western part of what is now called Asia Minor; including Mysia, Lydia, Caria, and part of Phrygia.
 

 
 Seven Spirits. Commentators generally agree that the term signifies the Holy Spirit in His completeness.

title: Revelation of John 1:5
text:
The faithful witness. Jesus came to bear witness unto the truth.  See  John 18:37 .
 

 
 Firstborn of the dead. The writer points out Jesus as the first victor over sin and death, the firstfruits of those who shall live and reign with him in glory.
 

 
 Loveth. A continuing action.
 

 
 Loosed. A completed act, in the death on the cross, whereby Christ redeemed mankind in his sublime sacrifice.  See  Romans 6:10 Hebrews 7:27 .

title: Revelation of John 1:6
text: Priests. The kingdom is composed of those who offer spiritual sacrifices of prayer, praise, and service, to their Lord.  See  Exodus 19:6 I Peter 2:5 I Peter 2:9 .

title: Revelation of John 1:7
text:
With the clouds. The imagery of the Son of man riding upon the clouds at his second coming is frequent throughout the Scriptures.  See  Daniel 7:13 Matthew 24:30 Matthew 26:64 Acts 1:9-11 .
 

 
 They that pierced him. Not the Roman soldiers, but the Jews who crucified him.  See  Matthew 27:25 Acts 2:23 Acts 5:30 .  The verse quotes the prophecy of Zechariah.  See  Zechariah 12:10 .

title: Revelation of John 1:8
text: The Alpha and the Omega. The first and last letters of the Greek alphabet, expressing the beginning and the end.  He who speaks is the Eternal One.

title: Revelation of John 1:9
text:
The tribulation. As foretold by Jesus. See  Matthew 24:9 .
 

 
 Patmos. An island about 10 miles long and 6 miles wide, in the Aegean Sea, about 50 miles west of Miletus.
 

 
 For the word. John was probably banished to the isle of Patmos because of his faith in Jesus. It is possible, however, that he was bidden to go to the isle of Patmos in order to receive the revelation.

title: Revelation of John 1:10
text:
In the Spirit. In a state of prophetic illumination.  See  Revelation of John 4:2 Revelation of John 17:3 Revelation of John 21:10 .  Peter had a like experience ( Acts 10:10 ), and so did Paul ( II Corinthians 12:1 ).
 

 
 The Lord's day. This may mean the first day of the week.  See  Acts 20:7 I Corinthians 16:2 .  Or it may mean the final and great day of the Lord, to which he felt himself transported.  See  Joel 2:31 Malachi 4:5 .
 

 
 Trumpet. The sound of the trumpet was a signal of the divine presence.  See  Exodus 19:13 Exodus 19:16 Exodus 19:19 Joel 2:1 Matthew 24:31 .

title: Revelation of John 1:11
text: Seven churches. See notes on  Revelation of John 2:1 Revelation of John 2:8 Revelation of John 2:12 Revelation of John 2:18 Revelation of John 3:1 Revelation of John 3:7 Revelation of John 3:14 .

title: Revelation of John 1:12
text: Seven golden candlesticks. Representing the seven churches.  See  Revelation of John 1:20 ; also  Zechariah 4:2 Zechariah 4:10 .

title: Revelation of John 1:13
text:
A son of man. Having the figure of a man.  See  Revelation of John 14:14 Daniel 7:13 .
 

 
 Down to the foot. A garment indicative of priestly and regal dignity.

title: Revelation of John 1:14
text: White wool. This vision of John is similar in many details to the vision of Daniel.  See  Daniel 7:9 Daniel 10:6 .

title: Revelation of John 1:15
text:
Brass. Either bronze, an alloy of copper and tin, or electrum- gold combined with silver, steel and bronze; brilliant when polished.
 

 
 Voice of many waters. Ezekiel also makes a like comparison of the voice of the almighty.  See  Ezekiel 1:24 Ezekiel 43:2 .

title: Revelation of John 1:16
text: A sharp two-edged sword. Figurative language to express the convincing and convicting word of the Spirit.  See  Hebrews 4:12 Ephesians 6:17 II Thessalonians 2:8 .

title: Revelation of John 1:17
text:
As one dead. Overcome by fear in the presence of the divine majesty.
 

 
 Fear not. John had passed through a similar experience at the transfiguration, and with almost the same words Jesus restored his confidence.  See  Matthew 17:6 Matthew 17:7 .
 

 
 The first and the last. Eternal; from everlasting to everlasting.  See  Revelation of John 1:8 Psalms 90:2 Isaiah 41:4 .

title: Revelation of John 1:18
text:
The Living one. That is, living from all eternity, before time was, both before and after he came into the world to redeem it.
 

 
 Keys of death and of Hades. Symbols of his authority over death and the realm of the dead.

title: Revelation of John 1:20
text:
Mystery. Truth formerly hidden, but now to be revealed.
 

 
 Angels. Symbolic representations or types of the churches themselves; or possibly the responsible heads ('bishops') of the churches.

title: Revelation of John 2:1
text:
The church in Ephesus. The messages in this and the following chapter, while addressed to the individual historic churches, were doubtless intended to reach the whole church.
 

 
 Ephesus. The capital and chief commercial city of the Roman proconsular province of Asia.  Paul regarded this city as especially advantageous for the spread of the gospel.  He preached in the synagogue for three months, then taught and reasoned on gospel truth for two years in the school of Tyrannus. He was careful to send his beloved disciple Timothy to Ephesus, where a church membership composed of both Jews and Gentiles called for sound doctrine as well as the widest Christian sympathy.  See  Acts 19:8-10 .

title: Revelation of John 2:2
text:
Thy works, and thy toil and patience. In the trial with false prophets, and final withdrawal from them.
 

 
 Canst not bear. The false teachers were too heavy a burden to carry.

title: Revelation of John 2:4
text: Thy first love. The first ardent love with which they embraced the gospel.

title: Revelation of John 2:5
text:
The first works. Such works as had followed their first love.
 

 
 Move thy candlestick. Remove the church from the circle of the seven churches, as a candlestick no longer bearing a light.

title: Revelation of John 2:6
text: Nicolaitans. Probably a heretical sect which, claiming liberty under the gospel, committed various excesses.  See  Revelation of John 2:14 Revelation of John 2:15 ; also  Galatians 5:14 II Peter 2:13 II Peter 2:14 .

title: Revelation of John 2:7
text:
What the Spirit saith. Speaking through Christ to John.
 

 
 The tree of life. A symbolical reference to the tree of life in the garden of Eden.  See  Genesis 2:9 Genesis 3:22-24 .
 

 
 Paradise. This (Persian) word occurs in only two other places in the New Testament -  Luke 23:43 II Corinthians 12:4 .  Its meaning is a 'park' or pleasure-garden, and it is used to denote the place of rest for faithful souls after death.

title: Revelation of John 2:8
text:
Angel. See note  Revelation of John 1:20 .
 

 
 Smyrna. The only one of the seven cities still in existence.  It was a city of wealth, a seaport fifty miles north of Ephesus.  It was the home of the bishop Polycarp, and the place of his martyrdom, A.D. 155.
 

 
 The first and the last. Jesus Christ.  See  Revelation of John 1:8 .

title: Revelation of John 2:9
text:
Thou art rich. In spiritual things.
 

 
 Say they are Jews. Though Jews in name, they were not, in a true sense, the chosen people of God.  See  Romans 2:28 .

title: Revelation of John 2:10
text:
That ye may be tried. The persecutors of the Christians, in the endeavor to force them to deny Jesus, would put them to the test.
 

 
 Unto death. Even to the point of death.

title: Revelation of John 2:11
text: Second death. The final condemnation at the judgment.  See  Revelation of John 20:6 Revelation of John 20:14 Revelation of John 21:8 .

title: Revelation of John 2:12
text:
Pergamum. A city of great importance, 50 miles north of Smyrna, and about 15 miles inland from the coast.  It was a city of temples devoted to pagan worship.
 

 
 The sharp two-edged sword. A symbol of the word of God as expressed in the gospel.  See  Revelation of John 1:16 .

title: Revelation of John 2:13
text: Satan's throne. Probably a reference to the temple of Augustus near the top of the hill at Pergamum, where worship of the emperor was conducted.  It may refer, however, to the worship of Esculapius with its serpent symbol.

title: Revelation of John 2:14
text: Balaam. The story of Balaam and Balak is told in  Numbers 22:24 Numbers 31:8 .  To Balaam is attributed the plan of destroying the children of Israel through fornication and idolatry.  See  Numbers 25:1 Numbers 25:2 Numbers 25:5 Jude 1:11 .

title: Revelation of John 2:16
text: Repent. The admonition is to the whole church for tolerating idolaters and fornicators within its membership.

title: Revelation of John 2:17
text: Hidden manna. The reference is to the pot of manna stored in the tabernacle.  See  Exodus 16:34 Hebrews 9:4 . It is used here as a symbol of the spiritual 'bread of life' ( John 6:31-35 ).

title: Revelation of John 2:18
text: Thyatira. A place of considerable importance, with a large Greek population.  Among its industries the most famous was that of dyeing.  It was about 45 miles southeast of Pergamum, and 50 miles northeast of Smyrna.  Lydia, one of Paul's converts, was a purple seller from Thyatira.  See  Acts 16:14 Acts 16:15 .

title: Revelation of John 2:19
text: More than the first. As in  Revelation of John 2:2 .

title: Revelation of John 2:20
text: The woman Jezebel. This perhaps refers to some woman of influence within the church, who was leading the people to licentious and idolatrous living.  But more probably it is an impersonation of the powerful heathen influence which beset the church of Thyatira, as Jezebel, Ahab's queen, influenced the people of Israel.  See  I Kings 21:5-16 II Kings 9:30-37 .

title: Revelation of John 2:22
text: Adultery. In the Old Testament, idolatry was often called adultery, as an abandonment of God, the husband of His people.  See  Deuteronomy 31:16 Judges 2:17 I Chronicles 5:25 .

title: Revelation of John 2:24
text:
Have not this teaching. There were some who did not follow Jezebel.
 

 
 The deep things of Satan. Probably a sarcastic reference to the pretensions of the Gnostics, a sect which had mixed some elements of Christian teaching with wild and fantastic fancies from oriental religion.  The Gnostics claimed to know many mysteries of nature and of God.

title: Revelation of John 2:28
text:
The morning star. A symbol of the glory to be conferred upon those who become the children of God.  See  Job 38:7 II Corinthians 3:18 I John 3:2 .
 

 
 What the Spirit saith. In this revelation.

title: Revelation of John 3:1
text:
Sardis. About 35 miles south of Thyatira; formerly the capital of Lydia (the nation of Coresus), and notorious for its dissolute morals.
 

 
 Seven spirits of God. The sevenfold or complete Spirit, as in  Revelation of John 1:4 .
 

 
 Seven stars. The churches.
 

 
 Thy works. As the tree is known by its fruits, the works of the church at Sardis proved that it was dead.
 

 
 Be thou. Become.
 

 
 Establish the things that remain. This church must hold on to the little Christianity it still has.

title: Revelation of John 3:3
text: As a thief. Without warning.  See  Revelation of John 16:15 Matthew 24:43 I Thessalonians 5:2 I Thessalonians 5:4 II Peter 3:10 .

title: Revelation of John 3:4
text: A few names. Even in the church in Sardis, dead through luxury (idolatry of the things of the world) and sin, there were a few who were faithful to the truth they had received.

title: Revelation of John 3:5
text:
White garments. Emblematic of purity, victory, and worthiness to receive the reward.
 

 
 Book of life. A symbol to express the recording of the names of God's chosen.   See  Revelation of John 13:8 Revelation of John 20:12 Revelation of John 20:15 Revelation of John 21:27 ; also  Exodus 32:32 Exodus 32:33 Romans 8:29 Romans 8:30 I Peter 1:1 .
 

 
 Confess his name. Attest his discipleship. See  Matthew 10:32 Luke 12:8 .

title: Revelation of John 3:7
text:
Philadelphia. A rich and powerful city, 28 miles southeast of Sardis.  One of the letters of Ignatius (martyred about A.D. 118) was addressed to Philadelphia.
 

 
 Key of David. Emblematic of Christ's authority and power as a king, because he was the son of David.  See  Isaiah 22:22 Matthew 16:19 ; also  Matthew 1:1 Matthew 22:42 .

title: Revelation of John 3:8
text:
A door opened. For all, whether Jew or Gentile.  'Door' is a frequent figure of speech in the Bible text.  See  Acts 14:27 I Corinthians 16:9 II Corinthians 2:12 Colossians 4:3 .  In this connection it may mean a door to everlasting life, or into the church; or perhaps a wider field of missionary usefulness.
 

 
 None can shut. It is possible that the Jews in the church in Philadelphia objected to the admission of Gentiles.

title: Revelation of John 3:9
text:
Synagogue of Satan. A satirical reference to the assembly of the Jews at Philadelphia, who claimed to belong to the synagogue of the Lord, but were bitter persecutors of the Christians.
 

 
 Before thy feet.  In acknowledgment that the church at Philadelphia was a true representative of her King and Lord.  See  Isaiah 45:14 Isaiah 49:23 Isaiah 60:14 .

title: Revelation of John 3:10
text:
Word of my patience. The teachings of Jesus which encourage and enjoin loyal endurance.
 

 
 Keep thee from the hour of trial. This does not mean kept from tribulation, but delivered from disaster in the time of trial.
 

 
 The whole world. This is the first intimation of a widespread  persecution, which reaches its climax in  Revelation of John 3:13 .

title: Revelation of John 3:11
text: That no one take thy crown. The conqueror's reward is to him that endureth stedfastly unto the end.  See  Revelation of John 7:14 .

title: Revelation of John 3:12
text:
Pillar in the temple. He that overcometh shall have a prominent place in the church.  See  I Kings 7:15 I Kings 7:21 Galatians 2:9 . All Christians are living stones in the temple of God ( I Peter 2:5 Ephesians 2:20 ), but those who have endured the greater trials shall receive the more honorable place.
 

 
 Thence no more. Shall remain in the church as a pillar, both for this world and the next.
 

 
 The name of my God, etc.  This inscribing makes them citizens of heaven ( Philippians 3:20 ), who shall stand with God and the Lamb on Mount Zion forever.  See  Revelation of John 14:2 Revelation of John 22:4 .
 

 
 The new Jerusalem. The city of the elect.  See  Revelation of John 21:2 Galatians 4:26 .
 

 
 New name. A name in harmony with the glory of the life that is 'hid with Christ in God' ( Colossians 3:3 ).  See  Revelation of John 2:17 Revelation of John 19:12 Isaiah 56:5 Isaiah 62:2 Isaiah 65:15 .

title: Revelation of John 3:14
text:
Laodicea. One of the richest cities of Asia Minor, about 50 miles southeast of Philadelphia, and 100 miles east of Ephesus.  Colossae lay 18 miles to the southeast.  It is believed by some that Paul's letter to the Ephesians was in fact written to the Laodiceans.  See  Colossians 4:16 .
 

 
 Faithful and true witness. See note  Revelation of John 1:5 I Timothy 6:13 .
 

 
 The beginning of the creation of God. 'All things were made through him' ( John 1:3 ).  See  Colossians 1:15 Colossians 1:16 Hebrews 1:2 .

title: Revelation of John 3:15
text: Neither cold nor hot. Not actively opposing the gospel, nor ardently supporting it; a state of entire spiritual indifference.  See  Matthew 21:31 .

title: Revelation of John 3:16
text: Because thou art lukewarm. Alluding to the fact that lukewarm water nauseates.  This strong expression is intended to show that the self-satisfied and the proud offend the divine speaker.

title: Revelation of John 3:17
text: Have need of nothing. Riches tend to produce a fatal satisfaction with the things of this world.  See  Hosea 12:8 Luke 1:53 .

title: Revelation of John 3:18
text: Gold refined by fire. The true riches out of which all dross is burned, which shall be a treasure in heaven.  See  Matthew 6:19 Matthew 6:20 Luke 12:21 .

title: Revelation of John 3:20
text: I stand at the door. This is one of the most beautiful pictures in the whole Bible.  God so respects the individuality of each person that He will not force open the door of the heart of his own creature, but stands without, waiting patiently for each one to open the door and let him in.  See  Matthew 7:7 Matthew 13:15 John 14:23 .

title: Revelation of John 4:1
text:
After these things. Here begins a second vision or group of visions, that of God's presence in Heaven, the background of all that follows.  The main divisions in the Book of Revelation are marked by this phrase.  See  Revelation of John 7:9 Revelation of John 15:5 Revelation of John 18:1 Revelation of John 19:1 .
 

 
 Come up hither.   John was lifted up in Spirit, as was Ezekiel, to behold the visions of God.   See  Ezekiel 3:12 Ezekiel 8:3 Ezekiel 11:1 .

title: Revelation of John 4:2
text:
I was in the spirit. See  Revelation of John 1:10  and note thereon.
 

 
 Set in heaven. Already there, not placed there as a part of the vision.
 

 
 One sitting. The Eternal God.  See  Isaiah 6:1 Daniel 7:9 .

title: Revelation of John 4:3
text: Like a jasper stone, etc.  These comparisons are made to suggest the splendor of the great king.

title: Revelation of John 4:4
text: Elders. Like the elders in the synagogues and in the early assemblies of Christians, these 'older men' are in some way representative of the church.

title: Revelation of John 4:5
text:
Lightnings, etc. Expressive of the majesty of the Most High, creating terror in the hearts of men.  See  Exodus 19:16 Revelation of John 11:19 .
 

 
 Seven lamps. God's spirit.  See  Revelation of John 1:4  and notes thereon.

title: Revelation of John 4:6
text:
Crystal. Emblematic of great splendor.  See  I Kings 7:23 .
 

 
 Living creatures. See  Isaiah 6:1-4 Ezekiel 1:4-14 .  Symbolical, it would seem, of all created things.
 

 
 Full of eyes. Symbolizing the power of attention and vision.  See  Zechariah 4:10 .

title: Revelation of John 4:7
text: The first creature, etc.  In Ezekiel there are four composite figures, each having four faces.  Here there are four figures, each with a different aspect.  The lion is the noblest of wild beasts; the ox, the strongest of domesticated animals; and the eagle is the most wonderful of flying creatures; with them stands man, nobler and stronger and more wonderful than all.  The wings, as in Isaiah, show their readiness and power for service.

title: Revelation of John 4:8
text:
:11
 
These verses present a picture of worship and humiliation before the Lord God Almighty.  The song is that of the seraphim in  Isaiah 6:1-13 ; it has passed into the worship of the Christian church.

title: Revelation of John 4:11
text: Worthy art thou. The adoration is offered by the church and the whole creation, and is based here on the fact that God's will and His work are shown in that which He has made.

title: Revelation of John 5:1
text:
Book. This book is a symbol of the mystery of God; the volume of His plans and purposes and works.   See  Ezekiel 2:10 .
 

 
 Seven seals. Upon the opening of these seals is to follow the interpretation of the mystery which cannot be fully known till all are opened.  See  Isaiah 29:11 Ezekiel 2:9 .

title: Revelation of John 5:3
text: No one in the heaven, etc.  No one of created beings is worthy to open and read and declare the meaning of the revelation.

title: Revelation of John 5:5
text:
Lion... of Judah. Referring to messianic prophecy concerning Jesus.  See  Genesis 49:9 .
 

 
 Root of David. See  Isaiah 11:1 Isaiah 11:10 .

title: Revelation of John 5:6
text:
A Lamb. John looks, expecting to behold a conquering lion, but sees a lamb which shows by its wounds that it has been slain, but yet is alive.  It is a symbol of the crucified and risen Lord ( Revelation of John 1:18 ).  See  Isaiah 53:7 John 1:29 John 1:36 Acts 8:1 Acts 28:31 I Peter 1:19 .
 

 
 Seven horns. Symbols of power.  See  I Samuel 2:10 Psalms 112:9 Psalms 148:14 Daniel 7:7 Daniel 7:20 .
 

 
 Seven eyes. See note on  Revelation of John 4:6 .  It should be remembered throughout this book, that we have not a description of real things or even of pictures, but the record of visions, as in a dream, when nothing seems impossible or incongruous.

title: Revelation of John 5:7
text: Out of the right hand. The Father entrusts this revelation to the glorified Son, the sacrificed but living Lamb of God.

title: Revelation of John 5:8
text: Fell down before the Lamb. The church and creation, which have praised the Father as the Creator, now praise the Son as the Redeemer and Revealer.  See  Revelation of John 8:3  and notes thereon;  Psalms 141:2 .

title: Revelation of John 5:9
text:
Didst purchase unto God. Alluding to the redemptive blood on the cross.  See  Matthew 20:28 I Corinthians 6:20 I Corinthians 7:23 I Peter 1:18 I Peter 1:19 Revelation of John 14:3 Revelation of John 14:4 .
 

 
 Kingdom and priests. As in  Revelation of John 1:6 .

title: Revelation of John 5:11
text: A voice of many angels. The worship of Him who sits on the throne, and that offered to the Lamb ( Revelation of John 5:12 ), flow into one stream, indicating very strikingly the oneness of the Son and the Father.

title: Revelation of John 6:1
text:
One of the seven seals. Six seals are broken, in preparation for the opening of the book.  They give six pictures of the preliminary revelations, not all easy to interpret.
 

 
 Living creatures. See  Revelation of John 4:6-8 Mark 13:7 Mark 13:8 .
 

 
 Come. This command is given successively to each of the four horses.

title: Revelation of John 6:2
text: A white horse. Symbolic of conquest; the entry of Christ upon his victorious work and the promise of his success.

title: Revelation of John 6:4
text: A red horse. Symbolic of slaughter.  See  Matthew 24:3-8 Mark 13:7 Mark 13:8 .  Christ's coming brings a sword.

title: Revelation of John 6:5
text:
A black horse. Symbolic of mourning or of destitution.
 

 
 Had a balance. Indicating carefulness because of scarcity.  See  Leviticus 26:26 Ezekiel 4:16 .

title: Revelation of John 6:6
text:
A measure of wheat. Somewhat less than a quart, a small daily allowance for a workman, at the price of an average day's wages ( Matthew 20:9-13 ).  The language of the verse points to a time when it will not be possible to obtain more than the bare necessities of life - not a famine, but want or a scarcity of food.
 

 
 Hurt thou not. Be careful as to their use.

title: Revelation of John 6:8
text:
A pale horse. Symbolic of death.  See Eze 14.21, where the sore judgments of God are the sword, and the famine, and the evil beasts, and the pestilence as in this verse.  See  Matthew 24:6 Matthew 24:7 Luke 21:10 Luke 21:11 Luke 21:20 .
 

 
 Hades. The unseen world; the abode of the dead.  Thus temporal judgments move men to look for Christ's coming, and to prepare its way.

title: Revelation of John 6:9
text:
Underneath the altar. As slain victims, Martyrdom for Christ's sake is added as in  Matthew 24:9 .
 

 
 The testimony. See  Revelation of John 1:2 Revelation of John 1:9 .

title: Revelation of John 6:10
text:
How long. See  Zechariah 1:12 .
 

 
 Master. Expressive of God's supremacy.
 

 
 Avenge our blood. Vengeance belongs unto God ( Romans 12:19 ), and He will surely avenge those who call upon Him day and night (Lu 18.7, 8).

title: Revelation of John 6:11
text:
Who should be killed. The martyrs for the word and the testimony of Jesus are those who have overcome; and to them is given the promise ( Revelation of John 3:4 Revelation of John 3:5 ), and also the reward of a white robe of victory and purity.  See  Revelation of John 7:9 Revelation of John 7:13-17 .
 

 
 They should rest. Care should be taken here not to reason from this passage, that all shall sleep unconsciously in an intermediate world.  Sleep is the symbol of rest, but it belongs to life.  See  II Thessalonians 1:7 Hebrews 4:3 also Re 14.13; Da 12.13.
 

 
 Their fellow-servants. See  Revelation of John 11:3-13 .

title: Revelation of John 6:12
text:
A great earthquake. The breaking of the sixth seal brings signs of the approaching end as often described in prophecy.  See  Isaiah 29:6 Revelation of John 8:5 Revelation of John 11:13 Revelation of John 16:18 Matthew 24:7 .
 

 
 The sun became black. See  Isaiah 13:10 Isaiah 24:23 Ezekiel 32:7 Ezekiel 32:8 Joel 2:10 Joel 3:15 Amos 8:9 .  The black sun and the blood-colored moon describe the phenomenon of eclipses.

title: Revelation of John 6:13
text:
The stars of the heaven fell. See  Isaiah 13:10 Joel 2:10 Joel 3:15 .
 

 
 As a fig tree. See  Isaiah 34:4 Nahum 3:12 Matthew 24:32 .
 

 
 A great wind. See  Daniel 2:35 .

title: Revelation of John 6:14
text: Every mountain, etc. See  Isaiah 40:15 Jeremiah 4:24 Habakkuk 3:6 Nahum 1:5 .

title: Revelation of John 6:15
text: Hid themselves. Because of fear. See  Isaiah 2:10 .

title: Revelation of John 6:16
text:
Fall on us. See  Hosea 10:8 Luke 23:30 .
 

 
 From the face of him. See  Psalms 34:16 .
 

 
 Wrath. See  Nahum 1:6 Malachi 3:2 .

title: Revelation of John 7:1
text:
In the face of impending trouble, a fixed number are sealed that they may be delivered from it, and a great multitude come out of this tribulation.  The breaking of the seventh seal, and the revelation of judgment are suspended.
 

 
 Four corners. The four cardinal points, north, south, east, and west.

title: Revelation of John 7:3
text: Sealed the servants.  A seal put on the foreheads of the saints to preserve them through, not from, tribulations.  See  Exodus 12:7 Exodus 12:13 Ezekiel 9:4 Matthew 24:31 I Corinthians 1:22 .

title: Revelation of John 7:4
text: A hundred and forty and four thousand. Twelve times the number of the twelve tribes of Israel in thousands, an equal number from each tribe, seeming to mean those saved under a special covenant.  See  Revelation of John 14:1-3 Revelation of John 21:12 Revelation of John 21:16 Revelation of John 21:17 .

title: Revelation of John 7:9
text:
A great multitude. The Christian covenant is unlimited.
 

 
 And palms. Taken in connection with white robes, the palms are symbols of victory.

title: Revelation of John 7:14
text:
Great tribulation. The tribulation here spoken of is that foretold in  Matthew 24:21 , and may have had its first interpretation in the apostolic period, as in  John 16:33 , and again in  Acts 14:22 .  But in one aspect, the whole history of the church is a time of tribulation.
 

 
 Washed their robes. The startling figure, of robes washed white in blood, justifies itself in the redemption through Christ's death.

title: Revelation of John 7:15
text:
Before the throne. In a favored position because of their faithfulness.
 

 
 Serve him. Worship him.

title: Revelation of John 8:1
text: This verse concludes the record of the opening or breaking of the seals.  The book of revelation may now be opened.  But the seer did not look into it or hear it read.  The sight of the unsealed book leads to reverential silence, and for an appreciable time the vision stops.  Man cannot know yet all God's plans or the way of their fulfillment.

title: Revelation of John 8:2
text: This verse begins the third part of the book, which contains the vision of the trumpets, the proclamations of God which prepare the way of Christ and mark the progress of the church.

title: Revelation of John 8:3
text:
Another angel came. See  Revelation of John 7:2 Zechariah 3:1 .
 

 
 Over the altar. John has before him in his vision the temple of God in heaven patterned after the earthly temple and tabernacle of the Jews.  See  Exodus 25:40 Exodus 26:30 Exodus 30:1 Hebrews 8:5 .  The altar of incense was in front of the veil behind which was the ark of the covenant with the mercy-seat and cherubim.  See  Hebrews 9:2-5 Exodus 25:1-40 Exodus 26:1-37 .
 

 
 Golden censer. The fire-pan of  Exodus 27:3 I Kings 7:50 .
 

 
 Prayers of all the saints. The word 'saints' refers to Christians generally, all of whom are called to be saints ( Romans 1:7 ), not to a distinct class of Christians.  See  Revelation of John 5:8 Revelation of John 6:9 Revelation of John 6:10 ; also  Luke 18:7 Luke 18:8 .

title: Revelation of John 8:5
text: Upon the earth. The worship of heaven touches the earth, and there is a vision of divine glory, as at Sinai ( Exodus 19:16-21 ).

title: Revelation of John 8:7
text:
The first sounded. The trumpets tell of judgments proclaimed and show the world ripe for punishment; they bring calamity, first on the earth, then on the sea, next on streams and fountains, and then on the lights of heaven.  Everything is injured by sin, and nature itself cries out against man and thus appeal to God.
 

 
 Hail and fire. See  Exodus 9:24 Ezekiel 38:22 .

title: Revelation of John 8:8
text:
, 9
 
 Became blood. The reference here is to two of the plagues which afflicted the Egyptians.

title: Revelation of John 8:13
text: An eagle. A symbol of judgment.  See  Hosea 8:1 .

title: Revelation of John 9:1
text:
A star. A personification of an angel, supposed by some scholars to be a fallen angel.
 

 
 Pit of the abyss. The abode of evil spirits. See  Luke 8:31 .

title: Revelation of John 9:2
text: Smoke of a great furnace. See  Genesis 19:28 Exodus 19:18 .

title: Revelation of John 9:3
text: Came forth locusts. They produce great desolation.  See  Exodus 10:12-15 Joel 1:4 Joel 2:2-11 .

title: Revelation of John 9:4
text:
Neither any tree. A third part of the trees had been burned by the plague of the first trumpet.  See  Revelation of John 8:7 .
 

 
 As have not the seal. See  Revelation of John 7:3 Ezekiel 9:4-6 .  God's saints are kept safe.  The disciples had power over unclean spirits ( Mark 6:7 ), and those who received the gospel were turned from the power of Satan unto God ( Acts 26:18 ).

title: Revelation of John 9:5
text: Five months. The period from May to September, during which locusts might work destruction.  Locusts usually appear at intervals within this period, but in this vision they are continually present to torment.

title: Revelation of John 9:6
text: Shall seek death. The utter despair of the wicked because of the torments.  See  Job 3:22 .

title: Revelation of John 9:7
text:
Horses prepared for war. See  Joel 2:4 .
 

 
 Crowns like unto gold. Denoting victory.  These represent the spiritual hosts of wickedness, such as are called by Paul, 'principalities,' 'powers,' and 'world rulers of this darkness.'  See  Ephesians 6:12 Colossians 2:15 .

title: Revelation of John 9:11
text:
Abaddon is the Hebrew, and  Apollyon the Greek word for destroyer.  These evil spirits are ruled by a power of malignity and ruin.
 

 
 The sixth angel sounded. The sixth trumpet proclaims destructive war.
 

 
 Altar. See  Revelation of John 8:3 .

title: Revelation of John 9:14
text: River Euphrates. From the regions of this river had come the hosts of Assyria, and the Chaldeans, to war against Israel, and into those regions God's people had been carried captives.

title: Revelation of John 9:15
text: The third part of men. See  Revelation of John 8:7-12

title: Revelation of John 9:18
text: Fire and smoke and brimstone. A therefold picture of the terrors of war.

title: Revelation of John 10:1
text: Between the sixth and the seventh trumpet come the visions of the 'little book' and the 'two witnesses.' They relieve the pictures of deserved judgment by telling of revelations of truth and hopes of victory.

title: Revelation of John 10:2
text:
His right foot, etc.  Emblematic of power over land and sea.
 

 
 Little book open. Unsealed and also open; its contents may now be made known; the seer heard them announced as thunder; but he may not tell them yet.  Still, he does announce that God will not longer delay his word.

title: Revelation of John 10:7
text: Mystery of God. The revelation of the truth of the gospel.  See  Romans 16:25 Romans 16:26 Ephesians 1:9 Ephesians 3:3-9 Colossians 1:26 Colossians 1:27 .

title: Revelation of John 10:8
text: Take the book. The volume is now given to the chosen man, and he is to be sent to prophesy (proclaim) from it as it becomes a part of himself.

title: Revelation of John 10:9
text: Eat it up, etc.  The reception of the revelation would bring joy, but the sorrows predicted therein would bring grief to a sympathetic heart.

title: Revelation of John 11:1
text:
The sanctuary is measure for preservation; the courts of the temple remain desolate, two witnesses appear who are killed and return to life.
 
 A read like unto a rod./ See  Ezekiel 40:3 Zechariah 2:1 .
 

 
 Measure the temple of God.  This symbolizes, as often, the faithful church, made up of God's chosen ones, preserved in spit of persecution.

title: Revelation of John 11:2
text:
Court which is without. Corresponding to the Court of the Gentiles in the Jewish Temple.  See  Ezekiel 10:5 .
 

 
 The holy city.  Jerusalem.  See  Matthew 4:5 Matthew 27:53 .
 

 
 Forty and two months. Three years and a half, 1260 days, have a symbolic meaning, which we cannot now interpret.

title: Revelation of John 11:3
text:
My two witnesses. We cannot tell whether the words have a personal application; they certainly refer to the message of the church itself, the true witness to Christ.
 

 
 Clothed in sackcloth. Because they were to preach repentance and judgment.

title: Revelation of John 11:4
text: Two olive trees. Supplying the lamps in the temple.  See  Zechariah 4:3-14

title: Revelation of John 11:6
text:
To shut the heaven. To cause a drought, as did Elijah.  See  I Kings 17:1 .
 

 
 Over the waters, etc.  As did Moses and Aaron.  See  Exodus 7:17-21 .

title: Revelation of John 11:7
text:
Have power. God's word is ever mighty for judgment.
 

 
 The beast. The world-power opposing the church; as prophesied in  Daniel 7:1-28 .  This passage anticipates what is written in  Revelation of John 13:1 Revelation of John 13:2 Revelation of John 17:8 .
 

 
 Shall make war, etc.  Symbolic of the temporary triumph of the world-power of darkness over the church.  The passage doubtless has a direct reference to the persecutions of Christians by the Roman empire.

title: Revelation of John 11:8
text:
Lie in the street. This was a very great indignity in the eyes of the Jews.
 

 
 The great city. The last part of the verse shows that this was Jerusalem.
 

 
 Sodom and Egypt. Two names which are typical of great wickedness.  In the Scriptures, Jerusalem is sometimes spoken of as Sodom.  See  Jeremiah 23:14 Ezekiel 16:46-56 .

title: Revelation of John 11:10
text: Prophets tormented them. The true prophet always is a torment to those who have guilty consciences; as Elijah was to Ahab ( I Kings 17:1-21 ).  So also Peter, and Stephen.  See  Acts 5:33 Acts 7:54 .

title: Revelation of John 11:11
text: The breath of life. See  Ezekiel 37:1-14  also  Romans 6:5 .

title: Revelation of John 11:15
text:
:18
 
These verses constitute a song of triumph, for God has established his kingdom and has begun to execute his judgments.   Thus we are brought to see what the end shall be.

title: Revelation of John 12:1
text:
Series of visions.  Fourth division of the Book.  Clearer revelation of Christ and of his conflict with evil.
 

 
 A woman. Symbolizing the church, or the ideal Christian society.

title: Revelation of John 12:2
text: Travailing in birth. Referring to suffering which yet shall lead to life.

title: Revelation of John 12:3
text:
A great red dragon. Symbolizing the power of evil.  Red probably as symbolic of bloodshed.  See  Revelation of John 12:9 .
 

 
 Seven heads and ten horns. Symbolic of great power.
 

 
 Seven diadems. Symbolic of royal claims.

title: Revelation of John 12:4
text: His tail draweth, etc. The dragon's tail is his most destructive weapon.  Thus is pictured the great destroying power of the evil one.

title: Revelation of John 12:5
text:
A son, a man child. In Re 2.26, 27, we are told that he that overcometh shall rule with a rod of iron.  This 'son' is the Messiah as coming for the church which makes ready for him.  But it is not amiss to consider the 'son' also as in general the seed of the church, the company of saints.
 

 
 Her child was caught up. This does not accurately describe the ascension of Jesus, but it may symbolize it, as showing his continued life and that of his people.  The fact that the child was seen as 'caught up' into heaven, shows that these events occur on this earth, and not in heaven.

title: Revelation of John 12:6
text: The woman fled. Describing first the scattering of the church from Jerusalem, because of persecution.  See Mt 24.9.  In a large view the vision pictures a general scattering of those who suffer for the faith.

title: Revelation of John 12:7
text:
War in heaven. This shows a conflict in the spiritual world, such as is ever 'wrestling against the principalities, powers,' etc., mentioned in  Ephesians 6:12 .
 

 
 Michael and his angels. Representing the powers of light.  According to Jewish conception, Michael was the angel who guarded particularly the interests of the Jews.  See  Daniel 10:21 Daniel 12:1 .

title: Revelation of John 12:8
text: Neither was their place, etc.  This means that Christ and his church have already broken the power of Satan.  See  Isaiah 14:12-15 .

title: Revelation of John 12:9
text:
The old serpent. See  Genesis 3:1-4 .
 

 
 He was cast down, etc. His struggle now is with the church on earth.  A parallel passage occurs in  Luke 10:18 .

title: Revelation of John 12:10
text: Saying, Now is come, etc. The song of victory is because of the final triumph of the church and the gospel over the powers of evil.

title: Revelation of John 12:11
text:
They overcame. See  Revelation of John 3:21 .
 

 
 Because of the blood. By the strength of the blood of their Lord, and for the sake of their testimony, their faith held the Christians through persecution.

title: Revelation of John 12:12
text:
Rejoice, O heavens. See  Psalms 96:11 Isaiah 49:13 .
 

 
 Woe for the earth, etc.  The bitter struggle is still to go on in the world of men.

title: Revelation of John 12:14
text: Wings of the great eagle. See  Exodus 19:4 .

title: Revelation of John 12:15
text: Water as a river. The church finds refuge, though a flood - betokening a great host of adversaries - would destroy her.  The host finds its ruin in the earth, which seemed its strength; but the dragon persists in his assaults.  We may read here the beginning of hope, to sustain us in these visions which follow.

title: Revelation of John 12:17
text: The rest of her seed. See  Revelation of John 12:5 , and note thereon.

title: Revelation of John 13:1
text: A beast. A great world-power, hostile to the church, as the nondescript beast in  Daniel 7:7 .  It appeared to the early church as the Roman empire, the persecuting power of the world.

title: Revelation of John 13:2
text: Leopard, etc.  The beast is a composite of all the world-powers.  See  Daniel 7:4-8 .

title: Revelation of John 13:3
text: One of his heads, etc.  This may refer to some event in the life of Nero.  At any rate, it intimates that the power of evil would seem to prevail in spite of some victories of truth; and that successful evil would be held in admiration by mankind.  Men would worship Satan, because Satan maintained the power of the world.

title: Revelation of John 13:4
text: Authority unto the beast. Satan gave his power to the world, as it was the enemy of the church.

title: Revelation of John 13:5
text:
A mouth speaking, etc.  See  Daniel 7:8 Daniel 7:20 Daniel 7:25 Daniel 11:36 .
 

 
 Forty and two months. See  Revelation of John 11:2 Revelation of John 12:6 Daniel 7:25 .

title: Revelation of John 13:6
text: Tabernacle, even them, etc.  The tabernacle, even more than the Temple, is a type of heaven.

title: Revelation of John 13:7
text: The saints. The same as 'the rest of her seed' in  Revelation of John 12:17 .  See also note on  Revelation of John 12:5 .

title: Revelation of John 13:8
text: The book of life. See  Revelation of John 3:5 , and note thereon.

title: Revelation of John 13:10
text:
If any man is for captivity, etc.  See  Genesis 9:6 Jeremiah 15:2 Jeremiah 43:11 Matthew 26:52 .
 

 
 Here is the patience. That is, here is the reason why the saints should be 'patient' (stedfast) in tribulation.

title: Revelation of John 13:11
text: Another beast. The earthborn beast is less repulsive than the beast which rose up from the sea.  It would seem to be a partially Christianized, but really pagan power, deceiving man.

title: Revelation of John 13:14
text:
He deceiveth them, etc.  See  Revelation of John 2:20 II Thessalonians 2:11 .
 

 
 Make an image.  Very probably a reference to the image of the emperor of Rome, but it means any worship of evil principles, even under the guise of right.

title: Revelation of John 13:18
text: Six hundred and sixty and six. It seems presumptuous to attempt to explain the number 666.  Probably it is a cipher, the key to which has been lost.  There may have been many things in this book, which were made clear to early readers by oral interpretations now lost.

title: Revelation of John 14:1
text:
The two chapters immediately preceding present dark pictures of the temporary triumph of the powers of evil.  This chapter portrays the victory and glory that await those who overcome, the 'sealed' of  Revelation of John 7:1-17 , and tells of righteous judgment.
 

 
 The Lamb. As always, Christ.
 

 
 The Mount Zion. The heavenly Zion.  See  Psalms 2:6 Hebrews 12:22 .
 

 
 Written on their foreheads. See  Revelation of John 7:3 Revelation of John 22:4 ; also  Revelation of John 14:9 Revelation of John 13:16 Revelation of John 20:4 .

title: Revelation of John 14:4
text:
Not defiled. This tells of spiritual purity of life and character.
 

 
 Firstfruits unto God. The Christians of the apostolic age and those who follow their example, the whole body of those saved in the church.

title: Revelation of John 14:6
text: Eternal good tidings. The gospel, now to be fully proclaimed.  See  Revelation of John 10:7 I Peter 1:25 .

title: Revelation of John 14:7
text:
Fear God. See  Revelation of John 15:4 Jeremiah 10:7 Acts 5:11 .
 

 
 The hour of his judgment. See  Acts 10:42 Acts 17:31 Acts 24:25 .

title: Revelation of John 14:8
text:
Babylon. The great world power of old, and the great enemy of Israel, stands for the world-power of the later days and the great enemy of the church.  Babylon cannot represent apostasy within the church.
 

 
 Drink of the wine, etc.  See  Jeremiah 51:7 .

title: Revelation of John 14:12
text: Patience of the saints. See  Revelation of John 13:10 , and note thereon.

title: Revelation of John 14:13
text: Blessed. They who die now are blessed, for they die that they may rest and are delivered form evil to come.

title: Revelation of John 14:14
text:
A white cloud. See  Daniel 7:13 Matthew 24:30 Mark 14:62 .
 

 
 A sharp sickle. This verse with the two following, present a harvest scene; and Re 14.17-20, a vintage scene; and these two scenes correspond to the parable of the wheat and the tares ( Matthew 13:24-30 Matthew 13:37-43 ).

title: Revelation of John 14:20
text: Trodden without the city. Identical with Sodom and Egypt in  Revelation of John 11:8 .  See also  Luke 21:20-24 .  It is a frightful picture, that the winepress runs with blood, a very deep and very wide stream.  God's judgment is severe and prolonged.

title: Revelation of John 15:1
text:
The fifth series of visions, after the record of a victor-song, tells of the seven bowls of wrath upon the wicked.
 
 Another sign. See  Revelation of John 12:1 .  See  Revelation of John 8:1 Revelation of John 8:2 .
 

 
 The last. See  Revelation of John 16:17-21 Revelation of John 17:1 Revelation of John 21:9 .

title: Revelation of John 15:3
text: The song of Moses. That is, a song like that of Moses.  See  Exodus 15:1-18 .  God is blessed, as bringing deliverance through his righteous judgments.

title: Revelation of John 15:5
text:
Temple. See  Revelation of John 11:19 , and note thereon.
 

 
 Tabernacle of the testimony. So-called because it contained all that was symbolized in the tabernacle of Israel ( Exodus 25:40 ).  See  Acts 7:44 .

title: Revelation of John 15:7
text: Seven golden bowls. These seven bowls correspond to the seven trumpets.  The first bowl affects the earth; the second, the sea; the third, the rivers and fountains; the fourth, the sun; the fifth, the throne of the beast; the sixth, the river Euphrates; the seventh, the air.

title: Revelation of John 16:2
text: Noisome and grievous sore. Like the plague of boils upon the Egyptians.  See  Exodus 9:8-10 .

title: Revelation of John 16:3
text: Blood as of a dead man. See  Revelation of John 8:8 Revelation of John 8:9 Exodus 7:19-21 .

title: Revelation of John 16:4
text: Rivers and the fountains. See  Revelation of John 8:10 Revelation of John 8:11 .

title: Revelation of John 16:5
text: Righteous art thou. See  Psalms 19:9 John 17:25 .

title: Revelation of John 16:6
text:
Given them to drink. See Mt 23.34-37.
 

 
 They are worthy. That is, of judgment and punishment.

title: Revelation of John 16:10
text: Throne of the beast. Satan and his angels are here tormented, as well as his subjects.

title: Revelation of John 16:12
text: The river Euphrates. See  Revelation of John 9:13-19 Genesis 15:18 .

title: Revelation of John 16:13
text:
, 14
 
 As it were frogs. See  Exodus 8:5 Exodus 8:6 .

title: Revelation of John 16:16
text: Har-Magedon. That is Mount Magedon, a reference to Megiddon of the Old Testament, especially to the battle in which good King Josiah fell and lasting sorrow came to Israel.  See  Judges 5:19 II Kings 23:29 II Kings 23:30 II Chronicles 35:22 .

title: Revelation of John 16:17
text: It is done. The declaration of finality, as in our Lord's 'It is finished.'

title: Revelation of John 16:19
text:
Babylon the great. The world power, the city of the world as opposed to the city of God; doubtless represented to the early Christians by the city of Rome.  See  Revelation of John 14:8 .
 

 
 Cup of the wine. See  Revelation of John 14:10 .

title: Revelation of John 16:21
text:
Great hail. See  Revelation of John 11:19 ; also  Exodus 9:18-26 .
 

 
 Weight of a talent. A Jewish 'talent' weighed more than 100 pounds.

title: Revelation of John 17:1
text:
The sixth division of the book gives the vision of the harlot riding on the beast, and of the fall of Babylon.
 

 
 The great harlot. The harlot represents the faithless church, in her submission to the world.  In the prophetical sense, a harlot is one who has broken her marriage vows; Jerusalem and Judah thus broke their covenant vows with God.  See  Matthew 23:13-39 .  Tyre and Nineveh were both called harlots in the Old Testament.  See  Isaiah 23:17 Nahum 1:1 Nahum 3:4 .
 

 
 Upon many waters.  Unstable and faithless.  See  Jeremiah 51:13 .

title: Revelation of John 17:2
text: Drunken with the wine.  Jeremiah 51:7 .

title: Revelation of John 17:3
text:
In the spirit. See  Revelation of John 1:10 , and note thereon.
 

 
 A scarlet-colored beast. This beast was, as before, the Roman empire, representing the world with its pomp and luxury.

title: Revelation of John 17:4
text: In purple and scarlet. The attire of a harlot, indicating luxury and pride.  Contrast this picture with the woman of  Revelation of John 12:1-17 , the church in her first glory.

title: Revelation of John 17:6
text: Drunken with the blood. Referring to the madness of persecutions.  See  Matthew 23:29-39 Luke 13:33-35 .

title: Revelation of John 17:8
text:
Was, and is not. This probably refers to the power of Satan himself as manifested in the world-power.  He is the power of darkness ( Luke 22:53 ).  He was in heaven ( Revelation of John 12:3 ); is cast out and disappears for a time ( Revelation of John 12:17 ) appears again the beast coming up out of the sea ( Revelation of John 13:1 Revelation of John 13:2 ), and in the beast coming up out of the land ( Revelation of John 13:11-15 ).
 

 
 Out of the abyss. See  Revelation of John 9:1-11 .
 

 
 Go into perdition. See  Daniel 7:11 ; also  Revelation of John 19:20 Revelation of John 20:10 .
 

 
 That dwell on the earth. The ungodly shall admire and worship the pomp and pride of evil which panders to their own sin.  Thus it has always been, and is today.  But they whose names are written in the book of life will have their affection fixed on their Lord, and will not be deceived.
 

 
 Book of life. See  Revelation of John 13:8 , and note thereon.

title: Revelation of John 17:9
text:
The mind that hath wisdom. A caution that he is speaking enigmatically, and that only the saints will be able to understand.  This was probably on account of the persecutions of the church by the Jews and the Roman empire.  See  Revelation of John 13:18 .
 

 
 Seven mountains. This passage must have some reference to Rome, which was built upon seven hills.  But it typifies all seats of evil power and political influence.  In this sense, the number (seven) of the mountains symbolizes universal power.

title: Revelation of John 17:10
text: Seven kings. Probably referring to seven of the Caesars; but the exact reference cannot be now determined.

title: Revelation of John 17:12
text: The ten horns. Perhaps some allied powers which aided imperial Rome in warning on Christianity.

title: Revelation of John 17:14
text: These shall war, etc.  The forces of evil, arrayed against Jesus and his kingdom, shall finally turn on the church, as she has become apostate, and shall bring her to ruin.

title: Revelation of John 17:18
text: The great city. There can hardly fail to be some reference here to Rome as the capital of the world.

title: Revelation of John 18:2
text: Fallen, fallen, etc.  The fall and ruin of the world-power, which has opposed the kingdom of God.  See  Isaiah 21:9 Jeremiah 51:8 ; also  Revelation of John 14:8 .

title: Revelation of John 18:3
text: The wine of the wrath. See  Revelation of John 14:8 .

title: Revelation of John 18:4
text: Come forth, my people. See  Jeremiah 51:45 Matthew 24:16 .

title: Revelation of John 18:5
text: Reached unto heaven. See  Jeremiah 51:9 .

title: Revelation of John 18:7
text: She saith in her heart. See  Isaiah 47:5 Isaiah 47:7 Isaiah 47:8 .

title: Revelation of John 18:9
text:
:20
 
For a parallel picture see  Ezekiel 26:1-21 Ezekiel 27:1-36 .

title: Revelation of John 18:20
text: Rejoice over her, thou heaven. See  Jeremiah 51:48 .

title: Revelation of John 18:21
text: With a mighty fall. See  Jeremiah 51:63 Jeremiah 51:64 .

title: Revelation of John 18:22
text: The voice of harpers, etc.  See  Jeremiah 25:10 Ezekiel 26:13 .

title: Revelation of John 18:24
text: Blood of prophets. See  Matthew 23:34 Matthew 23:35 Luke 11:49-51 Luke 13:33 Luke 13:34 .

title: Revelation of John 19:1
text: After the prophetical dirge over the fall of Babylon, the great city, the tragedy of the Book of revelation, chapter 19 begins with a song of triumph of the redeemed, victors over the powers of darkness, the church which has thrown off the power of apostasy.  See  Revelation of John 12:10 Revelation of John 12:12 .

title: Revelation of John 19:7
text:
Marriage of the Lamb. This refers to the union of Christ and his church; an action in one sense going on throughout the passing years so long as believers are united to him.  The same great spiritual fact is portrayed in the Master's parables.  See  Matthew 22:2-13 Luke 14:15-24 .
 

 
 His wife. The bride is the New Jerusalem - the church.  See  Ephesians 5:23-25 .

title: Revelation of John 19:10
text:
Thy fellow-servant. See  Revelation of John 22:8-11 .
 

 
 The testimony of Jesus. The word of God, especially the New Testament.

title: Revelation of John 19:11
text:
The seventh section of the revelation begins here with the clear presentation of the milennial age - the Messianic triumph.  See  I Corinthians 15:25 .
 

 
 He that sat thereon. The Christ, on the white horse, as at the beginning.  See  Revelation of John 1:5 Revelation of John 3:7 Revelation of John 3:14 .

title: Revelation of John 19:13
text:
Garment sprinkled with blood. See  Isaiah 63:1-6 .
 

 
 The word of God. See  John 1:1-18 .

title: Revelation of John 19:14
text: Armies. The angelic host.  See  Revelation of John 17:14 .

title: Revelation of John 19:17
text: Come and be gathered. See  Ezekiel 39:17-20 .

title: Revelation of John 19:19
text:
The beast. See  Revelation of John 13:1-7 .
 

 
 Kings of the earth. As elsewhere, the beast and the kings of the earth represent the world-power which is hostile to the Lamb.

title: Revelation of John 19:20
text:
False prophet. The beast which came up out of the earth ( Revelation of John 13:11 ).  See  Revelation of John 16:13 .
 

 
 They two were cast alive. See  Daniel 7:11 .
 

 
 Lake of fire. See  Revelation of John 20:10 Revelation of John 20:14 Revelation of John 20:15 Revelation of John 21:8 .  The same as the Gehenna of fire in  Matthew 5:22 Matthew 10:28 Mark 9:43-45 , a place of utter destruction.

title: Revelation of John 20:1
text:
The harlot, the beast, and the false prophet have been vanquished, but Christ must triumph over Satan before his victory is complete.
 

 
 Key of the abyss. See  Revelation of John 9:1 
 

 
 A great chain. See  II Peter 2:4 Jude 1:6 .

title: Revelation of John 20:2
text:
The dragon. See  Revelation of John 12:3-9 , and notes thereon.
 

 
 A thousand years. The number, as others in this book, is symbolic (see  II Peter 3:8 ).  It marks the period of the millennium, beginning with the first limiting of the power of the evil one by the incarnate Christ (see  Luke 11:18 ), and continues until Christ shall have put all enemies under his feet.

title: Revelation of John 20:4
text:
That had been beheaded. Thus the Book of Revelation strengthened the faith of those who were suffering persecutions, by giving them a vision of the final triumph of Christ and the blessedness of his followers.  See  Revelation of John 6:9-11 Revelation of John 11:11 Revelation of John 11:12 Revelation of John 12:5 Revelation of John 12:11 .
 

 
 Received not the mark, etc.  Had not devoted themselves to the services of Satan and the world.
 

 
 Reigned with Christ. Those who are truly Christians are called kings and priests, and share in Christ's power and glory.  See  II Timothy 2:11 II Timothy 2:12 .

title: Revelation of John 20:6
text: Second death. See  Revelation of John 20:14 Revelation of John 21:8 Matthew 10:28 .

title: Revelation of John 20:7
text: Satan shall be loosed. Christ's reign in his church is to be followed by a final outburst of Satan's power.

title: Revelation of John 20:10
text: Cast into the lake of fire. The final overthrow of Satan.  See  Revelation of John 14:10 Revelation of John 14:11 .

title: Revelation of John 20:11
text: A great white throne. The throne of judgment.  See  Isaiah 6:1 Daniel 7:9 .

title: Revelation of John 20:12
text:
The dead. That is, 'the rest of the dead' mentioned in  Revelation of John 20:5 ; it seems to mean those who had not their names in the book of life.
 

 
 Books were opened. See  Daniel 7:10 .
 

 
 Book of life. See  Exodus 32:32 Psalms 56:8 Psalms 69:28 Daniel 12:1 Luke 10:20 Philippians 4:3 .
 

 
 According to their works. See  Romans 2:6 II Corinthians 5:10 .

title: Revelation of John 20:14
text: Death and Hades. Hades signifies simply the unseen world, the 'abode of the dead.' Death shall be no more, and none shall be left in the abode of the dead, for they whose names are not written in the book of life, shall be cast into the lake of fire.  See  I Corinthians 15:26 .

title: Revelation of John 21:1
text: A new heaven. See  Isaiah 65:17 Isaiah 65:18 .

title: Revelation of John 21:2
text:
New Jerusalem. The old Jerusalem became one with Babylon the great, the harlot; but the new Jerusalem is the city which Paul calls the 'Jerusalem that is above' ( Galatians 4:26 ).  See also  Hebrews 12:22 .
 

 
 Bride. The church of Christ. See  Ephesians 5:25-32 ; also  Revelation of John 19:7-9 , and note thereon.

title: Revelation of John 21:3
text: Tabernacle of God. In this tabernacle, the believer enters boldly into the holy place, by the blood of Jesus.  See  Hebrews 10:22 .

title: Revelation of John 21:4
text: Wipe away every tear.  See  Revelation of John 7:17 .

title: Revelation of John 21:5
text: He that sitteth on the throne. See  Revelation of John 19:11-16 Revelation of John 20:11 Revelation of John 22:1 .

title: Revelation of John 21:6
text: The Alpha and the Omega. See  Revelation of John 1:8 , and note thereon.

title: Revelation of John 21:7
text: Overcometh. There are fourteen promises in the Book of Revelation, to those who overcome.

title: Revelation of John 21:8
text:
The fearful. Those who have not faith enough to endure persecution.
 

 
 The lake that burneth. See  Revelation of John 19:20 , and note thereon.

title: Revelation of John 21:9
text:
The seven angels. The eighth and last vision of the revelation begins with  Revelation of John 21:9 .  See  Revelation of John 17:1 .
 

 
 The bride. See  Ephesians 5:23-32 , and above.

title: Revelation of John 21:10
text:
In the Spirit. See  Revelation of John 1:10 .
 

 
 To a mountain. See  Ezekiel 40:2 .
 

 
 The holy city Jerusalem. All that follows is in striking contrast to the great city, the mother of harlots ( Revelation of John 17:5 ).

title: Revelation of John 21:12
text: For a parallel passage, see  Ezekiel 48:30-34 .

title: Revelation of John 21:17
text: Measure of a man. That is, the measure used by the angel was the same as would be used by a man.

title: Revelation of John 21:25
text: Shall in no wise be shut. Gates are for protection from enemies.  The perpetually open gates symbolize perfect safety.  See  Isaiah 60:11 .

title: Revelation of John 21:27
text:
Maketh an abomination. Probably means the practice of idolatry.  See  Revelation of John 17:4 Revelation of John 21:8 .
 

 
 The Lamb's book of life. See  Revelation of John 3:5 , and note thereon.

title: Revelation of John 22:1
text: A river of water of life. See  Ezekiel 47:1 Zechariah 14:8 John 4:10 John 4:14 .  See also the description of a river in the garden of Eden ( Genesis 2:10 ).

title: Revelation of John 22:2
text: The tree of life. See  Revelation of John 2:7 Genesis 2:9 .

title: Revelation of John 22:3
text: No curse any more. The punishment for sin - banishment from the tree of life ( Genesis 3:16-19 Genesis 3:23 ) - shall be removed.  All shall have access to that tree of life in the precincts of the heavenly city.  See  Matthew 19:29 Acts 3:25 .

title: Revelation of John 22:6
text: God of the spirits, etc.  He who inspired the spirits of the prophets.  The verses  Revelation of John 22:6-21  form a conclusion to the whole book.

title: Revelation of John 22:7
text: I come quickly. See  Matthew 24:34-42 .

title: Revelation of John 22:11
text: He that is unrighteous. Even at the last a word of warning.  See  Isaiah 6:10 Ezekiel 3:27 Ezekiel 20:39 Daniel 12:10 Matthew 26:45 .

title: Revelation of John 22:14
text:
Right to come. See note on  Revelation of John 22:3 .
 

 
 May enter in. The gates are ever open to those whose names are written in the Lamb's book of life.

title: Revelation of John 22:15
text: Dogs. The impure; lascivious persons.

title: Revelation of John 22:16
text:
The root and the offspring of David. See  Isaiah 11:1 Isaiah 11:10 Matthew 1:1 Matthew 22:42 .
 

 
 The morning star. See  Revelation of John 2:28 , and note thereon.

title: Revelation of John 22:17
text:
This verse is called 'the great invitation'; because of its great offer, its mercy, and its universality.
 

 
 He that is athirst.  See  Revelation of John 21:6 Isaiah 55:1 John 7:37 .

title: Revelation of John 22:19
text:
This book. The Book of the Revelation of Jesus Christ.  See  Revelation of John 22:7 Revelation of John 22:9 Revelation of John 1:3-11 .
 

 
 Take away his part. He shall be denied access to the tree of life.  See  Revelation of John 22:2 .
 

 
 The holy city. The heavenly city, inhabited by those who have overcome.

title: Revelation of John 22:20
text: He who testifieth. Jesus Christ.  See  Revelation of John 1:2 .  Thus the book ends with the Lord's promise of his return, the church's prayer that it may quickly come, and ( Revelation of John 22:21 ) a benediction of grace.
